News.title: Bob Dylan meets with Pope Leo at Vatican – as fans left stumped by music icon’s ‘confusing’ outfit
News.content:
KNOCKIN ON HEAVEN'S DOOR Bob Dylan meets with Pope Leo at Vatican – as fans left stumped by music icon’s ‘confusing’ outfit







Next

KNOCKIN’ on Heaven’s Door hitmaker Bob Dylan, 85, has sat down with Pope Leo at the Vatican.

But fans of the music legend were left confused by the musician’s strange get-up as he met the first American Pontiff.



As Pope Leo, born Robert Francis Prevost, came face to face with the music icon Bob, the singer wore a black hoodie.

The music legend had taken time out of his Italian tour to shake hands with the pope.



Dylan did not remove his hood as he posed with Pope Leo, though he did seem to remove his black leather gloves for a handshake.

The music legend’s strange ensemble involved an open-collared white shirt and loosely knotted tie, underneath a hoodie and black jacket.

In one particularly odd photo, Dylan did not seem to have bothered to put down his umbrella.

The singer performed at the Palazzo dello Sport as part of his Tough and Rowdy Ways tour before heading north to Bologna.

Chicago-born Pope Leo gifted Dylan a rosary.

In return, the singer gave the Pontiff a copy of Chronicles: Volume One, which details his long music career.



Rev. Antonio Spadaro, known for building bridges between the Catholic Church and the world of entertainment, brought the two Bobs together.

He raved on X: “It was hard not to feel the emotion of being part of an encounter that had a real sense of history about it, with the feeling that, at every step through the Apostolic Palace, absolutely anything could happen!”

The Chicago-born pope quoted Dylan’s little-known 1963 anti-nuclear protest song Go Away You Bomb in the preface to a book about disarmament.



And the singer has brushed shoulders with Pontiffs before, playing at the 23rd National Eucharistic Congress in Bologna, Italy, in 1977, as Pope John Paul II watched on.

John Paul II even referenced Blowin’ in the Wind as he addressed the crowd that night.

Pope Leo, 71, was recently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a common type of lung cancer.

The lump was caught by doctors “at an early stage,” and surgery earlier this month successfully removed a growth.

He went under the knife to have the lower part of his right lung where the growth had formed removed, the Vatican said.



The surgery lasted about 90 minutes and was successful with no complications, the Vatican said.

His diagnosis marks the first major health issue of his 17-month tenure.

Dylan fans on social media reacted to the photos saying: “my glorious confusing goat (greatest of all time).”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another said: “Is this s*** for real?”

While a third said: “he put on random clothes cause he knows he’s Bob Dylan”.

News.title: How Farage aims to show he’s still a serious candidate for PM after being blasted for being weak on defence
News.content:
Next

NIGEL Farage will today try to turn around his flagging poll numbers by showing he is still a serious candidate for Prime Minister.

This will see the Reform leader finally unveil his first defence spokesman after months without one.



Senior RAF officer Angus MacIntyre will take up the post after leaving a 40-year military career just last Friday.

It is telling that Farage has overlooked several jobless Reform MPs for the role but has instead drawn from the armed forces itself.



For months the Reform chief has faced criticism that he is weak on defence, and that when it comes to backing Ukraine he is often accused of being missing in action.

Today’s announcement aims to blunt that line of attack and begin to arrest the gradual slide in popularity he has been suffering.



Will it be enough to get him back to winning ways?

Since the highs of last summer when Reform seemed an unstoppable political force, Farage’s insurgent party has slipped into third behind Labour and the Tories.

It followed the £72million donation from two cryptobillionaires, a distracting Clacton by-election, two undercover stings and endless rows.

Farage has been written off before during his 30-year political career and got the last laugh, and he is still commanding a respectable 21 points in the polls.



But momentum can be everything in politics. Once lost, it is very hard to get back.

He will hope the gap in the news cycle today will allow him breathing space to get a hearing on this most pressing of issues.

The other big event today is a likely interest rate rise for the first time in more than three years.



At noon Bank of England chiefs are expected to hike rates in response to stubborn inflation caused by the Iran war.

It will deal a blow to Andy Burnham and his promise to ease the cost of living.

For that, he has Donald Trump to thank.

Talking of which, it will be interesting today to see how Farage responds to questions over his friend in the White House…

News.title: Uncle, nephew and worker horrifically suffocate in pig farm slurry pit after one fell in
News.content:
FARM TRAGEDY Uncle, nephew and worker horrifically suffocate in pig farm slurry pit after one fell in







Next

AN uncle, his nephew and a worker have suffocated in a horrific accident after one fell into a pig farm manure pit.

The trio are believed to have inhaled toxic fumes in what is Spain‘s deadliest farm disaster in 23 years.



A farm owner, 61, his nephew, 37, and another employee, 33, were confirmed as the deceased by Navarre Regional Police.

Cops investigating the incident said the leading theory is that one of them fell into the pit and the other two died trying to rescue him.



Emergency services were called to the pig farm near Pitillas, a municipality around 30 miles south of Pamplona, just after midday on Wednesday.

Paramedics, rescue helicopters and firefighters raced to the scene, but were unable to save the trio, who had died by the time they arrived.

The tragedy has sent shockwaves across the region, with Pitillas mayor Javier Ayerdi considering declaring an official period of mourning.

Ayerdi confirmed that the victims were residents of Caparroso, a neighbouring municipality.

The three deaths bring the total number of workplace fatalities in Navarre to 16 this year, according to data from the Workers’ Commissions Union.

It is the worst livestock farm disaster in Spain since April 2003, when four members of the same family died inhaling toxic fumes in Murcia.



Manure pits are particularly hazardous environments because they are poorly ventilated and the fermentation of animal excrement and urine rapidly depletes oxygen.

In many cases, the dangerous gases in these pits are odorless.

The most recent accident of this kind in Navarre happened in 2023, when a 74-year-old man died from inhaling fumes from a sheep manure storage tank.



A year earlier, two other workers suffocated at a cattle farm in a similar incident.

A dairy farmer died in a vain attempt to save his son when they both got into difficulty after climbing into a slurry tank in Cheshire.

Alan Ford, 72, climbed into the tank to rescue his son Richard, 42, at New Farm in Aston by Budworth on August 26.

Dad of five, Richard, who lived at the farm, had entered the tank earlier to repair a pipe.

After he got into difficulties, Alan also entered the tank to try and help him himself, an inquest heard.



Emergency services, including the air ambulance, were called to the family farm at 12.20pm, but despite the best efforts of all those involved, both men were pronounced dead at the scene.

News.title: Two teens arrested for murder 6 months after dad-of-three stabbed to death
News.content:
BLADE ARRESTS Two teens arrested for murder 6 months after dad-of-three stabbed to death







Next

TWO teens have been arrested after a dad-of-three was stabbed to death earlier this year.

Adrian Brown, 34, had been at the West Indian Sports and Social Club in Moss Side, Manchester, on May 8 when he was attacked at around 11pm.



The musician, known as Dre, suffered severe stab wounds to the chest and sadly died in hospital.

Addressing the incident, Detective Superintendent Toby Facey described it as a “shocking act of violence” as cops launched an investigation.



A 17-year-old boy and 18-year-old man were arrested on suspicion of murder today, cops said.

Police have also arrested a 27-year-old woman on suspicion of assisting an offender.

All three remain in custody for questioning.

In a heartbreaking tribute, his partner Tamia Zameer said at the time of his death: “R.I.P to my number one, Adrian.

“I love you always and forever. Me and your boys will cherish every moment that we had.

“We will miss you so much. Your legacy will forever live on and I will get the justice that you deserve.”



Adrian’s mum, Jennifer Meade, said: “My son, you did not deserve this. I can’t put into words how I feel. They took my boy.

“He was a loving son, brother, uncle, boyfriend, and he adored being a dad to my grandkids. I will miss you so much.

“Rest in peace, son. I love you more than you know.”

Detective Inspector Alex Wilkinson, of Greater Manchester Police (GMP), said the force had been working “tirelessly” to figure out what happened to Adrian that night.

“These arrests show the progress we are continuing to make and our commitment to bring offenders to justice,” he said.



“Our thoughts continue to be with Adrian’s family who have been updated on the investigation throughout and are being supported by specially trained officers.

“It has been almost six months since the fatal stabbing took place at the West Indian Sports and Social Club in Moss Side.

“We’d like to thank the people that have come forward since that night, however we believe that there may be more people out there who saw this tragic incident.

“All information is vital to our investigation to ensure we can support Adrian’s family and get justice for him.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops are urging anyone with information or footage to get in touch either online or over the phone.



Information can also be shared anonymously on the Greater Manchester Police website.

News.title: Labour’s immigration U-turn could leave taxpayers facing £5.2BILLION-a-year benefits bill, Tories warn
News.content:
Next

LABOUR’s immigration U-turn could leave taxpayers facing a £5.2billion-a-year benefits bill, the Tories warned last night.

Nearly half a million migrants granted permanent residency by 2030 could end up claiming Universal Credit, according to new Conservative analysis.



Their warning comes after Shabana Mahmood watered down her immigration crackdown after pressure from some Cabinet Ministers and more than a 100 Labour MPs.

Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately fumed: “Our country cannot afford the ballooning benefits bill. People who come to the UK should be contributing, not drawing benefits.



“We will prioritise Brits in the welfare system and stop giving benefits to immigrants. Indefinite Leave to Remain and Limited Leave to Remain will no longer give automatic access to Universal Credit and sickness benefits.

“This will save billions and there’s a principle at stake here too: British citizenship matters We are not a cash machine for the world.”

Home Office forecasts suggest 1.4million migrants will secure settlement by 2030, with the Tories estimating around 450,000 could claim Universal Credit if current claiming rates continue.

Their analysis found nearly one in three settled non-EU migrants already receive the benefit – with numbers soaring by almost 83,000 since June 2024.

The £5.2billion figure is a Conservative projection based on current claiming rates, rather than an official estimate of the cost of Labour’s concessions.

It comes after Ms Mahmood allowed nearly 300,000 foreign care workers and their families to retain a five-year route to settlement while also ditching proposals to make migrants wait until British citizenship before claiming benefits.

News.title: Fury as smoky-bacon flavoured crisps could be headed for the chop under Burnham’s Brexit reset
News.content:
Next

SMOKY bacon-flavoured crisps could be heading for the chop under Andy Burnham’s post-Brexit deal with Brussels.

They may breach EU regulations which ban “meaty” names on vegetarian food to supposedly stop shoppers from getting the wrong end of the stick.



That could spell trouble for veggie chicken and meat dishes for hard-working Brits if the PM agrees to follow the bloc’s new rules.

Britain and the EU agreed a food and drink deal before a summit taking place at the end of November.



Labour has agreed to align with EU plant and animal health rules including on labelling.

It comes as ketchup, mayonnaise and vinegar sachets could be banned from cafes and restaurants as the PM tries to align the UK with the EU.



The bloc has outlawed single-use plastic packaging for condiments in the catering sector on environmental grounds from January 1, 2030.

The regulations will forbid European restaurants and hotels from offering ketchup and mayonnaise sachets to dine-in customers from January 2030, to cut down on “unnecessary” waste.

The packets are also going to be banned in Northern Ireland under post-Brexit arrangements that require the country to follow some EU rules.

A No 10 spokesperson said: “A ban on single-serving sachets is not in the scope of any agreement with EU partners.



“It is not part of our EU reset.

“If any consultation on single-use sachets is taken forward, it will be solely as a result of the UK choosing to do so”

News.title: China bizarrely tries to claim bomb is a WINE bottle after its artillery shell was found in another country
News.content:
HINT OF GUNPOWDER China bizarrely tries to claim bomb is a WINE bottle after its artillery shell was found in another country







Next

CHINA has attempted to claim that a large military-grade explosive found in a shipping container in another country was simply a wine bottle.

The 32kg object, cylindrical with a pointed end, is just a “shell-shaped wine bottle”, Beijing insisted.



The explosive export was found in Papua New Guinea, where police identified it as a working artillery shell.

Four Chinese citizens were arrested after the alarming discovery at a shipping wharf in Port Moresby.



Papua New Guinea cops x-rayed the shell to verify its lethal contents after it was found on Friday.

A police report confirmed that the item was an undetonated 130mm Type 59 Artillery Projectile, packed with chemical explosives and a fuse, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.



But China continued to claim that the 32kg object was simply a “shell-shaped wine bottle” that “poses no danger at all”.

The object sparked a diplomatic row between the two nations, as Beijing insisted that such a weapon could never have been exported from its shores.

The Chinese Embassy in Papua New Guinea wrote on Facebook: “China enforces some of the world’s strictest firearm control laws and regulations.

“Therefore, it is virtually impossible for an illegal military-grade artillery shell to be smuggled out of China to PNG.”



Some shared images online of an “artillery round replica militaria bottle holder” that is sold on Etsy.

But the replica was made of plastic, and significantly lighter than the object found in the shipping container.

One bemused commenter asked: “What sort of wine bottle weighs 32kg?”



Cops dismissed the idea that it could be a dummy.

Papua New Guinea’s military and police launched a joint investigation after finding the shell, said police commissioner David Manning.

He explained: “Police acted quickly upon receiving information that the artillery round had been discovered.

“The area was secured to prevent the risk of harm in the surrounding area.

“This enabled police and military explosive disposal experts to move in, examine the device and have it safely moved to be stored in a secure facility.”



It comes as island nations like Papua New Guinea have become caught up in power plays between China and the West, as powers compete for access to the Second Island Chain.

The strategic string of islands hosts naval bases which act as barriers to China’s sea operations.

Australia signed a defence deal with Papua New Guinea last October, the first of its kind.

Aussie PM Anthony Albanese and PNG’s foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko both slammed a Chinese nuclear-capable ballistic missile test in the Pacific that took place in July.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And last week Australia’s defence minister Richard Marles warned China’s massive military build-up in the region was whipping up “conditions of pressure” in southeast Asia.



He said: “We’re obviously seeing the biggest conventional military build-up that the world has seen since the end of the Second World War from China.”

News.title: Britain is overspent, overborrowed and overtaxed yet Burnham STILL hands out cash
News.content:
Next

ANDY BURNHAM wants to please everyone, but if he keeps giving everything away we will have nothing left.

Four months into the job, and we still haven’t found anyone he is willing to say no to — apart from businesses begging him not to put up their taxes.



He forced Keir Starmer out of No10 with no plan other than to get his hands on the public credit card and embark on a spending spree for his backbenchers.

Look at the latest immigration chaos.



The Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, promised to be tough on indefinite leave to remain but all it took was a few grumpy Labour MPs to complain and Burnham caved.

On the face of it this is an immigration issue, but it is also another chance for Burnham to tap the public credit card.

Now low-paid foreign-born care workers will be able to get settlement after just five years, at a cost to the taxpayer of ­billions of pounds.

A price he seems to be willing to pay to buy off people in his own party.

Now add to that the already ballooning bill for working-age benefits, which will soon hit an eye-watering £183billion a year.

That’s more than we spend on defence, schools and policing put together.



It works out at about £10,000 for every working household in the country — ­especially hard to stomach at a time when families are feeling the pinch.

And now we hear this week from Burnham’s trip to the Commonwealth that he wants to apologise (again) for Britain’s part in the slave trade.

He said he wouldn’t put reparations on the table, but when asked whether his apology could end up costing taxpayers more, he couldn’t give a straight answer.



This is the trouble with a Prime Minister who simply cannot say no.

Once you open the door to more demands, where does it end? The bill could be enormous, and it won’t be Burnham picking up the tab.

The job of a Prime Minister is not to please everyone. It is to make difficult choices in our country’s best interests.

Britain is overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of- control welfare system.

Every day that Andy Burnham ducks hard decisions and hands out more cash, Britain slides deeper into a mess of the Labour Party’s making.



At the Budget last month, he had a chance to do the right thing and cut wasteful spending.

Instead, he and his Chancellor spent yet more money we don’t have on things we can’t afford.

Labour’s welfare addiction has maxed out Britain’s credit cards, and the Government is taking out more credit cards to pay down that debt.



You’d have to be completely hard of thinking to believe that is a good idea.

Our children and grandchildren will one day be paying for their stupidity.

Hard-working taxpayers are already being crushed under the highest tax burden in our country’s history.

But worst of all, at a time when Russia might attack one of our Nato allies, Britain cannot fund our defence because the Prime Minister is giving all our money away.

We simply can’t afford Andy Burnham. If he is too weak to stand up to Labour backbenchers and French exchange students, what chance does he stand against Vladimir Putin?



This week he said he is going to release a ten-year plan. That’s very ambitious for a man without a ten-month plan.

But now we hear it will be a consultation instead! A plan to consult on a plan. And who knows how much cash he’ll have handed out by the time that’s finished.

Britain doesn’t need a Prime Minister working out what he thinks. We need a leader who already understands the difficult choices we must make and has the courage to make them. That is what my new Conservative Party have a plan to do.

We will cut spending by £70billion and get millions of people off welfare and back into work. The Labour Party think that is cruel, but any parent knows that sometimes the kindest thing is to say no.

We will cut the deficit by £35billion, and start living within our means. Borrowing so much is making our ­country poorer and weaker.



No other party in British politics seems to care about the mess we are leaving for our children.

We will fund Britain’s defence properly, because the world is a dangerous place and we are already under threat.

Cyber-attacks are happening every day on British businesses, and Russian warships are in the English ­Channel. There is no time to waste.

Then, we will cut your taxes. Because a strong economy will make life better for every single person in this country.

Under the Conservatives, there will be more opportunity, life will be more affordable and people will be rewarded for working hard and doing the right thing.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

That is what a real plan for this country looks like, and those are the decisions a serious leader would take. Britain cannot afford three more years of Andy Burnham spending like there’s no tomorrow because he wants to people please.

He should be taking the tough decisions, or he should get out of the way so ­someone else can.

News.title: Bedfordshire school on lockdown after nearby shooting as police launch manhunt
News.content:
Bedfordshire school on lockdown after nearby shooting as police launch manhunt

Bedfordshire Police are searching for a gunman after officers responded to reports of a firearm discharge near a school shortly before 3.30pm on Wednesday

View 3 Images The incident occurred close to a school (Image: Casey Edwards)

A manhunt for a gunman is underway after a Bedfordshire school was placed into lockdown when a firearm was discharged nearby.

Bedfordshire Police said they responded to reports of a firearm discharge shortly before 3.30pm on Wednesday, November 4 in Grebe Drive, Leighton Buzzard. Specialist armed officers were deployed to the area and later identified a vehicle believed to be at the scene of the discharge.

Officers indicated for the driver to stop and a chase ensued. The car came to a stop in Porz Avenue, Dunstable after it collided with an unrelated vehicle.

View 3 Images Police were called to reports of a firearms discharge shortly before 3.30pm (Image: Casey Edwards)

One man was treated at the scene for minor injuries and those inside the suspect vehicle fled on foot. Police are searching the area. A lower school in close proximity to the incident was placed in lockdown for a short period as a precautionary measure.

Police did not name the school in their statement, but Greenleas School is in close proximity to the incident and has issued a public statement following the incident.

Greenleas School said in a statement on its website: "School is open as normal 5th November. Thank you to the children, staff and parents for their composure and calm during the incident today."

View 3 Images Police did not name the school in their statement, but Greenleas School is in close proximity to the incident (Image: Google Maps)

Porz Avenue remains closed between Boscombe Way and Lovatt Road roundabout as emergency services respond to the crash.

Residents have been asked to avoid the area and use alternative routes if driving.

"We understand this is a concerning incident but would like to reassure the public that a strong police presence will remain while initial enquiries take place," Bedfordshire Police wrote in a post on Facebook.

Additional scene guards have been allocated in Grebe Drive and on the A505. Anyone with information has been asked to call 999, quoting Operation Tanglewood.

Article continues below

The Mirror has reached out to Greenleas School for further comment on the incident.

News.title: 'Trump has spent years treating Americans like fools - now they have made biggest fool pay the price'
News.content:
'Trump has spent years treating Americans like fools - now they have made biggest fool pay the price'

The man who demanded unquestioning loyalty now faces two years of blocked appointments, frustrated ambitions, investigations and potentially a third impeachment.

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Donald Trump has spent years treating Americans like fools, poisoning their politics, insulting their intelligence and believing his bullying, lies and arrogance would never catch up with him.

‌



‌



Now the country he thought he could manipulate indefinitely has delivered a crushing verdict on his presidency. And the humiliation is richly deserved.

‌



Americans have stripped his Republican Party of control of both houses of Congress, turning even strongholds such as Texas, Kansas and South Carolina Democratic. Trump blamed his absence from the ballot. The truth is that millions knew precisely who they were voting against.

‌



Now the man who demanded unquestioning loyalty faces two years of blocked appointments, frustrated ambitions, investigations and potentially a third impeachment. His Republican protectors have been swept aside. Congressional committees can finally demand answers about the conduct of his administration.

Trump promised Americans they would grow tired of winning. Instead, they grew utterly sick of him. And after years of being taken for fools, Americans have finally made the biggest fool of all pay the price.

‌



Crisis is now

Millions of families are being urged to stockpile three days' worth of food and water in case of floods, extreme weather, power cuts, or cyberattacks that disrupt essential services. It is sensible advice in an increasingly uncertain world.

But for those struggling to afford tonight's dinner, filling cupboards for a future emergency is an impossible luxury. Only 44% of households have sufficient supplies, with younger adults particularly exposed.

‌



Ministers suggest building up stocks gradually. But when soaring rents, energy bills and food prices swallow every spare penny, even a few extra tins can be unaffordable.

The Government wants Britain prepared for the next national emergency. It must recognise that millions are already living through a financial one.

Article continues below

Stroll not scroll

Only one in six British teenagers exercises daily, with girls particularly missing out. Youngsters need more encouragement to get active. After all, if scrolling through TikTok counted as exercise, Britain would have the fittest thumbs in the world.

News.title: Man arrested after pointing 'finger gun' at troops near White House as tensions rise
News.content:
Man arrested after pointing 'finger gun' at troops near White House as tensions rise

The 28-year-old was arrested for "threats in a menacing manner" and according to D.C. law, the charge carries a maximum sentence of up to 180 days in prison or an $1,000 fine

View 3 Images A man was arrested near the White House on Monday (Image: Getty Images)

A 28-year-old man was arrested this week after allegedly threatening National Guard troops. The threat reportedly amounted to making a 'finger gun' gesture.

‌



‌



Court documents describe William Clark's actions as allegedly making a "finger gun" gesture at National Guard troops near the White House. His arrest comes amid hostilities between locals and the National Guard.

‌



He was arrested for "threats in a menacing manner", court documents say, which carries a maximum sentence of up to 180 days in prison or an $1,000 fine. The documents also said he carried out "assault on a police officer".

‌



He was "holding a cell phone in one hand while the other hand was making a shooting gesture with a finger gun".

View 3 Images Members of the National Guards in Washington D.C. (Image: Getty Images)

Mr Clark is facing a misdemeanour charge and pleaded not guilty, according to court records.

‌



The incident occurred at 15th and E streets NW at around 5.20pm local time and he was detained by National Guard members until D.C. police arrived.

The National Guard has been in the US capital for more than a year.

‌



Troops were also deployed to at least seven states for the midterm election held on Tuesday. Their focus was on monitoring ballot boxes and assisting in election security efforts.

The Guard's presence has not been received well with local officials, who have said the deployment is unnecessary, costly and lacking a clear strategy.

‌



View 3 Images The National Guard has been present in the US capital for more than a year (Image: Getty Images)

Last month, one member of the National Guard was shot in the leg while trying to break up a fight in Washington DC and last year, two others were shot blocks away from the White House, killing one and critically wounding the other.

Article continues below

US President Donald Trump has argued that the National Guard has significant reduced crime in the capital. But critics say that guardsmen cannot make arrests and have not been stationed in high crime areas.

According to The Hill news outlet, the Pentagon is expected to keep a National Guard in DCuntil Inauguration Day 2029.

News.title: US midterms 2026 live: Trump breaks cover in rambling White House ballroom speech but doesn't mention results
News.content:
Donald Trump has nicknamed himself 'Mr Veto' after the Democrats surged to a resounding victory in yesterday's US midterms elections, and firmly leaves the President in 'lame duck' status

Donald Trump has appeared at the construction site of his White House ballroom, where he gave a rambling speech about his controversial project - but made no mention of the devastating midterm election loss his party suffered.

Speaking to reporters at the site, Trump went on about how his site "will be the most beautiful ballroom" in the world. He pointed to workers who had been brought in to work on the renovations as he claimed he "grew up with construction sites."

Trump went on to praise the structure claiming "you could put as many helicopters as you want on the roof", before going on to describe the ballroom as 'drone-proof, missile-proof and bulletproof.'

Trump has today vowed to veto Democratic legislation in what he describes his "ultimate power". Reacting to a crushing night in the US midterm elections, the President welcomed the moniker "Mr Veto," in terms of describing his approach to the Democrats. His rival party took control of the House and the Senate in a humiliating blow to the world leader.

It is a historic rout of the Republican Party — and a scale of victory most Democrats wouldn't dream of even a few months ago. While official results are still yet to be announced, Democrats have had several important wins so far, including Democratic flips in North and South Carolina.

Young voters have strongly turned out for the Democratic Party, and their support could prove pivotal, a campaign group has said. "Preliminary results from tonight make it clear that this is a blue tsunami,” Santiago Mayer, executive director of Voters of Tomorrow said.

News.title: Body of newborn baby found at homeless shelter as mum arrested
News.content:
Body of newborn baby found at homeless shelter as mum arrested

A 39-year-old woman, believed to be the mother, has been arrested after the body of a newborn baby was found at a homeless shelter in the state of Brandenburg, Germany

View 2 Images The property in Calau in the Brandenburg region of Germany was being used a homeless shelter, local media has reported (Image: Google Maps)

A mum is suspected of killing her new born baby with the body found at a homeless shelter in Germany.

‌



‌



The 39-year-old woman was arrested following the discovery of the baby on Sunday at the accommodation on Am Bahnhof street in Calau, Brandenburg, and she remains in custody.

‌



A spokesperson for the Cottbus public prosecutor's office reportedly said: "It appears to be a violent crime" but no details were given about the nature of the injuries and how they came about.

‌



It is understood that the arrested woman is the mother of the dead child and that the baby died shortly after being born. Local media has reported that the baby was found by another resident at the homeless shelter.

Helicopter crashes close to Florida beach days after jet disaster - One dead and two injured READ MORE :

Police have been seen this week at the shelter including a forensic team on Wednesday with investigators searching a courtyard and they appeared to hone in on an outbuilding. Dustbins were also examined and photographed by detectives, reported Bild.

View 2 Images Police forensics teams have been seen searching outbuildings at the property (Image: Google Maps)

‌



The investigation is ongoing and the woman is being held in custody at Luckau-Duben.

It comes after a child was found dead in a hotel room in Germany, with police treating the death as a suspected homicide.

‌



Emergency services were called to a hotel on Arnulfstrasse in Munich, the capital of the German state of Bavaria, at around 9.40am local time (8.40am GMT) on Wednesday after a hotel employee discovered a child's body. German media have reported that the child was 12 years old.

A woman, who is reported to be the child's mother, was found seriously injured at the scene. The hotel has been identified by German media as the Eden Hotel Wolff.

‌



German newspaper Bild is reporting that investigators suspect the woman, who is said to be a Ukrainian national, killed her child before attempting to take her own life.

The four-star hotel, which was founded in 1890, is located directly opposite Munich Central Station. It has more than 200 rooms, as well as an on-site restaurant and wellness facilities. Investigations into the circumstances surrounding the incident are ongoing, with police reviewing footage from the hotel's CCTV cameras.

News.title: Mum tried to fight off machete wielding 'gangster' holding baby in her arms
News.content:
Mum tried to fight off machete wielding 'gangster' holding baby in her arms

Kadeem Hodgson, 26, chased Lauren Parr and her six-year-old daughter down the street with a machete before attempting to force himself into a neighbour's house in St Helens

View Image Kadeem Hodgson, of Longridge Avenue, St Helens (Image: Merseyside Police)

A machete wielding thug landed blows within cms of a mum's head as she held held her baby as he hacked at a door she was desperately trying to keep shut.

‌



‌



Kadeem Hodgson, 26, described in court as a "minor league gangster" had pursued a "defenceless, screaming" woman and her six-year-old daughter along the street brandishing a machete. As she took shelter in a neighbours home he hacked wildy at the door while the neighbour held onto her baby on the other side.

‌



Hodgson was captured on CCTV chasing Lauren Parr she fled to a neighbour's home with her six-year-old daughter. The terrifying incident took place on Sutton Heath Road in St Helens at approximately 4.45pm on September 10, after the woman's son arrived home and told her he was being pursued by Hodgson.

‌



Liverpool Crown Court heard that there had been an "earlier incident" between the two men.

At the hearing on November 4, prosecutor Derryn Gibney said: "Lauren Parr left her property with her daughter - both in their pyjamas - her daughter was barefoot. They ran down the street when she noticed the defendant following behind her, who gestured to his waistband."

CCTV footage shown to the court captured Ms Parr sprinting into a neighbour's front garden with her daughter held in her arms. She placed her daughter down on the grass as she called out to her neighbour, Siana Beech, who scooped up the screaming child and rushed inside the house, reports the Liverpool Echo.

‌



Seconds later, Hodgson appeared and stormed into the garden, charging towards the property. The sound of frantic banging followed as he attempted to force his way through the door.

He subsequently appeared to abandon his efforts and fled the scene as neighbouring residents, drawn outside by the commotion, emerged from their homes. Ms Gibney said: "The footage, the Crown says, speaks for itself. Siana Beech describes she was trying to keep the door shut herself. At one point the machete, which the defendant was hacking at the door with, was coming through the door in proximity to her head, and damage was caused to the front door."

‌



In a statement, Ms Beech said: "He had blood all over his face. I saw the man trying to force his way through my front door. I was holding my one-year-old daughter and trying desperately to keep the door shut.

"He kicked the door and tried to shove the machete through the gap. At one point it came within 10cm of my head.

‌



"I genuinely believed he would get through and that I, my children or my partner would be seriously hurt or killed. I still think of how close the machete came to my head and I wonder what would have happened if the door had opened."

She revealed the harrowing ordeal had left her feeling unsafe within her own home and "constantly on edge and afraid it will happen again".

‌



She said: "The thought that I would be unable to protect my children continues to haunt me. Since the incident they have been lashing out and behaving differently. They've said that the bad man is coming back. It's heartbreaking to hear this. I worry about how this has affected their sense of safety.

"The incident was relatively short but its consequences have continued. Every unexpected noise can bring the fear back. Since this has happened, I'm constantly thinking about protecting my children and what I would do if someone tried to enter again.

‌



"I never expected to have to hold a door shut while someone with a machete tried to get inside.

"The physical damage to the door can be repaired, but the fear and memories cannot be repaired so easily. I'm still living with the consequences every day. I want to feel safe again. I want my children to feel safe again."

‌



Hodgson, of Longridge Avenue, St Helens, pleaded guilty to possession of a bladed article, affray, and criminal damage. He appeared in court today, November 4, for sentence.

He has 23 previous convictions for 33 offences, including possession of a bladed article, wounding, affray, and threatening someone with an offensive weapon.

‌



Sarah Griffin, defending, said: "He realises the offending is shocking. He hasn't sought to justify his behaviour. He is remorseful. He regrets that his issues with others have affected innocent parties and he has asked to apologise to the victims through me.

"He has taken part in a thinking skills course because he now acknowledges the significant impact of these offences."

‌



'You had a machete down your trousers and you chased a defenceless, screaming woman' Passing sentence, Judge Simon Medland said: "You're still a young man with the whole of the rest of your life ahead of you. You have committed multiple offences in your few years and you have three youth cautions against your name.

"There's yet the opportunity, if you choose to take it, to stop committing offences. But for as long as you conduct yourself like this, as a sort of minor league gangster, the sentences will get longer and longer.

‌



"So my question to you is this. Do you want to spend years in custody, or do you want to do something useful with your life? You'll have plenty enough time to have a think.

"I can assure you if you don't take the opportunity of readdressing your life, you will find yourself committing offences where you're sentenced to years and years in custody.

‌



"On the last occasion, you were sentenced to 28 months. You didn't take that warning. You didn't take the warning either, when you were sentenced to 17 months for threatening someone with a blade in 2020.

"We come to this matter. You had a machete down your trousers and you chased a defenceless, screaming woman into another house. She was carrying a little girl. She was terrified and you were the cause of that.

Article continues below

"I'm told you understand that now, and so you should. That behaviour was appalling."

Hodgson was handed a 31-month sentence for possession of a bladed article, alongside a concurrent 21 months for affray and one month for criminal damage, bringing his total time behind bars to 31 months.

News.title: Man accused of murdering woman, 21, had 'Jack the Ripper' fascination, court hears
News.content:
Man accused of murdering woman, 21, had 'Jack the Ripper' fascination, court hears

Brandon Rainey, 30, is accused of murdering 21-year-old Chloe Mitchell whose dismembered body was found in two bins in Ballymena, a court heard

View 3 Images Chloe Mitchell's dismembered body was found in two bins (Image: PA)

A woman had a "cruel and brutal death" before being “mutilated and dismembered”, a murder trial has heard.

Brandon Rainey, who is accused of murdering the 21-year-old Chloe Mitchell, told a “catalogue of lies” to police and had a fascination with Jack the Ripper, jurors were told.

Belfast Crown Court also heard that Rainey attempted to order “amputation knives” online from surgical companies.

Ms Mitchell’s body was found dismembered and put into two residential bins in Ballymena days after she went missing in June 2023.

Rainey, 30, formerly of James Street in the town, has been charged with murdering Ms Mitchell and attempting to prevent the burial of her body. He pleaded not guilty to the charges at a hearing in 2024.

View 3 Images Brandon Rainey is on trial for murder

A large number of Ms Mitchell’s family and friends were in court today with Rainey, wearing a grey hoodie and grey cargo trousers, in the dock.

The court heard that Ms Mitchell’s cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head and stab wounds to the chest. Outlining the case against Rainey, prosecution barrister David Russell KC told the jury there is a “body of evidence that we say points clearly to Mr Rainey being the perpetrator in the killing of Chloe Mitchell”.

“It was a cruel and brutal death at his hands and we say given the nature of the attack he clearly intended to kill her,” he said. “She had been the victim of a sustained assault with weapons whilst alive and then mutilated and dismembered in death.

“And we say that when you stand back and hear all the evidence in this case you’ll be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that Brandon Rainey murdered Chloe Mitchell.”

Mr Russell described Rainey and Ms Mitchell as being in “an on/off relationship” at the time of her death, adding that she was a young woman with “significant addiction issues”.

View 3 Images Family and friends of the victim pictured outside court (Image: Liam McBurney/Press Association)

He read the recollection of two of Ms Mitchell’s friends who had been with her when she was last seen alive on June 3. One recalled an incident when they had been at Rainey’s home and he had “become aggressive with Chloe and wouldn’t let her leave”, and another when he grabbed her by the hair and “threw her against the shutter of a shop so hard she fell”.

On the evening of Friday June 2, Ms Mitchell and two friends went to Rainey’s flat in James Street, where they drank with him for a short time, before the friends left Ms Mitchell alone with him.

During this encounter one of the friends recalled Rainey saying “I would love to chop someone up and melt them in the bath”, and when challenged on this saying he was “only joking”.

Jurors were shown CCTV of a man taking three journeys to and from the direction of James Street carrying black bags at around 5.20am on June 3.

‌



Mr Russell outlined the moment an officer found Ms Mitchell’s remains on Sunday June 11 in two residential bins in the James Street area. He said the officer was alerted by a “smell emanating from the back” of a neighbouring property.

“The bin was full, it smelled putrid and other resources were sought to carry out a search of that bin,” Mr Russell said. The officer then identified a further bin in the alley and “when he opened it a large number of flies came out of the bin”.

‌



Mr Russell read graphic descriptions from the post-mortem report describing the condition of Ms Mitchell’s dismembered body that had been split between the two bins.

A number of those in the public gallery with Ms Mitchell’s family left or became visibly emotional as the intense injuries were outlined.

‌



“The severe decomposition and dismemberment of her body precluded her from being visually identified,” Mr Russell said. “Her teeth were compared to dental records and a tattoo correlated with one described by family members.”

Mr Russell said the post-mortem report noted that incisions related to the dismemberment were “relatively clean cut, consistent with having been cut with a sharp object such as a knife”.

‌



Ms Mitchell’s ears were not found with her body or in either of the bins. There were further descriptions of injuries to the 21-year-old’s head, with fractures to the right side of her skull and “probable bruising to skin” that would be “consistent with at least some of the blows, if not all, having occurred while Chloe was alive”.

A fracture to the right side of the jaw “could have been a punch but could also have been the result of a kick or a stamp”, again with bruising indicating this may have occurred while Ms Mitchell was alive.

‌



Mr Russell said she also suffered “at least 55 stab wounds to the skin’s surface consistent with having been caused with a bladed weapon such as a knife” and it was “apparent bruising associated with some of the stabbings suggesting they took place when Chloe was alive”.

The barrister went on to outline what he described as a “very substantial forensic connection between Brandon Rainey and 22 James Street and Chloe Mitchell”.

‌



He described a number of areas of Rainey’s flat where blood spots or smears matching Ms Mitchell were identified including the front door handle, meter box, utility room wall, living room armchair, bedroom wall and beside table.

Items with blood matching Ms Mitchell were also recovered and examined by police including three blood stained plastic bags and a blood stained Nike trainer found on the outside window sill.

‌



Mr Russell described police findings from the examination of Rainey’s phone, where he had made repeated attempts to order “amputation knives” online from surgical companies.

Also on the defendant’s phone were repeated searches for Jack the Ripper, and it was heard that his username on one online gaming profile was “randotheripper”.

‌



Testimony was read from a man who recalled attending a barbecue in Ballymena on June 1 when Rainey stripped to his boxer shorts revealing he had a large knife in a sheath.

This witness also claims to have overheard the defendant saying to his mother: “Would you still love me if I dismembered 50 people and hid their parts?” and could not be sure if he was joking.

‌



Mr Russell read jurors some of the contents of Rainey’s interviews with police in June 2023, both before and after the discovery of Ms Mitchell’s remains.

When the defendant was asked by police if he knew where Ms Mitchell was, he answered “I don’t know”, which the prosecution barrister described as the “first of a catalogue of lies”. He said Rainey “repeatedly lied to police” in saying he did not know where Ms Mitchell was and “repeatedly denied harming her”.

Article continues below

The trial continues on Monday.

News.title: 'A little rich of him': Why the Tories have no right to lecture Labour on border control
News.content:
'A little rich of him': Why the Tories have no right to lecture Labour on border control

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp laid into Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood earlier this week when she unveiled a massive overhaul of settlement rules for migrants

View 3 Images

Tory criticism of Labour's immigration reforms is a "little rich" after their record in power, the Mirror's Political Editor Lizzy Buchan has said.

‌



‌



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp laid into Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood earlier this week when she unveiled a massive overhaul of settlement rules for migrants. Under the plans, half a million people face longer waits for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) as the standard wait to qualify will double from its current five years. High earners and NHS staff will be among those who can apply sooner.

‌



Ms Mahmood announced a carve out for care workers as she rowed back on controversial plans to make them wait up to 15 years to qualify. Mr Philp accused her of carrying out a humiliating U-turn - and claimed she'd bowed to pressure from within her party.

‌



Speaking to the Mirror's Nicola Thorp on the Sense Check show, Lizzy said it was difficult for the Tories to attack Labour after their record in Government on immigration. Net migration surged after Brexit, peaking at 944,000 in year ending March 2023. It was dubbed the "Boris wave" by critics.

Shabana Mahmood's huge changes to UK immigration rules explained in full READ MORE :

View 3 Images Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp tried to attack Shabana Mahmood over immigration reforms (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

Lizzy said: "The Conservatives were in charge when so many people came over. As was Chris Philp. I think it's quite hard for the Conservatives to really land blows with those kinds of attacks considering they not only allowed lots of people to come here legally during those years when Boris Johnson was PM and after, but also they allowed the asylum system to get out of control.

‌



"They started housing people in hotels. They're responsible for so much of that. So I think it's a little rich of him to say that. And actually... these reforms are really tough. [They are] far more hard line than anything the Conservatives did."

Mr Philp authorised use of asylum hotels as an immigration minister in the pandemic, which ramped up under the Tories. Labour has pledged to end use by the end of this Parliament.

‌



View 3 Images Lizzy Buchan Mirror Political Editor said 'The Government are trying to bring immigration under control and therefore starve Farage and his gang of that argument and that ability to kind of whip people up."

‌



Nigel Farage was nowhere to be seen in the Commons when Ms Mahmood delivered her statement on Monday - choosing instead to deliver an "emergency" press conference outside of Parliament.

Asked about Reform's response, Lizzy said: "It's a bit of a tricky one for Reform in a way because they want to get rid of ILR completely and replace it with, I think, rolling sort of five-year visas. But the plans are quite tough, and so it's not that easy for him to come at Shabana Mahmood... So I think it's quite tricky for them.

Article continues below

"Actually, that's part of why Labour's doing it, really. It takes some of the air out of what Reform are trying to argue about Britain's immigration system being totally out of control. The Government are trying to bring it under control and therefore starve Farage and his gang of that argument and that ability to kind of whip people up."

New episodes of the Mirror's show Sense Check are available on YouTube. Subscribe to the channel to make sure you don’t miss an episode www.youtube.com/@MirrorSenseCheck.

News.title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
News.content:
Vice-President JD Vance sent shockwaves through Washington on Wednesday by blaming his party's midterm defeat squarely on the Iran war, in what was widely interpreted as an effort to distance himself from President Donald Trump ahead of a potential 2028 White House run.

In a carefully calibrated, 600-word statement on X, the vice-president acknowledged that Trump's 2024 voters had deserted Republicans in the midterm election.

"The reason we lost is the war," he wrote. "The president himself said so last night."

In interviews late Tuesday night and Wednesday, Trump had defended the war but acknowledged that it played a factor in Democrats flipping control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

Vance's view on the war in Iran is an open secret in Washington. While he has repeatedly backed the conflict since the US and Israel attacked Tehran in February, he has reportedly expressed opposition in private meetings with administration officials.

But those disagreements had been kept out of the public eye - until now.

News.title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology
News.content:
The UK has signed up to "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith" talks that address the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, Commonwealth leaders in Antigua have said.

The formal conclusions marking the end of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, known as the communique, is the joint text setting out what has been agreed.

The 18 page document, external includes a paragraph in which the leaders "welcome the agreement of the Government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms".

It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened the door to a formal apology on behalf of the UK for its role in the slave trade, while ruling out the prospect of reparations.

Officials said the timeframe for the talks would be agreed at a later date, though the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has suggested they are likely to conclude in around a year.

Asked whether the government might reach the point of a formal apology by the time it hosts the G20 leaders' summit in Manchester next November, Miliband told BBC Newscast, external: "Broadly speaking, yes."

News.title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients
News.content:
The distress of the man on the other end of the video call was clear to dementia specialist nurse Louise Burns. He was struggling to get his elderly mum, who had the condition, out of hospital - she needed support to move into her home.

Burns was able to put him at ease. She is part of a team running virtual clinics that support more than 100 patients and family members a week: "No matter what stage they are at, we try to help," she says. She explained the discharge process and where to go for help. The man's mother was soon back where she wanted to be.

Traditionally, a service like this would have been run by the National Health Service â but the clinic, which was set up during Covid and continued because of strong demand, is entirely funded by the charity Dementia UK.

The charity's chief nursing officer Paul Edwards says it is "trying to fill the gaps" within stretched NHS services. Burns adds: "The NHS and social care are under such huge pressure and dementia cases are rising - it's not always easy to get the support you need."

Dementia UK is just one of many charities working in the health sphere. From children's care to mental health and cancer services, charities are playing an increasingly important role in caring for patients.

News.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
News.content:
By 2014, Wong, who was then at the forefront of a civil disobedience movement known as the "Umbrella Movement", had already become one of the most recognisable faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement.

In 2016, he co-founded Demosisto with Law and Agnes Chow, an activist who is now also in exile.

But he often expressed discomfort at being labelled a "protest leader".

"We have a lot of facilitators in this movement and I'm one of them...âInstead of having a top-down command, we now have a bottom-up command hub," Wong told The Financial Times in November 2019.

Demosisto disbanded in 2020, the year Beijing introduced the controversial National Security Law (NSL) in Hong Kong.

Law left for the UK and continued his advocacy abroad, while Wong stayed on in Hong Kong and tried to run for a seat in its legislature â but was barred, with authorities citing his opposition to the NSL as one of the reasons.

Meanwhile, the court cases against Wong were stacking up.

On 23 November 2020, he pleaded guilty to several charges related to his involvement in protests outside the Hong Kong police headquarters in 2019.

Then came the NSL charges. While still in prison in February 2021, Wong was among 47 people charged with "conspiracy to commit subversion". The group became known as the Hong Kong 47 and remains the largest prosecution so far under the NSL.

Wong was still serving his 56-month sentence for the subversion conviction when he was charged with collusion under the NSL last year.

On 22 November 2020, the day before he pleaded guilty to the protest charges, Wong wrote in a post on Instagram addressed to "the people of Hong Kong": "To be honest, I have never had much faith in Hong Kong's politics, but I have every confidence in the people of Hong Kong.

"Even as political power now poses a comprehensive challenge to the resilience of our civil society, I believe the people of Hong Kong will, as always, find a way to see things through."

The harshest NSL sentence thus far had been handed to former media tycoon Jimmy Lai, who was jailed for 20 years, also for colluding with foreign forces.

News.title: Interest rates expected to rise for first time in over three years
News.content:
Policymakers at the Bank of England are expected to raise interest rates on Thursday in what would be the first increase to the benchmark rate for more than three years.

Most analysts are predicting an rise from 3.75% to 4% in a move that would increase the cost of borrowing for individuals and businesses, but boost savers.

The Bank rate has fallen from its 2023-24 peak of 5.25%, although the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has left the rate unchanged at its last six meetings.

Rising inflation, driven primarily by the cost of petrol and diesel, will push policymakers into an interest rate hike, analysts suggest.

The announcement will be made by the Bank at 12:00 GMT on Thursday.

Close attention will also be paid to any hints from the MPC on the future direction of interest rates.

"The decision is increasingly less about whether rates reach 4% and more about what follows after that," said Chris Cheverall, head of UK at trading platform CMC Markets.

"A quarter-point rise is already widely expected, but the Bank now has to balance inflation that is still too high against an economy where the growth outlook has weakened sharply."

News.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'
News.content:
Wild weather is a way of life for people living along the coast in the Philippines, Taiwan, China and Japan. But the last few months have been extraordinary.

A wave of intense and, at times, unpredictable storms exacerbated by the El NiÃ±o weather pattern has killed dozens, shuttered major airports and wiped out crops and infrastructure across a swathe of East Asia.

In October, nearly all of Taiwan shut down as a monster storm big enough to engulf the island of 23 million roared towards its north-eastern coast. Equivalent to a category five hurricane, Typhoon Champi's 295km/h (193mph) winds had the power to flatten homes and whip up destructive waves.

Thankfully it did not make landfall in Taiwan, skirting past the island while dousing it in rain. But it had far-reaching impacts: hundreds of flights were cancelled in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan. In the Philippines' Batanes archipelago, seaside highways shut as huge waves crashed onto the shore, and in southern Japan's Okinawa islands, power was cut to 15,000 homes.

News.title: Pound rises to its highest level since the Brexit referendum
News.content:
The value of sterling fell significantly after the Brexit referendum in June 2016, and reached further lows during the Brexit process, the Covid pandemic and the 2022 mini-Budget.

Some traders said the UK was being seen in a different light given relative political stability, solid growth and the rapprochement with the European Union.

Sterling has responded strongly to Brexit developments and political uncertainty in recent years.

Jim O'Neill, an economist and former Treasury minister, said: "I'm not surprised. People were, and to a lesser extent, are, underestimating the improving momentum in the UK,"

A stronger pound can help rein in inflation, and increase buying power for consumers on imports and on holidays.

UK growth so far this year has outperformed all forecasts, but there are signs that higher energy and fuel prices have now hit consumer confidence.

The Bank's nine member Monetary Policy Committee faces an important decision on interest rates on Thursday, with the first rise in three years widely expected.

On Wednesday sterling was up 0.28% against the dollar at $1.3434 and was flat against the euro at â¬1.1996 as of 23:01 GMT.

News.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK
News.content:
A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

It is not clear when the flight will take place.

Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.

Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen.

Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths.

There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated.

"Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low."

There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa.

It has since become the deadliest in the country's history, with a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.

News.title: Police to escort fire crews in latest crackdown on Bonfire Night disorder
News.content:
Police officers are to be embedded in fire stations and will travel with crews to tackle potential attacks on firefighters during Bonfire Night.

The move is part of Scotland's biggest police operation since the visit of President Donald Trump last summer and a response to a "unique" combination of safety concerns.

As many as 1,700 officers could be deployed to deal with fireworks-related disorder, a European football match involving Celtic and potential protests in Glasgow.

Additional public order vehicles and drivers are being brought in from 18 English and Welsh police forces under mutual aid arrangements.

Emergency services have long recommended organised displays as the safest and often most impressive way of enjoying fireworks.

News.title: More asbestos found in Parliament, as MPs urged to get on with revamp
News.content:
More asbestos has been discovered in Parliament, the BBC has learnt, as MPs come under pressure to sign off on a major revamp of the crumbling home of UK democracy.

Known asbestos items in the Palace of Westminster and wider parliamentary estate, such as insulation, roofing, floor tiles and ropes, now number more than 1,650 - an increase of 500 since 2021.

It comes as the government considers holding a vote on refurbishing Parliament, which could cost up to Â£40bn and take 61 years, after years of indecision and delay.

The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for Parliament's restoration, with every additional year of delay costing taxpayers Â£420m.

More asbestos items were found during surveys in preparation for the long-awaited refurbishment project, parliamentary authorities said.

Asbestos has been identified as one of the main reasons for the refurbishment, given the dangers to human health when its fibres are airborne. While asbestos is largely fireproof, surrounding fire and heat can release fibres over long distances.

In the past five years, 700 items of asbestos have been removed from Parliament but the total has still risen, a Freedom of Information request by the BBC found.

Under Health and Safety Executive guidelines, most of it is classed as low risk in concealed areas, meaning it is less likely to be disturbed, but almost 200 items are classed as medium risk meaning they may require remedial works.

A spokesperson for UK Parliament said its "absolute priority is the safety of the those who work on and visit the parliamentary estate" with improved asbestos monitoring, new awareness training, and plans to further remove it.

Kris Gledhill, the son of former Labour MP Alice Mahon who died in 2022 of malignant mesothelioma - a type of cancer linked to asbestos exposure - told the BBC "asbestos should never be considered low risk".

News.title: Palestine Action ban undermined confidence in anti-terror laws, Supreme Court told
News.content:
The banning of Palestine Action has led to a "crisis in confidence" in the UK's anti-terrorism laws and triggered unprecedented civil disobedience from law-abiding protesters, the Supreme Court has been told.

Opening a major legal challenge to the group's proscription last year, lawyers for co-founder Huda Ammori said that no other protest organisation had been treated the same way.

They told the five justices that the UK's highest court had never before had to consider whether banning a group under terrorism legislation was compatible with freedom of speech and protest.

Twenty-seven protesters were arrested outside the Supreme Court on Wednesday as the hearing took place, the Metropolitan Police said.

Lawyers for Ammori told the court that thousands of elderly people, many veterans of other radical causes, had been arrested for holding up signs supportive of the group since its proscription.

Home Office figures seen by the BBC indicate that there have been more than 4,000 arrests so far at protests in which people have held up signs supportive of the group.

In practice, many demonstrators have been arrested more than once, with 1,200 charges authorised by prosecutors to date. Those trials are in limbo until the outcome of this case.

Henry Blaxland KC told the court that "far from depriving Palestine Action of the oxygen of publicity" and "far from discrediting its brand", proscription of the group has had the opposite effect.

"All it's done is to pour fuel on to a fire of one of the most publicly-contested issues of our time," he said.

"It was disproportionate to do that and in my submission completely unnecessary."

During often tense exchanges with the judges, Ammori's team accepted that Palestine Action could not be described as an ordinary and peaceful protest group.

They said that its members had carried out "direct action" protests by occupying or vandalising firms linked to Israel's military - with only three of 385 incidents assessed by the Home Secretary as constituting an offence under the Terrorism Act.

The UK's definition of terrorism includes incidents of serious damage to property for a cause - and at least two break-ins at defence firms have been described in criminal courts as having caused millions in damage.

Raza Husain KC, for Ammori, said that the judges had to put aside allegations of criminality - for which the state had many powers - and consider whether the Home Secretary's decision to label the group as terrorists had been disproportionate.

"Palestine Action was proscribed on the basis of less than one per cent of its actions over five years assessed as falling within the outer limits of a definition of terrorism," he said.

"The Home Secretary's own experts confirmed the vast majority of its direct action would not constitute an act of terrorism on the basis that any damage to property is typically more minor. Common tactics include graffiti, petty vandalism, occupation, and lock-ons."

One Palestine Action member has been convicted and jailed of fracturing a police officer's back with a sledgehammer - but the court was told that the group had never advocated such violence.

News.title: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
News.content:
Kellogg's has told the BBC the "snap, crackle and pop" sound made by its Rice Krispies may be noticeably quieter after an uproar over the cereal giant's recipe change.

Rice Krispies and Coco Pops are no longer being made with whole rice grains, with the tiny toasted puffs being made using corn flour and rice flour instead.

A Kellogg's spokesperson said retaining the iconic sound had been a "huge focus" when designing the new recipe, but that customers "might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before".

The firm was responding to complaints online that the taste of the breakfast staples had changed, with some fans adding they missed the "pop" sound.

Kellogg's said it had adapted the recipes due to "changing weather conditions" that have disrupted supplies of some grains and cereals.

The cereal giant said the new versions had been "carefully assessed for taste, appearance and texture", but some shoppers said their children would no longer eat them.

Some expressed dismay that the taste and texture were "totally different" and dubbed the change "grim" and "disgusting".

"There's no snap, crackle and pop in these," a parent named Dani wrote on TikTok. "My toddler won't eat them."

Lauren, also posting on TikTok, added that she had been eating Rice Krispies every day for breakfast "for years and years".

"I had a bowl of the new recipe and you can immediately tell the difference," she said. "They don't have the snapping sound when you put in the milk."

Jessicake meanwhile said they tasted "weird and stale".

The "Snap, Crackle and Pop" - made when milk is added to the puffed rice - has been a centrepiece of the brand's marketing since the 1950s.

Kellogg's insisted the snap, crackle and pop is "still there, but consumers might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before".

Recipe changes are notoriously difficult for big brands. Chocolate makers are constantly accused of reducing cocoa content in their products and debates rage online over whether ketchup ingredients have changed.

When Scottish fizzy drink Irn Bru cut its sugar content in 2018, fans famously stockpiled crates of the old version.

No changes are being made to Rice Krispies products in the US and Canada, which are owned by a separate company.

Kellogg's said the recipe change in the UK would help "maintain consistent quality" as extreme weather takes a toll on crops and pushes up ingredient prices.

Extreme weather in Spain in 2022 and 2023 in particular had reduced availability of the types of rice the company uses for its breakfast cereals, the company said.

Rice Krispies, launched nearly a century ago, are sold around the world and come in variations such as vanilla and strawberry flavours in some markets alongside the widespread chocolate-flavoured Coco Pops version.

"We appreciate that even small changes to a much-loved product can feel noticeable and that's why we have approached this with a lot of care and consideration," Kellogg's said.

The firm said it appreciated the customer feedback and would "continue to look at ways to make [its] products even better in the future".

The cereals have already undergone some change, with reductions in salt content in the 1990s and lowered sugar in 2018. The company said Rice Krispies and Coco Pops will continue to meet UK food standards on levels of fat, salt and sugar in food.

A backlash against processed foods in recent years, especially those low in fibre and high in sugar, has put breakfast cereals generally under the spotlight from healthy eating advocates.

Kellogg's stressed the cereals contain no artificial colours, flavours or sweeteners and the nutritional benefits in each bowl, such as fibre, Vitamin D and iron are staying the same.

However, the new recipes mean packaging will now include a "contains wheat gluten" warning. It also continues to contain barley-malt extract.

News.title: Passengers thought mass train attack 'was a joke'
News.content:
Some train passengers initially remained sitting down and thought a man was joking after he told people "I've been stabbed, run", a court has heard.

Anthony Williams stabbed 10 people on the train which made an unscheduled stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November last year.

Cambridge Crown Court heard the first person who was stabbed, Jonathan Gjoshe, later asked hospital staff "am I going to die today?".

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 10 counts of attempted murder, and four other alleged attempted murders in earlier incidents in Peterborough and London.

A second stabbing victim said Williams ran away when his pet cockapoo fought back, and another said he threw luggage at the attacker to fend him off.

Jurors have seen CCTV footage of Williams' attack, which took place on the York to London King's Cross LNER service, after it had left Peterborough.

The court was played a video interview with Gjoshe, who said he was on his phone in carriage J at the time and initially thought Williams was someone he knew.

"I've made eye contact with himâ¦ he's pulled a knife, but I just think it was the way he's poked me, the way he's stabbed me, it was a bit weird because it was slow."

Gjoshe said that once he felt a shock "that's when the adrenalin kicked in" and he jumped over the train table.

He said his whole arm was "drenched with blood" and went through the carriage telling people "I've been stabbed, run", but said some other people on the train remained "sitting down, thinking it was a joke".

"It was like a movie, it was quite horrific."

He spent four days in hospital and asked staff "am I going to die today or not? please tell me this".

News.title: £200m taxpayer-funded trains sit barely used for three years
News.content:
A new fleet of publicly funded trains that cost more than Â£200m still remain mostly unused more than three years after the first one was delivered.

They were initially promised to be fully up and running by 2022 but Transport for Wales' boss has said it might not be until the end of 2027 when their tram-trains will be in full service.

Data obtained by the BBC reveals that less than half of the 36 fleet - what TfW call the "final piece" in their Â£2bn South Wales Metro project - have passed rigorous statutory testing.

TfW chief executive James Price said he wants trains that work "100% well, 100% of the time" before putting them into full service.

News.title: Fourth arrest after Halloween party stabbings
News.content:
A fourth boy has been arrested after five teenagers were stabbed at a Halloween party in Hampshire.

Police were called shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday to a home in Park Road in Chandler's Ford where an "unknown group" had gained entry to the event over a garden fence.

One boy, 17, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition. The other four boys, who all suffered serious injuries, have since been discharged.

A 16-year-old from Southampton has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. Police have been given an extra 36 hours to question a 16 and 17-year-old, also from the city, who were held on Monday morning on suspicion of the same offence.

A 16-year-old boy from Bristol remains in custody having been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder on Monday night.

Two witnesses told the BBC a fight started after a group came in over a garden fence, although they said the motive for the stabbings was unclear.

One of the teenagers said: "I was [standing] in the hallway near the exit and I saw someone I know pull up their shirt and say 'I've been stabbed'.

"And then I later saw him lying outside the front of the house with someone compressing his wound."

The other witness said: "A big group of people started shouting and then a fight broke out and then we just heard the dad tell everyone to leave.

"And that was when we saw someone injured on the floor."

Police cordoned off parts of Park Road and the adjoining Valley Road.

The five boys who were stabbed had been invited to attend the supervised party.

News.title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales
News.content:
The number of deaths from cocaine use in England and Wales has nearly quadrupled in a decade, overtaking those attributed to heroin for the first time.

Cocaine was linked to more than one in five drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025, more than any other single substance, with charities blaming its increased purity and availability.

Meanwhile a record 115 ketamine-linked deaths were registered, almost twice as many as in 2024, according to Office for National Statistics data, external.

The overall rate of drug deaths fell for the first time since 2012. But experts pointed out regional inequality was growing, with the rate of such deaths more than twice as high in the North East as in London.

There were 5,519 drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025 in England and Wales, the equivalent of 92.4 deaths per million people.

Of these, cocaine was mentioned in 1,233 cases - slightly fewer than the previous year but higher than the 1,210 deaths linked to heroin or morphine, which also marked a fall from the previous year's level.

However, deaths linked to opiate and opioid drugs combined were still higher. The ONS also said there was a lag between deaths occurring and being registered.

The fatality rate fell from 93.9 deaths per million people a year earlier, representing the first annual decline since 2012.

In September, National Records of Scotland said drug deaths there had risen by 11% in 2025 on the year before, marking the worst mortality rate in Europe,

In May the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency said drug-related deaths rose by 7.1% between 2021-23 and 2022-24, external.
