News.title: Hannity unloads on first show after midterms massacre — gives Iran war full-throated support and calls Abdul El-Sayed ‘crazy’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fox News’ Sean Hannity went off during his first show after a midterm election massacre of Republicans, giving the unpopular Iran war his full-throated support and calling Senate-elect Abdul El-Sayed “crazy.”

In what is being dubbed a “blue tsunami,” Democrats picked up key Senate seats in reliably red states, helping them take control of the next Congress — and they even made some historic wins in governors’ races.

“We’ll just call you crazy, because you are,” Hannity said on his primetime show Wednesday in a retort to El-Sayed’s taunting of the Trump administration.

When El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat from Michigan, became the first Muslim to be elected to the Senate Tuesday, he told President Donald Trump in his victory speech, “I know you struggle with my name, so after [Vice President] JD [Vance] swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator.”

Hannity said, without mentioning the blatant attacks Trump threw at El-Sayed while campaigning for his Republican opponent Mike Rogers, raged, “Now, forget the old niceties: ‘Oh, let’s just work together for the people in my state, for the good of the country’ — no. Those days are gone.”

open image in gallery Fox News’ Sean Hannity has unloaded during his first show after a midterm election massacre of Republicans, giving the unpopular Iran war his full-throated support and calling Senate-elect Abdul El-Sayed 'crazy' ( Getty Images )

During a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, late last month, Trump demanded that El-Sayed go through metal detectors at the U.S. Capitol building if he were to get elected.

“I’m here to keep a Jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator,” Trump said, adding that El-Sayed “would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate.”

El-Sayed has vehemently denied any ties to the Islamist organization known as the Muslim Brotherhood.

After insulting El-Sayed, Hannity backed Trump’s war against Iran, which has been credited with playing a major role in Republicans’ crushing defeat after the conflict sent gas prices soaring.

“The Iran war — yes, I absolutely stand by. It was the right call to prevent the Iranians, the radical No. 1 state sponsor of terror, from getting nuclear weapons,” Hannity said.

open image in gallery When El-Sayed, a progressive Democrat from Michigan, became the first Muslim to be elected to the Senate Tuesday, he told President Donald Trump in his victory speech, 'I know you struggle with my name, so after [Vice President] JD [Vance] swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator' ( Getty Images )

But Hannity did admit that the eight-month-long war has caused a headache for Americans at the pump.

“Unfortunately, after that decision was made, there was some indecisiveness, and it prevented a quick-lasting outcome, and as a result, Americans did suffer by paying higher energy prices,” the Fox News host continued. “Democrats drove a truck through that. Americans are mad. It’s time now to fix that problem.”

Hannity made clear he is going to extremes, like leaving the country now that the Democrats have the majority in Congress.

“I’ve made my choice. I’m not going to back down. I’m not going to Ireland [a jab at Trump enemy Rosie O'Donnell] because of one election-year loss. These things sadly are cyclical; it is predictable,” he said. “And Donald Trump, he’s still the president, and the radicals in D.C. have the most powerful check-and-balance that they’re going to have to deal with day in and day out.”

"My message tonight is 'All hands on deck, stay away from circular firing squads, finger-pointing, blame, allow Democrats to show their true colors as they are now doing, have real answers on the other side,” Hannity added.

open image in gallery Hannity said the Iran war ‘was the right call,’ despite it being credited with playing a major role in Republicans’ crushing defeat after the conflict sent gas prices soaring ( Getty Images )

Trump, who spent all of last month hosting near-daily rallies to drum up support from his base and tell his supporters to pretend he was on the ballot, has done everything but blame himself for the GOP shellacking.

In his first public appearance since the midterm losses, Trump stood where his multi-million-dollar White House ballroom is being built and talked construction.

“This is the safest place in Washington,” Trump said as he discussed one of his unwelcome pet projects. “It’s good for me. It’s relaxing.”

Trump suggested in a phone call to Fox News as the election results rolled in that he is willing to work with Democrats where he could, but would remain uncompromising on immigration and transgender policies.

“The power of veto is one of the stronger powers that a president has, and they'll send over things that are insane, and I'll veto them,” he said.

News.title: Zelensky has awarded Melania Trump one of Ukraine’s highest honours. Here’s why
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has awarded US First Lady Melania Trump a state honour.

The presidential decree, dated November 2, cited her "significant personal contribution" to humanitarian support for Ukraine and her work to help Ukrainian children, including those deported or forcibly moved from Russian-occupied territory.

The Order of Princess Olga, 1st class honours women who have made exceptional contributions in spheres including science, education, culture and charitable work.

Ukrainian officials said Melania Trump played a pivotal role in securing a six-day ceasefire to evacuate civilians from the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky, which began on Tuesday and concluded on Sunday.

It marked the longest local pause in fighting since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Previous attempts to pause the fighting have either failed to take hold or quickly unravelled.

Residents evacuated from the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky during a humanitarian mission ( AFP/Getty )

Nearly 800 people were evacuated during the ceasefire, Melania Trump said.

The plight of the city in Ukraine's Kherson region caught the attention of the US first lady, and the White House said she brokered the humanitarian mission.

“The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a frontline war city on the brink of disaster,” she said at the time of the deal.

“Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water.”

Pope Leo XIV also spoke this month with Zelensky and Vladimir Putin, urging them to allow humanitarian aid into Oleshky and the safe evacuation of civilians, the Vatican said.

Zelensky previously said he was grateful to Melania Trump for her role in halting the fighting in and around Oleshky.

“We are grateful that they are organising this possibility to evacuate people,” he said.

Russia’s ombudsperson Yana Lantratova said: “Her personal involvement is of great importance to the entire process.”

Both sides are eager to win US President Donald Trump’s approval as he pushes for an elusive peace settlement.

On Thursday, Melania Trump will ​host ​representatives of Russia ⁠and ​Ukraine at ​the White House in an “extraordinary moment in American history”.

“This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American first lady,” the White House said.

News.title: Bank of England set to hike interest rates to 4% to tackle rising inflation
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Bank of England is poised to hike interest rates for the first time in more than three years, economists think.

Rate-setters are widely expected to tighten monetary policy in a bid to tackle rising inflation in the UK economy.

Traders in the financial markets are predicting that rates will increase to 4% from 3.75% when the Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announces its next decision on Thursday.

This would be the first time that the central bank increases borrowing costs since August 2023, and means that mortgage holders could be facing a squeeze.

Pressure on the MPC to take action has grown since official figures showed the rate of Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation rose to 3.5% in September, the highest level in 11 months.

open image in gallery

The conflict in the Middle East has helped push CPI further away from the Bank’s 2% target rate, with a surge in petrol and diesel prices a major driving force.

And inflation is expected to be pushed higher this winter after Ofgem’s energy price cap rose by 3.6% for a typical household on October 1 and is forecast to jump by a further 22% in January.

Ellie Henderson, an analyst for Investec, said: “We imagine that many committee members’ patience with the recent rise in inflation has worn thin.

“The longer energy prices remain elevated, the greater the risk that a temporary price shock becomes more permanent; a ‘risk management’ hike could guard against this.”

open image in gallery

She cautioned that producers might “not be willing or able to shoulder the burden of higher energy prices for much longer” and that this could push up prices in shops.

Alexander Harvey, UK economist for Oxford Economics, said a November rate hike looks to be a “done deal” for the committee, which will be responding to higher oil and gas prices.

“So far, two factors have been central to the MPC’s decision-making since the outbreak of the conflict in the Middle East: the scale and duration of the energy price shock, plus the extent of any second-round inflation effects from elevated energy prices,” he said.

“These factors will continue to dominate the outlook for Bank rate.”

He said the key thing economists will be looking out for is any signal from the Bank as to where interest rates could go from here, with the financial markets expecting further hikes into 2027.

Other central banks have already increased their interest rates, including the US Federal Reserve which did so last month for the first time in three years.

The MPC will also take into account other economic indicators including that the UK’s unemployment rate fell to the lowest level in more than a year in the three months to August, to 4.7%.

Furthermore, the economy unexpectedly grew in August, by 0.1%, suggesting resilience in the UK despite pressure on consumer spending and wider volatility because of the Iran war.

News.title: 1 deputy dies and another not expected to survive after firefight with suspect at Washington home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

One of two sheriff's deputies wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Washington state has died, and the other is not expected to survive, authorities said Wednesday.

Deputies responded to a home in Spangle, a small farming community south of Spokane, on Tuesday afternoon after a woman told her neighbor that she had been shot by her brother, the Spokane County Sheriff's Office said.

They determined the suspect had a felony warrant and that there might be other victims, and SWAT team members and deputies tried to breach the door.

Gunfire erupted from the home, and the two deputies were struck. They were taken to a hospital in critical condition. One died that night, and the other was being kept on life support Wednesday, allowing for the donation of his organs, the sheriff's office said in a written statement.

“He will continue to serve others with the gift of life,” the statement said.

Neither was identified, but Sheriff John Nowels described them as younger members of the SWAT team. The deputy who died had a wife and two children.

“Although we know our Deputies knew the risks, they bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know,” the sheriff's office said. “They did this with honor and with an unwavering sense of duty."

Other deputies returned fire and found the suspect dead inside, along with one other victim in the house and one in the yard, authorities said.

The names of the victims and the suspect have not been released.

Authorities are investigating the shooting and what may have led to it.

The woman who reported being shot by her brother was hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries.

News.title: Lone Texas Republican Ted Cruz unleashes over GOP 'blue tsunami' midterm loss
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Texas Senator Ted Cruz delivered a scathing assessment of his party’s sweeping defeats following major Democratic victories across the United States, describing the losses as a "blue tsunami" after Republicans were ousted from nearly every major office across his home state.

He pointed to elevated gas prices, a rise in home and automobile repossessions, alongside record numbers of weekly plasma donations, as clear indicators that citizens across the country were struggling financially.

"That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care," Cruz added.

Cruz launched into the economic crisis many Americans are facing on a daily basis.

"2026 was not simply a blue wave. It was a blue tsunami. It was an a-- kicking," Cruz said on an episode of his podcast, Verdict with Ted Cruz, released Wednesday. "It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation."

His commentary came as Democrats ended more than three decades of Republican rule in a state long considered out of reach for the party.

James Talarico claimed a U.S. Senate seat against scandal-plagued Republican nominee Ken Paxton, while Gina Hinojosa ousted three-term Governor Greg Abbott. Meanwhile, Democrat Vikki Goodwin defeated Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick, and Democrat Nathan Johnson won the attorney general’s race.

Democrats in Texas also won statewide seats overseeing land, agriculture, and energy regulation, along with judicial offices, while successfully flipping control of the state’s House of Representatives.

"Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas," Cruz said. "We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people’s lives and we need to deal with the consequences."

Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz says he would rather be killed by 'American killer robots' than Chinese ones ( Politico )

The election results represented a dramatic reversal in a state that President Donald Trump won by approximately 14 percentage points in 2024, where Republicans had held every statewide position since 1994.

The shift formed part of a widespread nationwide surge for Democrats, signaling a broad rejection of MAGA and a rebuke of policies under Trump, including tariffs and the war in Iran, which voters blame for driving up cost-of-living expenses.

"Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high," Cruz said. "Too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care."

The 55-year-old senator has represented Texas in the US Senate since 2013 and is not scheduled for reelection until 2030.

A former state solicitor general and longtime Trump ally, Cruz previously survived two high-profile Democratic challenges that generated hopes of a Democratic realignment in Texas. He defeated Beto O’Rourke by nearly 3 points in 2018 before defeating Colin Allred in 2024 by over 8 points, despite polling indicating a tight race.

"I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas," Cruz said. "That’s not something I ever thought I would say."

News.title: Flood of migrants already heading to southern border, MAGA faithful claims in doomsaying push
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

MAGA faithful Steve Bannon has claimed that a flood of migrants is already heading to the southern border after Democrats saw massive wins in Texas’ midterm elections.

Bannon and his podcast guest Todd Bensman have begun doomsaying less than 24 hours after Democrat James Talarico flipped a Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa was elected the first-ever Latina governor in the ruby red state.

“They’ve already got caravans coming up. They’re all excited down in Central America that the gates are opening again,” Bannon told Bensman, an immigration expert at a conservative think tank called The Heritage Foundation, on his War Room show Wednesday.

When contacted by The Independent for evidence to back up his claims, Bannon cited several news articles about caravans of Hondurans traveling north in anticipation of the midterms.

Dozens of people left Honduras Tuesday to head to the U.S. in hopes that the midterms would weaken Trump’s immigration crackdown, The Tico Times, a Costa Rica-based English-language newspaper, reported.

open image in gallery Steve Bannon and his podcast guest Todd Bensman have begun doomsdaying less than 24 hours after Democrat James Talarico flipped a Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa was elected the first-ever Latina governor in the ruby red state ( Getty Images )

“Trump is on his way out in these elections. That’s why we’re taking the risk. Here in Honduras, we have nothing left,” Jimena Morazán, a 47-year-old traveling with five relatives, said in the article.

The Latin Times said Tuesday’s caravan was the third significant organized movement of Hondurans to leave out of San Pedro Sula since early fall.

“The border is quiet, but it’s not dead. There are still lots of runners coming across,” Bensman warned. But President Donald Trump has said himself that the border is secure under his presidency, which lasts another two years.

The U.S. Customs and Border Protection has reported nearly 140,000 encounters in the 2026 fiscal year. But the agency has also celebrated 16 consecutive months of zero releases at the border, meaning that migrants are not passing into the U.S.

Hinojosa and Talarico have both pledged to secure the border, but have also spoken out against aggressive tactics used to curb immigration under Trump and current Republican Governor Greg Abbott.

open image in gallery 'They’ve already got caravans coming up. They’re all excited down in Central America that the gates are opening again,' Bannon said Wednesday ( Getty Images )

“As governor, I will never offer up Texas as a staging ground for operations that terrorize families and enrich [Abbott’s] donors,” Hinojosa said in a January press release.

Talarico has suggested on his campaign website that “Our border should be like a front porch — it should have a welcome mat out front and a lock on the door.”

“We should be cracking down on the cartels, not our communities. We should be deporting gang members, not small business owners. We should be hunting down human traffickers, not moms and babies,” he said.

Bannon also used a “welcome mat” metaphor for immigration — but as a dig at Democrats like Talarico.

“The invaders know when Democrats take control, the welcome mat is out,” he told The Independent.

The Independent has reached out to the Department of Homeland Security for comment.

open image in gallery Hinojosa and Talarico have both pledged to secure the border, but have also spoken out against aggressive tactics used to curb immigration under Trump and current Republican Governor Greg Abbott ( Getty Images )

Bensman had suggested Trump use the National Guard to keep the border secure if Democrats in Texas, where about half of the southern border is located, fail to do so.

“There are about 4,000 Texas National Guard down there. They’ll probably all be pulled, maybe the Trump administration will have to nationalize them…or just replace them with regular Army, who provide another very important duty of arresting, tracking groups and providing backup to the Border Patrol,” Bensman said.

Trump has used the National Guard during protests against his immigration agenda in Los Angeles and to crack down on already declining crime in Washington, D.C., earlier in his second term — and it was met with fierce backlash.

“I think that they should be able to hold the line for a couple of years, but after Trump leaves…if there’s a Democrat in the White House, probably, it’s all gonna be on again,” he added.

News.title: Water infrastructure shifts into the conflict zone crosshairs, says Unicef report
News.content:
Water infrastructure is coming increasingly under attack in conflict zones, leading to disease outbreaks and forcing civilians to make dangerous journeys to fill buckets, according to a new report.

Water Under Fire, published by United Nations children’s agency Unicef, found that attacks have become “more frequent, varied and geographically widespread”.

It said the number of attacks that damaged or destroyed water systems tripled between 2021 and 2025.

Recorded incidents, ranging from strikes on water plants to restrictions on access to water treatment chemicals, rose from less than 45 in eight countries in 2021 to more than 135 in 15 nations by 2025, according to data from Insecurity Insight, a Geneva-based humanitarian organisation that tracks threats facing people in conflict.

Maia Giorgio, humanitarian policy specialist at Unicef, stressed that the report only covers documented attacks, warning that it may be “just the tip of the iceberg”.

“It’s a global phenomenon, and unfortunately, it’s under-documented,” she said.

“Without water, you don’t have a functioning healthcare system. Without water, you can’t prevent infectious disease, and we know that children are particularly vulnerable,” she added.

News.title: Man City have a striker who will not be stopped and a defence that cannot be trusted
News.content:
“You can look at it that it’s difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it’s only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance – you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option,” Haaland added.

This was a victory to bounce back from losing in the Premier League at the weekend, but the question will be how can City mount a title challenge with such a brittle defence. Champions League winners do not leave themselves open at the back like this, and City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet.

Maresca insisted last week that his starting line-up is Donnarumma plus 10 others, but the reality is that Haaland is the guaranteed name on the team sheet. And his goalkeeper’s errors are becoming a problem.

This one added to the goals against Aston Villa and Paris St-Germain that were also on his watch. He could have claimed the cross that led to Brighton’s winner at the weekend too.

Here he went from hero to villain in the space of a few minutes at the start of the second half. Firstly, from kick-off Christoph Baumgartner got close with his angled drive heading towards the top corner until Donnarumma’s fingertips turned the ball around the post. It was a save that had the Italian celebrating like he had scored a goal.

But he had his head in his hands after Leipzig’s next move. Nico O’Reilly could have done better after losing the ball in midfield, then failing to track the overlapping run from Baku. With Red Bull Arena waiting for a cross, Baku had spotted Donnarumma slightly out of position and beat him at the near post. It was superb improvisation, but without doubt a goalkeeping error.

News.title: Gyokeres the creator and executioner to see nervous Arsenal past Slavia Prague
News.content:
“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”

Those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

“We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

The goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

News.title: Liverpool calamity hands Iraola his most chastening night yet
News.content:
Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

News.title: Oil prices plunge after Republicans suffer midterms defeat
News.content:
Oil prices fell sharply after JD Vance blamed the Republicans’ election rout on the Iran war.

The price of a barrel of Brent, the global benchmark, fell as much as 10pc to $93 a barrel by Wednesday evening, while WTI was down more than 8pc to $88.

It marks the first time since Oct 7 that Brent has fallen below $100 a barrel.

The decline came after the vice president said that voters had abandoned the party owing to dissatisfaction with Donald Trump’s war in the Middle East.

This has boosted traders’ hopes that the US President could seek to de-escalate his conflict in the Gulf, which would increase global oil supplies.

Posting on social media, Mr Vance said: “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

Mr Trump later admitted Mr Vance’s comments were “largely true”.

He said he expected oil prices to “go up a lot more” than they did because of the war, reaffirming that “Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon.”

“If I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again, because long term, it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.

“I thought the oil would go up a lot more, and I did it on that basis.

“You have no choice. You have to do it. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon, or everything that you see here someday might not exist.”

Traders also responded to the prospect that the Democrats could restrict Mr Trump’s funding for the war.

Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at Rystad Energy, said the President is now likely to come under “greater institutional pressure” to strike a peace deal with Iran.

This will ease pressure on economies around the world after oil prices have risen by roughly 70pc since the war broke out in February.

The Republican rout also prompted Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX to lose nearly $159bn (£118bn) in market value when trading opened in New York amid fears the Democrats’ success will derail the AI boom.

The carmaker and rocket company both fell 5.8pc as Wall Street opened after the Democrats swept to victory although they pared losses later.

Mr Musk, the billionaire boss of both companies, was the leading donor to the Republicans during the election campaign as he hoped for light-touch regulation of his AI ambitions.

However, analysts said the Democrat victory would slow down the pace of the rapid build-out of data centres.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for Texas Governor and is expected to oppose the rapid build-out of AI.

A sharp decline in the value of data-centre developers Tesla and SpaceX, both based in Texas, would wipe billions off Mr Musk’s nearly $900bn fortune. He spent $446m on backing failed Republican candidates.

As the Democrat victory emerged, Mr Musk wrote on X: “Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

He later wrote: “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time.”

News.title: Ebola risk to UK remains ‘low’ despite evacuation of infected Briton
News.content:
Authorities have insisted that the risk to the UK is low after it emerged that a UK humanitarian worker infected with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Britain for treatment.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said it would not disclose the identity of the worker but confirmed a British citizen currently in the DRC has tested positive for the viral haemorrhagic fever.

“The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated. Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low,” the FCDO said in a statement.

The patient is due to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday, according to Reuters, and will be transferred to one of the UK’s high-consequence infectious disease units based at the Royal Free Hospital in London and the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle.

The worker had been responding to the outbreak currently raging in the Ituri region of DRC. The first cases of the Bundibugyo strain of the disease were first reported in May and there have now been more than 10,000 cases and 5,000 deaths.

It is the second largest outbreak in history and is taking place in a region racked with conflict and where mistrust of authorities is widespread.

Several aid agencies are working in the area including Médecins Sans Frontières, Oxfam and Unicef.

There are no specific treatments or vaccines for the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus and the backbone of treatment is supportive care. In July the World Health Organization launched the Partners trial in DRC to test whether the monoclonal antibody MBP134, the antiviral remdesivir, or a combination of both can improve survival. Another monoclonal antibody will soon be added to the study.

Researchers are also testing multiple vaccines, two of which were developed specifically for Bundibugyo. These are ChAdOx1, developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469.

News.title: Budget cuts and ministerial churn has weakened aid spending transparency, report finds
News.content:
The UK has become less transparent in how it spends its aid budget, amid repeated cuts and ministerial turnover, according to a new report.

The 2026 Aid Transparency Index, the world’s only independent peer-reviewed assessment on aid transparency evaluates how well major donors, development banks, and UN agencies disclose their spending and activity data. In the latest ranking the UK’s transparency score fell 13.9 points from “very good” to “good”.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) lost points for its lack of “comprehensive forward-looking country and organisational budgets and strategies, and project objectives”.

Twenty of the 33 ranked international organisations, over 60 per cent, scored “good” or “very good”, with just three rated “poor” or “very poor”. Germany, the US and the UK gave over 40 per cent of all overseas development aid in 2025, yet all three saw their transparency scores fall, according to the index.

“It’s not like [the FCDO] made a conscious decision to do anything badly or to miss anything… Our gut feeling is they’ve just taken their eye off the ball,” said Gary Forster, CEO of Publish What You Fund, a global campaign for aid and development transparency, which published the index.

“The FCDO hasn’t had a meaningful strategy since 2023,” he told The Telegraph.

For over two decades, the Department for International Development (DFID) operated as its own cabinet level ministry after it was set up in 1997 by Tony Blair, then Labour prime minister. In 2020, Conservative prime minister Boris Johnson merged it with the Foreign Office to create the FCDO.

The responsibility for aid was downgraded from a secretary of state to a minister of state position. Even then, there has been rapid ministerial turnover, with four international development ministers in the past two years.

The UK’s development budget, which funds programmes to tackle poverty and is a lifeline to millions around the world, has been repeatedly cut in recent years.

The UK historically prided itself on committing to spend 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on Official Development Assistance (ODA). In 2020 that figure was cut to 0.5 per cent and last year, Sir Keir Starmer, former prime minister, cut the target to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

News.title: Emery endures heaviest European defeat as Villa manager to old foes Barcelona
News.content:
“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which showed it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”

Sports.title: Wolves hit back to beat Bristol City after late Neave double
Sports.content:
Substitute Sean Neave scored a late brace as Wolves came from behind to secure a 2-1 Sky Bet Championship win over Bristol City at Ashton Gate.

The hosts took a 34th-minute lead when Scott Twine was fouled 25 yards out and got up to fire in an unstoppable right-footed free-kick, sending the ball curling away from Jose Sa's dive and into the top corner.

But Wolves piled on the second-half pressure and were rewarded after 82 minutes when Kieran Trippier volleyed in a cross from the right, Adam Armstrong's first-time shot was saved and Neave pounced to net the rebound.

Six minutes later Neave was on target again, nodding home from close range after Ladislav Krejci had headed a Trippier free-kick across goal.

Wolves were deserved winners and move up to second in the table, but the result was cruel on the Robins, who defended with great tenacity.

City boss Michael Skubala made two changes from the team that won 3-2 at Bolton, promoting striker Sam Bell and midfielder Twine from the bench, while Wolves brought in Jean-Ricner Bellegarde for the injured Jordan James.

Until Twine's spectacular strike, the only fireworks had come from a display before kick-off.

Wolves looked the more dangerous side in the opening half-hour but had only an Armstrong shot, comfortably saved by Brad Collins, to show for their efforts.

Lorent Tolaj headed wide for City from a 29th-minute cross by Rio Cardines, but his side were equally goal-shy at the end of some promising attacks.

Skubala's men were clearly boosted by the goal and were quicker into the challenge for the remainder of the half without creating clear openings.

Wolves began the second period attacking the end where their travelling fans were massed and looked certain to equalise in the 57th minute.

Rodrigo Gomes, only just introduced as a substitute for Marshall Munetsi, who had needed treatment for a head injury just before the break, broke clear down the middle only to delay his shot and be denied by a brilliant recovery tackle from Cam Pring.

Collins spilled a low shot from Rafiki Said after 61 minutes, recovering to smother the rebound effort from Armstrong.

Wanderers fashioned another good chance four minutes later when Bellegarde rose to meet a Trippier corner and saw his downward header parried by the diving Collins.

City were dangerous on the break and Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto made a triple change in the 73rd minute, sending on Mateus Mane, Neave and Tommy Doyle for Said, Fer Lopez and Bellegarde.

It made the difference. City had late efforts from Dom Ballard and Tolaj, but Neave's opportunistic double settled the outcome.

The managers

Bristol City's Michael Skubala:

"We fell to a sucker punch. When you get to 80 minutes ahead against a very good side you have to take something from the game.

"As a group, we have to defend better. The goals were soft from our perspective and we could have been stronger to prevent the second in particular.

"But there were also occasions when we made poor decisions in the opposition half and were loose in our possession of the ball.

"Cam Pring made a great recovery tackle to help defend our lead, but the chance came from us giving the ball away and we have to be better in that respect.

"There were positives, but in the end we didn't get the job done and we need to take the learnings from why it didn't happen.

"Now have another home game against Norwich on Saturday. It would be lying to say our home form is not a concern and we need to bounce back."

Wolves' Cesar Peixoto:

"The team showed character and soul to win that game. They kept on believing right to the end and so did our supporters, who stayed behind us at a goal down, which was very important.

"We got what we deserved in the end. We created a lot of chances from wide areas in the first half without getting on the end of them often enough.

"They scored from their only shot after we had dominated possession, but we did not move the ball quickly enough and we talked about that at half-time.

"In the second half the players reacted to what we asked of them and everything was done quicker. The fans played their part and the result is for them too.

"Sean Neave is a young guy making his first steps in professional football and those goals will do him a lot of good. He has a lot of ability, but is humble and plays for the team.

"It was a tough game because we had to push right to the very end. Now we will have to look after the players and help them recover for the next game, which comes very quickly."

Sports.title: 'Sloppy' Arsenal survive second-half scare to beat Slavia Prague
Sports.content:
Arsenal survived a second-half fightback from Slavia Prague to win 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena and continue their unbeaten start to the season in the Champions League.

The Gunners, runners-up last term, appeared on course for an emphatic victory after scoring twice through Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres in a one-sided first half.

But Slavia roared back into the contest in the second period and gave Arsenal a scare as Wiktor Nowak's late goal from close range set up a nervous finale for Mikel Arteta's side.

Arsenal hung on to claim their third win in four Champions League games but needed a goal-line clearance from Gabriel Magalhaes and several saves from David Raya, who brilliantly pushed an Oskar Kubiak header against the post shortly before Slavia's goal.

Image: Noni Madueke celebrates putting Arsenal in front at Slavia Prague

Slavia had 17 shots in the second half, having only had one before the break as Arsenal were made to work for a result which looked a foregone conclusion after their dominant start.

Arteta freshened up his side with six changes from Sunday's 1-0 win over Liverpool and Arsenal scored their early opener when Madueke finished coolly having been put through on goal by Gyokeres.

The striker added the second with a sumptuous, curling finish after combining with Mikel Merino but Arsenal missed chances to extend their lead before the break and Slavia responded.

A switch from a back four to a back three allowed the hosts to commit more bodies forward and they tested Arsenal's resolve with a succession of chances. Raya's goal was eventually breached but the win sees the Gunners move up to third in the league phase table.

Saliba back in squad William Saliba returned to Arsenal's squad for the first time this season as an unused substitute following his back injury.

Analysis: Gyokeres finding form

Gyokeres didn't score a single goal in his first 10 appearances of the season for Arsenal but his brilliantly taken effort against Slavia Prague makes it two in his last three following his goal in the Carabao Cup tie against Fleetwood Town last week.

He will need to do it against stronger opposition if he is to prove he should usurp Kai Havertz as Arteta's first-choice No 9. But this was an encouraging display which suggests the Sweden international might be turning a corner after a tough start to the campaign.

Image: Viktor Gyokeres celebrates his goal with his team-mates

His goal, immaculately dispatched into the far corner from the left-hand side of the box, will be his biggest source of satisfaction. But there were signs of improvement in his all-round game too.

Gyokeres created the opener with a smart pass around the corner for Madueke and had plenty of other bright moments with his back to goal, linking the play tidily, bringing others to play, and ultimately making an invaluable contribution to a hard-fought victory.

Arteta: Our second half was very sloppy

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's narrow victory against Slavia Prague, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta says his side's performance was far from their 'normal standard'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports:

"Obviously we need to value that winning away in the Champions League is extremely difficult. We knew that - and we knew the players and the opponent that we had in front of us.

"Two very different halves, the first one we played a really high level - exceptional at times, I would say. The scoreline should have reflected three or four goals. We didn't do it.

"And at half-time, I told them that they [Slavia] are a team with huge spirit, they will keep running and keep believing. They will become more chaotic. We didn't control that at all, right from the beginning.

"We were on the back foot, very sloppy, we gave so many balls away, so many bad clearances. We didn't keep the ball in our structure at all. And then you have to suffer because teams in the Champions League are really good. A lot to learn."

Raya: Delighted with win but we can improve

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya to TNT Sports:

"First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals.

"The second half was a completely different half. From them, they went up a gear.

"We were a little bit surprised and they made it really difficult for us - which we have to learn from.

"We know how important away games are and how difficult places like this can be. They became man-to-man all over the pitch.

"Delighted with the win, but we've got things to improve going forwards."

Arsenal have most wins in Europe

Arsenal have won 13 matches in all competitions this season, the joint most of any side in Europe's big-five leagues along with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Nine of Noni Madueke's last 10 goals for Arsenal in all competitions have been scored away from home.

Viktor Gyokeres has been involved in 16 goals in 25 Champions League appearances (12 goals, four assists).

Slavia Prague had 17 shots in the second half of the match - the joint-most in a single half against Mikel Arteta's Arsenal in a Champions League game along with Sporting CP's 17 in the second half in November 2024.

Sports.title: Boro struggle without Lankshear as Wrexham beat Championship leaders
Sports.content:
Championship leaders Middlesbrough suffered only their second league defeat of the season as Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a much-needed 2-0 win.

George Thomason rifled Wrexham in front in the 71st minute and substitute Oli Rathbone sealed it with an 84th-minute header to give Wrexham only their fourth win of the season, coming after back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Sheffield United left the Red Dragons hovering just above the drop zone.

Boro arrived in Wales unbeaten in 11 league games, but with top scorer Will Lankshear out through injury they looked a far cry from the side who had scored 13 goals in their previous four matches.

Lankshear's return of 15 goals this season was as many as the entire Wrexham squad prior to kick-off, and his absence through injury told on the league leaders as they struggled to make much of an impression before the break.

Kyle Joseph's ambitious bicycle kick dribbled wide before Adilson Malanda failed to get enough power on a header from Sebastian Berhalter's free-kick - the first effort on target from either side 29 minutes in.

Callum Brittain then cut in from the right and beat two defenders, but having done the hard work he mis-hit a weak shot straight at Anthony Patterson.

Parkinson had said his Wrexham players needed to have an "honest self-assessment" after Friday's 1-0 loss to Sheffield United and responded with four changes, bringing in Thomason and Max Cleworth following injury, along with George Dobson and Ben Whiteman.

The response was clear. Although Wrexham took time to grow into the game, they ended the first half looking the more dangerous side.

Right after Brittain's chance for Boro, the lively Thomason dragged a low ball across goal but Lewis O'Brien could not stretch far enough to turn it in.

Cleworth then went close with a first-time strike from range which had Radek Vitek scrambling to push clear.

Wrexham thought they had scored less than 40 seconds into the second half, but O'Brien was narrowly offside when he tucked in the rebound after Vitek spilled a low strike from Kieffer Moore.

Parkinson's side looked full of energy as they harassed Boro into mistakes, prompting a triple change by Kim Hellberg, though it did little to help them.

Boro were gifted a chance in the 66th minute as Patterson's terrible clearance went straight to Amario Cozier-Duberry but he sliced a shot wide.

Five minutes later the league leaders trailed. Cleworth launched a long ball into the box and Malanda's clearance fell for Thomason to lash home from the edge of the box.

Jeremy Sarmiento then fired into the side-netting for Boro but this was not their night, and moments later Rathbone, who had replaced Thomason seven minutes earlier, settled it as he nodded in O'Brien's chipped cross at the back post.

The managers

Wrexham's Phil Parkinson:

"It was important we put that back in place tonight. I've got to stress that it hasn't been missing all season. We've had some really good performances.

"However, in that first half against Sheffield United we lacked everything we want to be as a team.

"Tonight we were very structured. The spaces were tight, so we could get up to the ball and take it off them. The amount of times we got up to the ball and came out in our duals is exactly how we want to play as a team."

Middlesbrough's Kim Hellberg:

"Every team would miss their top goalscorer. I think it's tough when the decision is made very late and you have planned for it. That doesn't help…

"You need to find ways. Today I think it would be difficult because we weren't sharp enough. Whoever would be on the pitch there were not so many opportunities.

"To be fair to Will, he's not often involved so much in the build-up. He's very good in the box and in pressing. We need to find ways, but I think every team struggles if they miss a player who has scored 13 goals in 13 games."

Sports.title: Humphries recovers from food poisoning to win Players Championship title
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries revealed he lost over a stone due to food poisoning but still stormed to his fourth Players Championship title of 2026 with an 8-4 victory over Niels Zonneveld as Dutch legend Raymond van Barneveld took a huge step towards world championship qualification.

Humphries has now prevailed in three of his four Players Championship appearances in Leicester this season, marking the perfect preparation for the upcoming Grand Slam of Darts admitted he was forced him to pull out of the European Championship last month and then struggling with huge weight loss and a lack of practice.

It was also a terrific day for Van Barneveld, who took a huge step towards world championship qualification with a run to his second ProTour quarter-final of 2026, while Gary Anderson moved him into the provisional Players Championship Finals field with a run to the last four.

"It was more about coming back and seeing what my energy levels are like because I've obviously been very ill for the last two weeks," admitted Humphries.

"I've had food poisoning and I've not really moved about a lot for three and a half weeks.

"I've lost a stone. Well I did when I went on the scales after eight or nine days. I weighed myself and I'd lost 15 pounds. Jesus, what the hell. I couldn't eat.

"I'd never miss a major if I could. I think that's the first one I've ever missed. I was devastated to miss the European Championship because I was on a good run after winning the Grand Prix.

"I didn't win the Swiss trophy but I played really good. So I thought to myself I feel like I'm a little bit back here and I can maybe go on and do something great this year and that's a backward step when you have to miss a tournament.

"I didn't practice for two weeks. I had a few throws the last four days. It re-evaluates that confidence again that makes you think you carried on from where you left off.

"To come here and win it takes you back a little bit. So obviously I know the game's there to win these things. But the way I've been the last few weeks it's an unexpected win for myself.

"I've had a good year. I still want to win another major. If it's not the Grand Slam or Players Championship, I want it to be the World Championship.

"I think that's the thing I really search for now. Put my name in the legacy of some of the greats that's ever been."

Sports.title: Haaland nets Man City winner to haunt RB Leipzig again
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland haunted RB Leipzig again to earn Manchester City a thrilling 3-2 victory in the Champions League.

Haaland netted 12 minutes from time, tapping in from Elliot Anderson's low cross, for his 13th goal in nine appearances against the Bundesliga side, his most against any opponent in his career, which returned City to winning ways after their defeat to Brighton on Saturday.

City made hard work of the tie in which they led twice, having been gifted a first-half opener when Castello Lukeba comically turned the ball into his own net after Leipzig had been on top with Christoph Baumgartner and Antonio Nusa going close.

Gianluigi Donnarumma made a top save to deny Baumgartner at the start of the second half but seconds later the Man City goalkeeper was caught out at his near post by Ridle Baku's smart finish, the right-back tucking the ball in from a tight angle when everyone expected him to cross low into the middle.

The tie burst into life from there with Haaland, a bystander in the first half with just three touches, denied with his first chance, before Enzo Fernandez gave City the lead again, arriving in the box to power a header home from Iliman Ndiaye's perfect cross.

But within three minutes, Leipzig were level once more as Nusa grabbed himself a deserved goal, firing low across Donnarumma into the bottom right corner from inside the box.

City were spurred into their best spell of the game after that, helped by the introduction of Jeremy Doku, as Anderson set up Haaland, who couldn't miss from close range.

Leipzig's David Raum and City's Rayan Cherki still rattled the woodwork at both ends in a frantic finale as the visitors held on to move up to seventh in the league phase table.

'Donnarumma unconvincing again'

Sky Sports' Lewis Jones:

"Manchester City may have escaped Leipzig with three points but Gianluigi Donnarumma is doing little to convince that he is the reliable last line of defence.

"Another night, another collection of uncomfortable moments for the Italian. He was directly culpable for Leipzig's opening goal, getting himself into a muddle when the situation demanded composure from a cross from the right. It was a strange goal to concede.

"And it was hardly an isolated wobble. His handling looked uncertain on several occasions, while his decision-making invited pressure rather than easing it. David Raum nearly punished another moment of indecision when his free-kick rattled the crossbar, with Donnarumma looking anything but convincing."

Haaland: We have to step up

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland:

"I think it is the most I have scored against a club. I have played so many times against them in the Champions League with City and Borussia Dortmund too. Leipzig is a good team so I am happy."

On Elliot Anderson: "He has had an amazing start to his City career and that is what you expect. You have to come straight in and perform. It is not easy to come in, you need to adapt and new players and a new coach, so he has been impressive. Respect."

On Man City performance: "Not sure how many touches I had today, not the most but what is the most important is that I managed to help the team to win. I think we need to step up a bit. When we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that."

Maresca: We need to be careful with transitions

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca:

"Tough game in some moments. We controlled quite well but some moments we struggled. Champions League, Germany away, it's tough so happy with the three points.

"They are well organised, they were aggressive and dangerous with the wingers. We needed to be careful on transition. Happy with the three points and now we recover and move on."

Sports.title: Djokovic out of ATP Finals race after shock Paris exit along with No 1 Zverev
Sports.content:
For just the second time in 20 seasons, Novak Djokovic has failed to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals after a shock defeat in the second round of the Rolex Paris Masters.

The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, started well against 25-year-old Australian Rinky Hijikata, the world No 83, but faded badly in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

With two places still available for the season-ending championship, Djokovic needed a run to the semi-finals in Paris to stay alive in his hopes, but his exit leaves the door open for the remaining contenders, including 12th-placed Taylor Fritz and 13th-placed Tommy Paul.

Hijikata told Sky Sports: "It took a lot. I was getting outplayed in the first set and had to hang tough.

"In the end I was glad I maintained my level and trusted myself in the big moments. I felt I had to take it to him and play aggressive."

'I deserve to be where I am' - Zverev suffers Musetti defeat

Alexander Zverev became the first male player in the history of tennis to lose in straight sets on his debut match as world No 1.

The 29-year-old German, who won the French and US Opens this year, was elevated to top spot in the ATP rankings for the first time on Monday.

However, he blew a 5-2 lead in a first-set tie-break on his way to a surprise 7-6 (7-5) 6-2 defeat by Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.

Speaking in his press conference, Zverev said: "To put it simply, he played really well and I played really badly. It was perhaps one of my worst matches in the last few months.

"I was a bit annoyed the last couple of days because achieving the world No 1 status is something that every player dreams of. But then I feel like I'm the only world No 1 in history who has to explain why it's normal for me to be No 1, which I find quite difficult because I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today.

"I don't think anyone has had to explain themselves as much as I have in the last couple of days, which is annoying."

The 29-year-old, who climbed to No 1 on Monday, suffered a surprise defeat days after losing to Australia's ​Alex de Minaur in the Vienna Open ‌semi-finals.

Musetti, a former world No 5, seized the initiative by winning six of ​the final seven points of the opening-set tiebreak before taking command of the second set.

The 24-year-old Italian broke Zverev for a ​2-1 lead and struck again to move ⁠5-2 ahead on his way to ⁠victory.

"It's pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of (Zverev), who was serving really well, especially in the first set," Musetti, 24, said in his on-court interview.

"It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2. I played five great points in a row."

Sports.title: Lions' Campbell has full movement in lower body after neck injury
Sports.content:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has full movement in his lower body after he was taken to hospital with a neck injury during Sunday's NFL win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end TJ Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory on Sunday.

The 26-year-old was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause.

Image: Campbell signed a contract extension with the Lions in May that takes him through 2030

Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart.

Campbell offered his own injury update on Wednesday, noting that he also has movement in his upper body.

In a statement, he said: "My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days.

"It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.

"I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan.

"I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this.

"I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me.

"The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done.

"To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

"One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough."

Sports.title: Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapses
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola arrived in Istanbul seeking improvement from Liverpool’s attack but departed with sudden cause for concern at the opposite end of the pitch. Fenerbahce ignited Dirk Kuyt’s interim spell with a tumultuous victory after Liverpool detonated their 100% Champions League record with several defensive lapses.

Liverpool’s second successive defeat left Iraola exasperated for entirely different reasons to Sunday’s loss to Arsenal. Blame was found only in the mirror this time around. It was so careless and so unnecessary.

The visitors led twice, through Trey Nyoni’s first senior goal and a header from substitute Alexander Isak, but Fenerbahce twice hit back quickly and snatched victory when Vedat Muriqi emerged as the strongest player from a pack of red shirts. Fenerbahce’s first goal came from a free-kick, their second from a corner and their third from a long throw-in.

“Cheap goals, messy goals,” as the Liverpool head coach put it. “We knew set pieces were one of the strengths of Fenerbahce. We have been dealing with them well, both this season and today, it has been something we have been working on since pre-season, but it cost us today. The last goal was maybe because they are strong and tall but the other two we have to control better.”

Ronald Araújo resting on the bench offers one explanation for Liverpool’s weak defensive display but does not cover every fault. The visitors enjoyed large spells of control and, despite an anonymous display from Bradley Barcola as the central striker, should never have given hope to an ageing, average Fenerbahce side packed with familiar names from the Premier League.

As expected, Turkish supporters tested the eardrums with incessant whistling whenever Liverpool took possession. They were a test for structural engineers too with their constant bouncing in the upper tier of the home end. Liverpool sought to dilute the atmosphere by controlling possession. Rio Ngumoha was prominent and N’Golo Kanté should have been booked for halting one promising run by leaping on the teenager’s back. Referee Clément Turpin was in a lenient mood with both sides.

View image in fullscreen Fenerbahce’s Archie Brown celebrates their victory. Photograph: Murad Sezer/Reuters

Fenerbahce had struggled to hold up play in the Liverpool half or create a chance of note when Archie Brown exposed the visiting defence with a superb ball from left-back. The pass sailed over the struggling Kostas Tsimikas and was controlled well by Mason Greenwood, before he was pushed over by the Liverpool defender. Neither Turpin nor the video assistant referee deemed it a penalty kick.

The decibel levels cranked up and went even higher when Liverpool took the lead moments later. Ngumoha was heavily involved with a darting run and shot that was charged down into the path of Dominik Szoboszlai. Brown, under pressure from Virgil van Dijk, headed the midfielder’s cross clear but only as far as Nyoni. The young midfielder swept a low volley beyond Ederson with the aid of a slight deflection off Kojo Peprah Oppong. It was a memorable milestone in the continued rise of Nyoni; the first goal of his career at the highest level.

It was also the cue for Fenerbahce to rouse themselves. The hosts almost levelled straight from the restart when Brown’s low centre was turned against Alisson’s crossbar by Irfan Can Kahveci, who may have been ruled offside. They did not have to wait long for the equaliser. After Szoboszlai was penalised for a foul on Kanté, Greenwood’s resulting free-kick took a huge deflection off Jérémy Jacquet’s stomach and sailed past the wrongfooted Alisson. The Liverpool keeper did not hide his anger at Jacquet turning away from the free-kick and leaving a costly hole in the wall.
