The second half mirrored the first with Liverpool in control until scoring and provoking a reaction from the Turkish side. Substitutes Cody Gakpo and Isak had only been on the pitch three minutes when they combined to restore the visitors’ advantage, the Swedish striker heading past Ederson from Gakpo’s left-wing cross.

But Fenerbahce again levelled swiftly when Kanté swept in a cross following a corner and Gakpo, attempting to head clear, glanced the ball away from Alisson’s grasp to give Brown a simple tap-in at the back post. “In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate,” Iraola admitted. “It was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication must have been difficult between Cody and Ali.”

Worse was to come for Liverpool when Birmingham-born Brown looped a cross into the heart of Liverpool’s box. Muriqi, a second-half replacement for Romelu Lukaku, managed to hold off three Liverpool players – Jacquet, Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni – and plant a header into the bottom corner. Iraola added: “It’s so frustrating because this is a difficult place to play and we were winning twice. We need to look at how we conceded the goals.”

Sports.title: Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague
Sports.content:
Another European away day, another victory for Arsenal: albeit only just. This time, Viktor Gyökeres stole the show as poor Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history despite a spirited late comeback. That unwanted record stands at 23, equalling the mark set by AEK Athens and FCSB – formerly known as Steaua Bucharest – while Arsenal are unbeaten in their 10 last away trips.

However, had it not been for a wonder save from David Raya, the Czech champions would have snatched a point after Wiktor Nowak pulled one back late on as Mikel Arteta’s usually watertight defence showed signs of fallibility under pressure.

In contrast to last week’s defeat against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup, Arsenal had been cruising until the last 15 minutes after Noni Madueke fired them ahead early on, set up superbly by Gyökeres.

That was the Sweden striker’s third assist in his past five appearances, although Arteta will have been even more encouraged by the emphatic finish that appeared to put the game beyond Slavia’s reach just before the break.

But the Arsenal manager admitted his side had taken their eye off the ball by allowing their hosts back into the game with some uncharacteristic defensive lapses as Slavia racked up 18 shots to his side’s 12.

“At half-time, the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game,” said Arteta. “We were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept and in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half. That is a huge learning.”

Slavia’s solitary victory in this competition came in their first-ever match in 2007 and after losing 3-0 to Arsenal here exactly a year ago, they knew their chances of avoiding the unwanted milestone were extremely slim. Arteta’s side have developed a killer instinct on their travels in Europe – not since May 2025 in the second leg of their semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain have Arsenal lost an away game in 90 minutes.

After their exploits at Anfield on Sunday that took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League, Arteta heavily rotated his side again with six changes. It’s perhaps not surprising that Martín Zubimendi ran out of steam given the Spain World Cup winner made only his third start of a so far frustrating campaign.

For the third time in Arsenal’s past four matches, Gyökeres was entrusted with leading the line after finally getting off the mark with a scrappy strike against Fleetwood. He finished as top scorer last season with 21 goals but has clearly been struggling for form and confidence. Yet there was no doubting the quality of his assist for Madueke’s opening goal after just eight minutes.

Raya’s long ball should have been dealt with by the Slavia defence but they made the criminal error of ­allowing it to bounce. That was the cue for Gyökeres to come alive as he beat his marker to the ball, chested it down and played the perfect pass for the England forward to run on to and score. Arteta’s reaction on the touchline suggested he enjoyed it too.

Mikel Merino was Arsenal’s hero here last year with two goals and he could have extended their lead on three occasions before the half-hour mark. The lively Madueke created his best opportunity after cutting the ball back to Merino but he could not beat Nazar Domchak in Slavia’s goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Noni Madueke, who scored Arsenal’s first goal, and Declan Rice applaud the travelling fans. Photograph: David W Cerny/Reuters

With Martin Ødegaard watching from the bench next to William Saliba on the latter’s return from a long-term back injury, Arsenal lacked some of their usual fluency in attack. But ­Slavia were still no match for them and their task became almost ­impossible seven minutes before the break. Gyökeres exchanged a smart one-two with Merino inside the area before curling a brilliant shot into the far corner.

To their credit, the hosts began the second half with much more aggression after introducing their record signing, Ange N’Guessan, from the bench. Ezri Konsa and Declan Rice both found themselves in the book as Arsenal were pinned back. David Jurasek let fly from long range and his effort was deflected just wide of Raya’s goal. From the resulting corner, Gabriel Magalhães somehow managed to clear two goalbound headers off the line in a matter of seconds. The Brazilian celebrated with a massive fist pump but his evening wasn’t over.

Mikulas Konecny should have done much better with another header before Raya managed to push Oskar Kubiak’s header on to the post despite being at full stretch in mid-air. Slavia eventually scored the goal all their endeavour deserved in the final minute of normal time when Nowak fired in at the far post. There were a few nervous moments in stoppage time as Konecny forced Raya into another save. Arteta breathed a sigh of relief at the full-time whistle as Slavia were condemned to their fate.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland settles thriller for Manchester City to end RB Leipzig resistance
Sports.content:
Feed Erling Haaland and Manchester City’s totemic No 9 will score. The problem, recently, has been a paucity of openings for him.

This was true again before Elliot Anderson crossed and Haaland slid home a priceless winner for Enzo Maresca’s disjointed unit, Rayan Cherki hitting a post late on.

The win ends City’s sequence of two defeats in three games yet the manager has major issues. He has to plug a leaky defence and drill his midfield to exert control.

And there is a shaky Gianluigi Donnarumma: City’s goalkeeper was culpable for Ridle Baku’s first equaliser for Leipzig, as he was for Nicolas Jackson’s winner in the recent defeat at Aston Villa, plus two more in the Paris Saint-Germain loss last month.

The manager said: “It’s not a concern but it’s a mistake. But in 48 hours [Saturday] we have Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that and then in the international break I will look. At the moment I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation. Gigio knows he was not good with the first goal.”

He was honest, too, about Antonio Nusa’s second for Leipzig, the forward taking advantage of a lax rearguard. “Both goals are quite silly goals we can avoid,” Maresca said.

Still, after going down against Villa and Brighton in the Premier League, the win is a certifiable tonic ahead of the Forest trip.

City’s quest to return to victorious ways featured an XI of four changes from Saturday’s Brighton reverse. Noteworthy was Maresca’s dropping of Rúben Dias as Abdukodir Khusanov’s pace was preferred at centre-back to the captain, Haaland taking the armband.

While the 2,000-plus travelling support were stationed in a quadrant to the right of Donnarumma’s goal, the noise came from the congregation behind Maarten Vandevoordt’s where a sea of red and white bounced to the tempo of a booming drum. They could roar particularly loud when Nusa flitted across City’s D and unloaded, and what should have been a regulation save for Donnarumma became a fumble – and corner for Leipzig.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández heads home for Manchester City in the second half. Photograph: Matthias Schräder/AP

As can be with this Maresca side, control was difficult to find and administer for any prolonged passage: Phil Foden twice lost the ball when turning into traffic was no aid, the second time meaning Nusa could zigzag towards goal.

The Brighton defeat featured close to zero service for Haaland and City’s 13-goal man was again hard to find, Matheus Nunes’s loose cross, when the captain lurked, emblematic. So, too, as a sign of Leipzig’s ascendancy, was Marc Guéhi scrambling to clear danger, Nusa firing in the ball from the left, and Christoph Baumgartner having space to shoot marginally wide of Donnarumma’s left post.

“Keep the ball and shift it faster” might have been Maresca’s instruction and when this happened City fashioned the breakthrough. Cherki speared a diagonal right-left into a galloping Nico O’Reilly, whose instant cross caused Castello Lukeba to panic and turn home, via a trailing left knee.

City had forced the issue and twice went close to a second moments later. First, O’Reilly floated the ball into Leipzig’s area but Haaland’s header faltered. Then the left-back was set up by Iliman Ndiaye’s cross only for O’Reilly to miss with the same part of his anatomy.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Yet as the second half began Leipzig were staring at a fifth defeat in the fixture, having won only once in six previous meetings, all in this competition.

Intent was signalled by Nusa’s mazy run along the left, his chip causing Donnarumma to push away when he might have caught. This roused the home supporters and better followed for their team – but not Donnarumma.

View image in fullscreen Castello Lukeba scores his first-half own goal to give Manchester City the lead. Photograph: Annegret Hilse/Reuters

Anderson’s loose ball for O’Reilly near halfway was snaffled by Leipzig, who marauded down the right before Brajan Gruda fed an overlapping Baku. Now came Donnarumma’s folly because, while the right-back’s shot was true, it was steered along a very tight angle, yet City’s No 1 allowed it to go in between him and his left post.

Here was the latest goal-costing error from the Italian – one for Maresca to ponder. Yet 1-1 was still a fair result away from the Etihad Stadium so relief emanated from those in black when Ezechiel Banzuzi’s shot hit side-netting only. Donnarumma’s wobble continued, though, as he fumbled another Baku attempt, narrowly recovering.

City were about to show character and quality: Ndiaye’s pinpoint cross from the left had Enzo Fernández arriving to head in supremely and Maresca’s team led again. Not for long. Leipzig waltzed through with ease and with Nunes out of position Nusa finished expertly from the left.

After Anderson skied over from close-range, Haaland did what makes him so lethal: score with his sole chance. “Not sure how many touches I had, but most important is that I managed to help the team to win,” the Norwegian said.

Sports.title: Champions League: Como clobber Lens 9-1 after Real Madrid roar back to deny AEK Athens
Sports.content:
Anastasios Douvikas led the rout with a hat-trick as Como cruised to a 9-1 victory at Lens, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game.

Only two teams had previously won a game by a margin of eight goals since the launch of the modern Champions League in 1992. Liverpool thumped Besiktas 8-0 in the group stage in 2007 and Real Madrid won by the same scoreline against Malmo in 2015.

Como are just the second team to score nine times in a game in the competition, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the league phase in 2024.

Cesc Fàbregas’s side made it three wins from four in their maiden campaign in the competition with a spellbinding display.

Nico Paz continued his fine form with a goal and two assists, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored for the Serie A side, who had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home in this campaign.

The last club to score nine away from home in the European Cup was Feyenoord against Olympiakos in 1971.

Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday and preserve their 100% start in the group phase.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid players pile on top of Federico Valverde after the midfielder’s 90th-minute winner in Athens. Photograph: Petros Giannakouris/AP

José Mourinho’s side, who started with Vinícius Júnior on the left flank after he missed the team’s previous two La Liga matches through suspension, twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side.

Aboubakary Koïta sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes before Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappé swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner.

Madrid have now won seven successive games across all competitions.

Scott McTominay found the net but Napoli endured a 4-1 defeat by Porto, who had lost their first three games in the competition, while Club Brugge are up to ninth after a 2-1 win at PSV.

Konstantinos Karetsas struck a 72nd-minute winner as Borussia Dortmund beat Real Betis 2-1, while Erik Botheim helped himself to two goals as Viking secured their first triumph with a 4-1 win against 10-man Sabah.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham stage dramatic comeback on Scott Parker’s opening night
Sports.content:
Scott Parker’s return to West Ham had looked like beginning in painful fashion but instead featured a stunning comeback from 3-0 down. The east London club’s new head coach had watched Cardiff’s Jack Moylan score a first-half hat-trick, before a rousing response after the break ended with Max Kilman levelling the scores at 3-3 eight minutes from time.

Elsewhere in the Championship, the leaders Middlesbrough went down 2-0 at Wrexham.

Parker had been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach earlier on Wednesday, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

A relieved Parker said afterwards: “I came in here at nine o’clock this morning and met the players for the first time, so I didn’t have a lot of input as such. As you can imagine, it was a difficult half-time talk. I just helped them tactically and told them: ‘OK, this is the way it needs to be now.’

“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive. There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed. We took a few more risks.”

Parker admitted he could have skipped the dugout and “sat in a box” with his appointment confirmed on matchday. But the new head coach – who won promotion to the Premier League with his former clubs Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham – chose to spend the night on the touchline.

“The first half was poor in many aspects,” Parker said. “We were very passive and slow with the ball. The biggest positive is the team we saw in the second half. These boys have come off two defeats. You come to Cardiff away and you’re 3-0 down at half-time. I can only imagine what they were feeling. They showed a lot of character and that pleased me the most.”

Moylan halted the initial feelgood factor among the visiting support in the 11th minute at Cardiff City Stadium. His right-foot drive from the tip of the D left the visiting goalkeeper Mads Hermansen helpless as it sped into the top left corner. Moylan was then brought down for a penalty – the Ireland midfielder got up to spank it home to the left as Hermansen dived right in the 37th minute.

Within two minutes, Will Fish thought he had turned in a corner for Cardiff’s third – the centre-back deftly headed towards goal, but Moylan was directly behind him and claimed his hat-trick after making the final touch.

After the break, it was a completely different story. Divine Mukasa reduced the deficit in the 58th minute, finishing calmly over the stranded Nathan Trott after a fine ball over the top from Jarrod Bowen, before Arne Engels capitalised on a mix-up in the home defence to make it 3-2.

In the 82nd minute, Bowen was again the supplier, curling in an inviting cross from the right that was turned in by the centre-back Kilman to make it 3-3 from close range.

At the Racecourse, Wrexham waited until the 70th minute to break the deadlock against Middlesbrough, before George Thomason smashed a shot into the ground from just outside the area, which rocketed past a crowd of defenders and through the unsighted visiting goalkeeper Radek Vítek. Oli Rathbone then made it 2-0 in the 84th minute.

Kim Hellberg, the Middlesbrough manager, refused to blame the absence of their top scorer Will Lankshear after the Championship leaders’ 11-match unbeaten run ended, but admitted it hardly helped.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Every team would miss their top goalscorer,” Hellberg said. “I think it’s tough when the decision is made very late and you have planned for it. That doesn’t help … You need to find ways. Today I think it would be difficult because we weren’t sharp enough. Whoever would be on the pitch there were not so many opportunities.”

Scott Twine scored a stunning, curling free-kick to give Bristol City the lead at Ashton Gate but the promotion-chasing Wolves turned the match around with two late goals from Sean Neave to make it a 2-1 win to the visitors.

Neave, on loan from Newcastle, came off the bench to score on 82 and 89 minutes to win it for Wolves, much to the delight of their manager, César Peixoto.

“The team showed character and soul to win that game. They kept on believing right to the end and so did our supporters,” Peixoto said. “We got what we deserved in the end. We created a lot of chances from wide areas in the first half without getting on the end of them often enough.

“Sean Neave is a young guy making his first steps in professional football and those goals will do him a lot of good. He has a lot of ability, but is humble and plays for the team.”

City’s manager, Michael Skubala, said: “We fell to a sucker punch. When you get to 80 minutes ahead against a very good side you have to take something from the game.

“As a group, we have to defend better. The goals were soft from our perspective and we could have been stronger to prevent the second in particular.”

Sports.title: Real Madrid close on agreement to sign Manchester United 16-year-old JJ Gabriel
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are closing in on signing JJ Gabriel, though Manchester United will consider legal action if the club believe any rules have been broken.

Madrid have offered the 16‑year‑old forward a multi‑year contract and, subject to final talks, hope to bring him to the Bernabéu in January. Gabriel is registered with United’s academy until the end of the season and it is understood the club have yet to be contacted by the player’s camp or Real Madrid regarding the proposed move.

Madrid intend to sign Gabriel via a Fifa loophole that allows clubs in the EU to secure young players on professional contracts if they have an EU passport, which Gabriel is eligible to acquire through both his parents.

Fifa would have to sign this off and United are on alert regarding any potential breach of regulations. A compensation fee would be due to United if Gabriel joined Madrid or any other team. Madrid have been approached for comment.

Gabriel walked out on United in September and is believed to be training in Spain. A move to Madrid offers the prospect of progression to senior football via their B team, Castilla, who play in the regionalised Spanish third tier.

Gabriel played in a pre-season friendly for United against Atlético Madrid in Stockholm in August at the age of 15 and had been training with the first team. If he had not informed United of his wish to depart, he would have been in Michael Carrick’s squad for the Carabao Cup third-round defeat against Brighton on 16 September. Had Gabriel featured, he would have become the youngest player in the club’s history.

Last season Gabriel became the youngest winner of United’s academy player of the year award and was the Premier League’s under‑18 player of the season.

Sports.title: Goalkeeper Jesús Owono experiencing ‘hardest days of my life’ after De Miguel’s death
Sports.content:
The FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after he was involved in the collision that led to the death of the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel.

Owono had raced out of his goal and crashed into De Miguel in added time at the end of the Spanish second division match on Monday afternoon, causing the striker to experience a cardiorespiratory arrest. De Miguel was taken to hospital in Santa Cruz de Tenerife but never regained consciousness and died on Tuesday morning.

“These are being the hardest days of my life,” Owono said in a statement published by Andorra. “I find it hard to find the words and very difficult to assimilate what has happened. I feel a huge pain, the loss of Jesús. I am thinking about him, his family and all the people who loved him.

“I know that there will be many questions to address and I will face up to whatever comes with respect. But right now, sincerely, I cannot think about anything other than Jesús and the pain that we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesús.”

Andorra’s statement said that the club remained “deeply affected” by De Miguel’s death and demanded “the greatest respect and sensibility”. The homicide division of the Spanish national police opened an investigation, which is standard procedure in Spain whenever there is a death not by natural causes. Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s chief prosecutor, José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, told the Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings against the goalkeeper were “very unlikely”.

The investigation will focus on the events that preceded De Miguel’s death, including the attention he received after medics sprinted on to the pitch. De Miguel was treated on the field for five minutes before being taken off on a stretcher and to an ambulance that waited in the corner. Tenerife had reported that medics were able to recover a pulse in the ambulance before he was admitted to intensive care.

View image in fullscreen Jesús Owono ‘would never intentionally hurt anyone’ one of his Andorra teammates said. Photograph: Walter Cunha/NurPhoto/Getty Images

“We can’t say if they acted correctly or incorrectly, but we can demand that all the emergency procedures follow international standards of correct practice,” Elvira González, the president of Spain’s Association of Nurses, Emergency Medics and Caregivers, told the Associated Press. “There is contradictory information. The first thing we need to know is where and when he supposedly recovered a pulse. The first minutes are critical. You can only move a person once a pulse is restored.”

Tenerife’s majority shareholder, Rayco García, told Cadena Ser radio: “There are those who say that the impact caused his death, and that later they were able to stabilise him artificially even though it was very difficult to bring him back. I prefer to wait for the autopsy and then we can take steps. I would like to see [the results of] the investigation to know if there is something to ensure this doesn’t happen again, something that could have prevented this tragedy.”

Owono had earlier been defended by his teammate Lautaro Spatz, who wrote on social media: “I also ‌want to say a few words about my teammate, goalkeeper ‌and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he ‌would never intentionally hurt anyone. In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Equatoguinean Football Federation expressed its support, saying that Owono, who has 47 caps for the country, was going through a situation of profound sorrow and grief.

Owono was sent off for the challenge and immediately walked towards the touchline, only to turn back as staff began running in the other direction. The goalkeeper deactivated his Instagram account on Tuesday after receiving abuse online, with some users commenting “murderer” on his posts. Andorra said they were offering psychological support to anyone at the club who needed it after De Miguel’s death. The Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, had said they would need “professional help”.

De Miguel, 30, was married and had an 18-month-old child, both of whom were in the stadium when the incident happened. Flowers have been left at the stadium by gate nine, his shirt number, and a minute’s silence was held at the Canarian government building.

De Miguel’s body laid at the Tanatorio Santa Lastenia funeral parlour in Santa Cruz before being flown to the Spanish mainland on Wednesday afternoon. Tenerife’s players and staff will fly to Madrid on a charter on Thursday morning and go from there to the village of Navahermosa in Toledo province, where De Miguel’s parents are from, for the funeral. A final homage will be held at Tenerife’s Heliodoro Rodriguez López stadium on Saturday evening.

Sports.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
Sports.content:
At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing.

To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more.

Add in two WSL assists and a goal and an assist on her France debut last month and it has been a breakthrough campaign for Hurtré that very few expected, except perhaps those who followed closely her career in France. They include the former France head coach Olivier Echouafni, who gave a 16-year-old Hurtré her professional debut for Paris Saint-Germain during the title-winning 2020-21 campaign, the only time a side have stopped OL Lyonnes from finishing top in the past 20 years.

“She listens to everything the coach says, she’s very attentive, she’s very focused,” Echouafni says. “She’s like a sun, because when you speak with her there’s a big light. She was always quite skilful, moving the ball quickly to draw out her opponent, and had a good shot and delivered quality crosses.

“Back then, she lacked athletic stamina, the ability to sustain repeated bursts and sometimes also struggled in one-on-one situations because she was so young, but she has made great progress since then. She has also made great progress mentally – her move to Birmingham has done her a world of good.”

WSL fans are enjoying Hurtré’s pace, skill and general attacking threats, but imprinted in Echouafni’s memory are her defensive efforts as a youngster. He recalls Hurtré, on her second league appearance, against Paris FC in May 2021, replacing the Canada full-back Ashley Lawrence with two minutes remaining. “She cleared the ball off the goalline and prevented the equaliser,” he says. “It was a very important action because, one week later, PSG won the championship.”

To describe her as surrounded by experienced professionals at PSG would be a big understatement. When she had made her debut, in Europe against the Polish side Gornik Leczna, she was on the same team as a 42-year-old Formiga. Her gratitude to PSG is clear: she was spotted at the Joie Stadium last week watching Manchester City take on PSG in the Women’s Champions League, sitting just above her former club’s bench. PSG loaned Hurtré to Dijon in 2022 to gain more first-team experience and to Bordeaux in 2023-24. An injury at each affected her game time but she left a strong impression.

“I wanted to sign Océane for two main reasons,” says Sylvain Carric, Dijon women’s general manager from 2022 until 2026, who now runs the Strasbourg women’s teams. “The first was, naturally, the quality of her left foot – it’s magnificent; she can put the ball exactly where she wants it. The second was her versatility. She’s capable of playing as a left-back, a winger or a No 8.

View image in fullscreen Océane Hurtré’s form at Birmingham has led to an international callup with France, where she scored on her debut. Photograph: Natalie Mincher/SPP/Shutterstock

“Océane left a fantastic impression during her time at Dijon. She had the intelligence to come to Dijon to grow, rather than remaining on the bench at PSG. She was a very good player and an excellent teammate, always smiling. She has been supported by a very good inner circle, especially her father, who I believe played an important role in her success. As for her potential, it was obvious, especially given that left foot, but she just needed to adapt her physique for the elite level. Now that she’s brought all those elements together, I’m certainly not surprised.”

Hurtré took a risk when she joined second-tier Birmingham in the summer of 2025 but it has paid off after she helped them to win promotion and she has goals against clubs including Arsenal, Brighton and Manchester City.

Birmingham’s head coach, Amy Merricks, said last month: “We’re incredibly proud of her. I’m not going to share it but, if I did share where she was when she first came in, people wouldn’t quite believe the turnaround. There were so many areas that she needed support with, transitioning to a different country at a young age. She’s learned English, which is a massive step.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Everyone sees her work on the pitch but we are fortunate to see the amount of work she’s done of it, and it absolutely translates. She’s diligent, she’s a student of the game, and she thoroughly deserved the call-up [for France].”

Hurtré was rewarded for her strong start with the WSL player of the month award for September. Sylvain Jamet, a women’s football writer for the French magazine footofeminin, saw her play at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Costa Rica and believes Hurtré has become “a lot faster” at Birmingham.

“Her technical ability and her set-piece deliveries with her left foot stood out,” Jamet says of Hurtré’s six years representing France’s youth teams. “Since she’s arrived in the UK, they must have worked on her speed.”

View image in fullscreen Océane Hurtré caused problems for the Latvia defence during her international debut last month. Photograph: Eddy Lemaistre/Icon Sport/Getty Images

Hurtré’s goal contributions in France’s 9-0 win against Latvia have boosted her hopes of a place at the World Cup next summer. Jamet, comparing her to Chelsea’s left-sided France player Sandy Baltimore, says: “They’re competing for the same place with France now. She’s less explosive than Sandy, but she’s better technically for the crosses and passing. Baltimore’s obviously fantastic, more like a one-v-one player, taking on defenders.

“Hurtré can cross from anywhere, she can do what [David] Beckham did, basically, crossing from deep, crossing from anywhere. She had very good first cap for France. There’s a good chance she will be in the squad for the World Cup. I really expect her to get one of those 26 places.”

Sports.title: Como make Champions League era history with incredible nine-goal mauling
Sports.content:
Como enjoyed an historic night as they thumped Lens 9-1 to equal the biggest win of the Champions League era.

Cesc Fabregas' side continued their stunning debut campaign in Europe's premier competition by producing their most impressive display yet with a record-breaking away victory.



4 Como have been the Champions League surprise package this term, especially after thumping Lens Credit: Getty

After thrashing Manchester United 4-1 last time out, Como reached a new level against Lens as seven different players found the net.

Anastasios Douvikas led the way with a hat-trick for the Italian side, grabbing a brace in the first half before Nico Paz struck to put the visitors 3-0 up at the interval.

And the best was yet to come in the second half, with Como grabbing six more goals to write their name into the record books.



Douvikos completed his treble, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli all struck for Fabregas' side.

Ruben Aguilar found the net on 65 minutes to score the smallest of consolation goals for Lens, as the game finished 9-1.



Records galore for superb Como

The result saw Como climb to fourth in the Champions League league phase table with their third win in four games, and record multiple records in the process.

The eight-goal margin equalled the biggest victory in Champions League history since it rebranded under this name in 1992.



Liverpool and Real Madrid have both previously won by this scoreline - doing so against Besiktas and Malmo respectively in 2007 and 2015.

Meanwhile, Como also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a game.

The German giants famously thrashed Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the 2024/25 season - with Harry Kane netting four goals on the night.

4 Fabregas' reputation continues to grow after Lens' historic 9-1 win in the Champions League Credit: Getty



4 Douvikas was the star of the show as he grabbed a hat-trick in the rout Credit: Getty

And there was further history for Como by recording their eye-watering scoreline away from home.

They are now the first team of the Champions League era to score nine goals in an away match, and the first to do so in 45 years in the European Cup altogether.

Feyenoord were the last side to do so, when they won 9-0 at Olympiakos Nicosia in September 1971.



And while Como found themselves in the record books for the right reasons, Lens instead made unwanted history.

Their crushing defeat was a record Champions League loss for a French club, and their third consecutive loss in this season's competition.

Lens now sit a lowly 33rd out of 36 in the overall Champions League standings after four games with three points.

4 Highly-rated Argentine youngster Paz impressed against Lens Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Como are flying high in fourth on nine points, three points behind Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and one point behind Arsenal.

The Serie A side, who finished fourth in Serie A last season to qualify for the Champions League for the first time, had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Man United 4-1 at home in this campaign.

Sports.title: Gianluigi Donnarumma is a Poundland James Trafford and Man City’s dynasty will end unless they fix these problems
Sports.content:
Gianluigi Donnarumma is a Poundland James Trafford and Man City’s dynasty will end unless they fix these problems

Gianluigi Donnarumma is a problem for Manchester City, whose dominant dynasty could well be coming to an end.

Concerns have been raised over Donnarumma and Man City's future despite winning 3-2 in the Champions League against RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

5 Donnarumma has been labelled a 'Poundland James Trafford' after making a big error for Man City against RB Leipzig in the Champions League Credit: AFP

The Italian goalkeeper was at fault for Leipzig's first goal of the evening on Wednesday, standing way off his line.

He was caught sleeping as right-back Ridle Baku fired a cross directly into an empty net with the City shotstopper missing.

Thankfully for him, the Premier League giants went on to win the game, albeit after he conceded another goal.

But ex-Arsenal winger Perry Groves thinks Donnarumma is starting to impact City's success, with talkSPORT host Adrian Durham in agreement.

Donnarumma is a 'Poundland Trafford'

Groves said after the full-time whistle in Germany: “The big problem they have, Man City, is Donnarumma.

"He's nowhere near the goalkeeper that he was. And if you watch Ridle Baku's goal and he sees that Donnarumma is off his line at the near post. And he rolls it inside him into the far side netting.

"And Donnarumma could have actually let another one in where he lets a shot from Antonio Nusa go through his hands.

“That would be a worry if I was Enzo Maresca."

Bringing up former City goalkeeper James Trafford, who they sold to Leeds this summer, Durham then added: “Do you know what? I call him a Poundland James Trafford, Donnarumma.

“I know people think it's disrespectful. He's had a great career. He's been brilliant, he's a European champion. He's won so much and fair play to him for that.

5 Donnarumma was well off his line and expecting a cross when Baku caught him out and scored from a wide position

5 And Durham thinks Trafford is better than Donnarumma, despite the latter forcing the England international's sale from Man City this summer Credit: Getty

“But he's got his angles all wrong for one of the Leipzig goals and the ball is fired and he's expecting a cross.

"But at this level, who knows what's going to happen? You can't just expect it to be a cross. And then if it's a shot that beats you at your near post, you look like a mug.”

Is Man City's dynasty over?

Man City struggled to their victory over Leipzig in the Champions League in the end, coming away 3-2 winners.

The Bundesliga outfit had more shots than them, hit the woodwork and had a goal disallowed as they piled pressure on.

That somewhat fortunate result followed a loss to Brighton in the league, a win via a penalty shootout over the same opposition in the Carabao Cup and another league defeat to Aston Villa.

And City's form in October through to Wednesday has talkSPORT's Micky Gray and Groves concerned for their future under Maresca after such a dominant period under Pep Guardiola.

5 Man City have dominated games in the Premier League and Europe in recent years, but there are concerns that that is now fading Credit: Getty

Gray explained: “Whether it's Premier League or Champions League. I don't think they've got the right balance yet.

"He is trying to bring a little bit of pace into it. Bringing [Abdukodir] Khusanov into that back line... he makes the odd mistake as well.

“I think the full-back positions, Nico O'Reilly wants to be a left winger or a left midfielder. Donnarumma, he made an absolute world class save. I think it was 1-0 at the time and he's tipped across the top corner. It was absolutely brilliant.

“They're great going forward, they're always going to create chances.

"But I think defensively, they're still vulnerable for me. They got a little bit fortunate tonight.

“I think overall they probably deserved to win the game but Leipzig asked them a lot of questions.”

5 City's struggles to control games and strike fear into opponents may signal the end of their dynasty Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, Groves then went on to question: “I think that Man City are coming to the end of their dynasty.

"Because you could tell in the second half especially that Martin Demichelis, the RB Leipzig manager, he sent RB Leipzig out on the front foot.

“He made sure that they played another ten, 15 yards further up the field. And that's why Baku got his goal, because he comes from right back.

“So, you can tell that teams, when they're playing against Man City, they get a feeling that they're always in the game. They've always got a chance, because Man City now don't put teams to bed.

"And they've had one clean sheet in the last nine matches.

"So, you know that if you're patient, but you're brave, then you can get at them.”

Sports.title: West Ham produce heroic comeback after Scott Parker’s ruthless decision on £21m star
Sports.content:
Scott Parker’s decision to axe striker Pablo paid off as he masterminded a stunning comeback in his first match as West Ham manager.

Just hours after being unveiled as the Hammers' new boss, Parker enjoyed a thrilling return to the dugout as his side fought back from 3-0 down at half time to draw 3-3 with Cardiff City.

5 Parker enjoyed a dramatic return to management on Tuesday night Credit: Getty

5 Max Kilman's 82nd minute goal saw West Ham fight back from 3-0 down to get a point Credit: Getty

Replacing Nuno Espirito Santo following his sacking 24 hours earlier, Parker's tenure got off to a quite unbelievable start in Wales.

Things could hardly have began worse, when West Ham found themselves three goals down at the break after Jack Moylan's hat-trick.

But few could have expected the response Parker would get from his side after the interval, as they then mounted a stunning comeback.

Divine Mukasa pulled a goal back on 58 minutes, and Arne Engels struck shortly after to make it 3-2 with 25 minutes remaining.

As the game entered its final ten minutes, Max Kilman grabbed a thrilling equaliser to spark pandemonium in the away end.

The late fightback saw Parker make an instant statement as Hammers boss, as his side avoided falling to a third straight defeat by snatching a point.

Parker benches Pablo

The result came after some bold team selections, as Parker made five changes to the side that lost 3-1 to West Brom on Saturday.

Most brutal of all was the decision to drop striker £21million man Pablo from the squad entirely after starting at the weekend.

With the forward not appearing to suffer an injury last time out, it is unclear whether he was dropped on form or if he sustained a knock in training, having scored just once in the Championship this term.

The Portuguese has struggled since his arrival from Primeira Liga side Gil Vicente in January, finding the net just twice in 28 games.

5 Pablo was the victim of Parker's first ruthless call as West Ham boss Credit: Getty

5 Parker represented West Ham as a player for four years and is now looking to guide them back into the top flight as manager Credit: Getty

He failed to get off the mark in 14 Premier League appearances last season, as the Irons were relegated to the Championship.

This term, his only league goal has come in a 6-0 thrashing of Lincoln in October, while he also found the net in a 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Fulham.

Parker appeared unconvinced by the forward's numbers, as he immediately axed him for the Cardiff clash, with Taty Castellanos taking his place in the starting XI.

This didn't initially seem to have the desired effect, as West Ham found themselves up against it after going 3-0 down at Cardiff.

But after pulling off a stunning second-half fightback, Parker was vindicated in his decision which helped snatch a point.

West Ham remain eighth in the Championship - now the final Championship play-off place following the decision to expand.

5 Parker is targeting promotion with a fourth different team with West Ham Credit: Getty

With six months of the season still left to play, Parker will now be looking to use his past experience to inspire his side to an automatic promotion push.

The former Hammers midfielder was available as a free agent after leaving Burnley in April.

Parker has won promotion out of the Championship three times in his managerial career with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley.

As a player, the former England international spent four years with West Ham between 2007 and 2011.

During that time, he made 129 appearances for the club, scoring 12 goals from midfield.

Sports.title: Goalkeeper makes emotional statement in first public comments since death of Jesus de Miguel after horror collision
Sports.content:
Goalkeeper makes emotional statement in first public comments since death of Jesus de Miguel after horror collision

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has released a statement in his first comments since the death of Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel passed away on Tuesday morning following a sickening collision with Owono in a La Liga 2 match on Monday.



2 Tenerife's De Miguel tragically passed away after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Owono in a match on Monday

The Spanish striker was clattered directly in the chest and head by the onrushing keeper as they competed for a bouncing ball.

He appeared to lose consciousness on the pitch as players waved frantically for medical staff to rush on and help him.

The 30-year-old was quickly taken to an ambulance, but it is reported that he suffered a cardiac arrest on the way to the hospital.



De Miguel then tragically died after the horrifying incident that saw Owono sent off and the match abandoned.

Owono releases emotional statement

Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter regarding Owono's involvement.



The goalkeeper, who isn't expected to face criminal consequences, has since released an emotional statement on the awful situation.

“These are the most difficult days of my life," he said in a post released by his club Andorra.



“I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.

2 Owono has commented on the horrific situation for the first time in an emotional statement released by his club Credit: Getty



“But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing.

“Rest in peace, Jesus.”

'He would never intentionally hurt anyone'

One of Owono's teammates at Andorra, Lautaro Spatz, defended the goalkeeper in a statement of his own on Wednesday.

After paying tribute to De Miguel, Spatz wrote: “I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened.

"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.



"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."

Sports.title: ‘Player I adore’ – Liverpool told academy star can reach top as rise with Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni continues
Sports.content:
‘Player I adore’ – Liverpool told academy star can reach top as rise with Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni continues

Wales manager Craig Bellamy could not speak higher of Liverpool's academy star Lewis Koumas after his rise to the first team.

Koumas has become a regular for his nation as well as a breaking into the starting line-up for the Reds under Andoni Iraola.



3 The 21-year-old has played 13 times for Liverpool this season after breaking into the first team following two loan spells Credit: Getty

Alongside the highly-rated Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni, who both started on Wednesday night in the Champions League, the 21-year-old has been rewarded with increased gametime this term.

So far this season under Iraola, Koumas has been handed his Premier League and European debut, playing 13 times already.

He has made seven top flight appearances for Liverpool, starting five times in all competitions, scoring and assisting one goal.



The forward spent the last two campaigns out on loan with Stoke City and Birmingham City, but he is now a key member of the Reds' squad at Anfield.

And after another international call-up for the upcoming break, Wales boss Bellamy has piled praised on the youngster.



Bellamy tips Koumas for the top

Bellamy told talkSPORT in his press conference on Wednesday: "We saw it in the summer with us, when we brought him on.

"We always felt that Koumas has got all the attributes to be a really top player and obviously he hit the ground running in pre-season.



"The gametime is had is good game time and it's only going to help us.

"From the period of when he played for us, going back to Liverpool and now leading into these games, he's had good game time."

The Wales manager added: "I have to be honest, the type of forward he is, the intensity he plays at I adore, it's like if you could send me a forward, it's him.

3 Koumas has become a regular for Liverpool under Iraola this season and his boss with Wales is also huge fan Credit: Getty



"He's the type of player I adore. He dips in, dips out, looks to stretch, willing to get on the ball at any occasion.

"I honestly feel Liverpool are handling him incredibly well which is going to definitely benefit our country.

"So I'm really positive on the Koumas front at the moment."

What else has Bellamy said?

Bellamy spoke very highly of Liverpool's up-and-coming star Koumas, but he was also asked about another name in the news.

Scott Parker was appointed as the new West Ham manager on Wednesday and the ex-Hammer thinks it's a perfect pick.



"I think it's a really good appointment," Bellamy said.

3 Parker has been appointed as the new West Ham manager after Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked earlier this week Credit: Getty

"I don't like seeing a manager lose their role...you never feel comfortable with it, but we understand the reality of the world we live in.

"They've made a change and I look at Scott and it's a real smart appointment, it make sense, and this is from the outside looking in.

"He's a person whose been in that situation before, in similar circumstances with parachute payments, relegated from the Premier League and morale is a bit down.



"He was a brilliant player and an even better human being. He will grab everyone together, the players will adore him.

"The insight of playing for West Ham, it's a special club. You don't realise how big they are until you go to them.

"He's been there and I see that as a huge advantage."

Sports.title: Newcastle fan wants Matthias Jaissle gone and replaced by sacked Premier League manager
Sports.content:
Newcastle fan wants Matthias Jaissle gone and replaced by sacked Premier League manager

Matthias Jaissle is 'out of his depth' at Newcastle and should be replaced with Thomas Frank, according to one Magpies fan.

Just three months after his appointment at St James' Park, pressure is already mounting on Jaissle as his side slumped to a fourth defeat in five games against Everton on Monday.

4 Matthias Jaissle has now lost as many games as he has won at Newcastle Credit: Getty

The Magpies lost 1-0 at home against the Toffees - just days after they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by the same opposition.

Back-to-back defeats saw Newcastle's worrying run of form continue, who now sit a lowly 13th in the Premier League table.

With results appearing to get worse rather than better, Jaissle has come in for increased scrutiny, even being warned that his side could be dragged into a relegation battle.

That's despite a solid start to life in the north east - which saw the German win four of his eight matches in all competitions, including a 2-2 draw with Liverpool on his touchline debut for the Magpies.

But with Jaissle's honeymoon period now well and truly over, one Newcastle fan has now called for drastic action to be taken.

Frank tipped for Newcastle job

On Tuesday's talkSPORT Breakfast, hosts Jeff Stelling and Andy Townsend took calls from Newcastle supporters, who shared their thoughts on the club's current situation.

Magpies fan Steve rang up with a bold suggestion - as he called for Jaissle to be sacked and replaced with former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank.

Frank has been out of work since being fired by Spurs in February, but has continually linked with a return to the Premier League, most recently at struggling sides Fulham and Crystal Palace.

Asked if he was worried about Newcastle, Steve replied: “Massively. I think the manager's well out of his depth.

“The recruitment team's going to take a lot of responsibility for this as well though because you can't lose players like Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and bring young players in expecting to deliver what the old players have delivered in the past.

4 Newcastle sit 13th in the Premier League - a place lower than they finished last season Credit: Getty

4 Frank's standing in the game remains high despite his stint at Tottenham not working out Credit: Getty

“The manager doesn't seem to have a style of play. He keeps saying we've got this 'vertical football'. It just seems like there's no plan at all. But the senior players have got to take some responsibility.

“I do think it's time for him to go, unfortunately."

Steve then named his recommendation for the Newcastle job in Frank, who garnered a strong reputation by guiding Brentford to the Premier League in a hugely successful seven-year stint.

He continued: “A lot of people laugh at this, but I think Thomas Frank's the man for the job.

"Listen, Thomas, what he did and what he did well at Brentford, he went into Spurs and he couldn't apply. It never worked.

“Whether he could do the same at Newcastle again if he was to get an opportunity - I think there's a debate on that, whether that would be the right appointment for Newcastle. I'm not quite so convinced."

4 Ironically, Frank was sacked Tottenham in February after a defeat to Newcastle Credit: Getty

What is the latest on Thomas Frank?

Despite a difficult six-month stint which led to his sacking at Tottenham, Frank has remained on the radar of Premier League sides since then.

talkSPORT revealed in October that the Dane was a leading contender to take charge at Fulham if they sack Alvaro Arbeloa.

He is also understood to be among the list of candidates explored by Crystal Palace as potential options to replace Pierre Sgae.

Frank meanwhile, has made it clear that he was in no rush to take a new job, saying in the summer: "There have been conversations and opportunities since leaving Spurs, but I have decided not to rush into the next role.

"For me, this summer is not the right time to go back into management.

"When the time is right, I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication."

Sports.title: talkSPORT host reveals what Xabi Alonso will do about Estevao after claims from sources
Sports.content:
talkSPORT host reveals what Xabi Alonso will do about Estevao after claims from sources

Chelsea and Xabi Alonso remain 'delighted' with Estevao despite his lack of playing time - he isn't going anywhere.

That's the latest from talkSPORT's Andy Jacobs, who has revealed all from conversations in the directors' box at Stamford Bridge about the Brazilian starlet, amid concerns he could look to leave the club.



4 Estevao has slipped down the pecking order at Stamford Bridge this season Credit: Getty

Doubts have emerged over Estevao's future in west London, with the winger appearing to be out of favour under new boss Alonso.

After an impressive debut season, the 19-year-old has struggled for minutes this term - highlighted by him being left on the bench during Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit against Liverpool last week.

Alonso then admitted the teenager 'could be happier' - having only had 47 minutes of Premier League action to his name - sparking further fears the Blues could be set to lose their young talent.



However, Estevao was handed his first league start against Manchester United on Saturday and instantly proved his worth.

The Brazilian was a real threat in the 2-0 win, having two goals ruled out for offside, leading to calls for him to feature more regularly.



However, with Alonso's system favouring a back-three, Estevao has found himself playing back-up to Pedro Neto at right-wing-back this term, unable to play as an out-and-out winger.

Meanwhile, in his preferred No.10 role, he has to compete with superstars Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, while Geovany Quenda started ahead of him in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham as Rogers was forced to deputise up front.



Estevao situation explained

Amid growing fears Estevao could see his future elsewhere, talkSPORT host and Chelsea fan Andy Jacobs has now reassured fans that talk of this is unfounded.

Having sat in the directors' box at Stamford Bride for the United win, he revealed that Alonso is, in fact, a huge fan of the teen

On Estevao, Jacobs told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs: “[He's] going nowhere. Apparently the manager loves him.

4 Alonso's preferred system has seen Estevao struggle for game time Credit: Getty



4 But the teenage sensation starred for Chelsea against Man United and the latest is that the teenager is happy at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

“The only concern he has is about his physicality with regards to the Premier League - which is why he played against Manchester United because they're not a physical team.

“So he's worried, he's seen things. I've seen him play against Leeds twice where he's just got blown out of the pitch.

“They're working on building him up."

As for Estevao himself, Jacobs insisted the player remains happy at Chelsea despite his lack of minutes.



He added: "He's very happy. He's no trouble and is a very good trainer. Very good kid off the pitch and they're delighted with him.”

After Jacobs gave Chelsea fans reassurances over Estevao's future, South American football expert Tim Vickery was quick to remind them of the huge talent they have on their hands.

4 Estevao is considered the next Neymar, but Chelsea recently faced fears they could lose their Brazilian star Credit: AFP

Having previously dubbed the the 'next Neymar', he insisted the winger ranks ahead of some huge other Brazilian names.



Vickery declared on talkSPORT: "This includes Vinicius Jr and Rodrygo - I think he's the best talent to come out of Brazil since Neymar without any of the baggage."

Estevao joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 as one of the most highly-rated teenagers in world football, with Barcelona, Real Madrid and Arsenal among the other clubs chasing him.

But he picked the Blues - and in his first campaign, he impressed, having a hand in 12 goals in 36 games in all competitions.

So far this term though, he's not scored or assisted in the first nine matches, although his one league start only came against United.

Sports.title: Police launch murder investigation after death of footballer Ezekiel Williams
Sports.content:
Police have launched a murder investigation into the death of non-league footballer Ezekiel Williams.

Officers have arrested three men after Williams was allegedly attacked in Milton Keynes in the early hours of Sunday morning.

2 A murder investigation has been launched after Williams' death

The 26-year-old, who played for eight-tier Hendon, later died from his injuries.

Williams joined Hendon in September and recently scored his first goal for the club.

Thames Valley Police has now confirmed a murder investigation has been launched following his death.

Officers have arrested two men in their 20s on suspicion of murder, with a third man, aged 30, arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Thames Valley Police statement

In a statement, the force said: "Two men, aged 21 and 28, both from Luton, have been arrested on suspicion of murder.

"A third man, aged 30 and also from Luton, has been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. All remain in custody.

"Officers remain in the area and there will continue to be an increased police presence around The Hub and city centre while enquiries continue.

"A dedicated Major Crime Unit investigation is underway."

The investigation comes after a GoFundMe page was set up in Williams' memory.

Those who wish to support his family have been given the opportunity to make a donation.

2 Police have arrested three men after an alleged attack on Williams Credit: X @HendonFC

Meanwhile, Hendon's London Senior Cup tie against Woodford Town, which was scheduled for Wednesday, has been postponed.

Hendon pay tribute to Williams

In a post on social media, the club said: "We are stunned and heartbroken to announce the sudden and tragic passing of midfielder Ezekiel Williams aged 26.

"A humble, unassuming and generous individual with a razor-sharp wit.

"Eze joined the club in September and quickly established himself as a highly popular member of the dressing room.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with Ezekiel’s family, friends, and everyone who knew him at this devastating time.

"He will be very sadly missed by all of us at Hendon Football Club."

The midfielder scored his first goal for the club in a 4-2 home defeat to Jersey Bulls on October 24.

His last appearance for the Greens came three days later against Egham Town.

Sports.title: Revealed: How England's reunited 'Pom Squad' plan to dominate Australia at the scrum - as returning Will Stuart opens up about his 'insufferable' eight-month injury nightmare
Sports.content:
Revealed: How England's reunited 'Pom Squad' plan to dominate Australia at the scrum - as returning Will Stuart opens up about his 'insufferable' eight-month injury nightmare

During the dark nights of last winter, Will Stuart was sleepwalking around his house with a ruptured achilles. It was an unusual complication in the England prop’s recovery programme and one which left the national team’s medics with an unexpected problem to solve.

Stuart’s left achilles popped in a scrum during Bath’s victory over Munster in December. He was put on pain-relief gas to numb the sensation. ‘I had to wait two weeks for surgery and that purgatory period is the most annoying bit,’ Stuart told Daily Mail Sport.

‘I had a few nightmares. I sleepwalk occasionally and I managed to sleepwalk with no achilles to the other side of the house. After the operation, the physio insisted I sleep with a boot on or I could re-snap my achilles by sleepwalking into the bathroom!’

It was the beginning of an eight-month nightmare, as Stuart missed the entirety of the Six Nations and the summer. Now the tighthead is back, ready to face the Wallabies on Sunday.

South Africa reinvented rugby’s tactics with their ‘bomb squad’ of front-row forward replacements from the bench. Now England’s equivalent, the ‘pom squad’, is set to be reunited. With Fin Baxter also returning from a long-term foot injury, England can deploy their scrummaging reinforcements from the bench, creating a double punch combination with Ellis Genge and Joe Heyes.

‘We felt really connected as sets of front rows in that previous block,’ said Leicester’s Heyes, who is set to start at tighthead prop with Stuart his reserve. ‘There's a huge amount of confidence that whoever's going to come on is going to finish the job or vice versa. It was, “Brilliant, this front row is coming on now”. It's good to have those boys back. I know they've had really challenging journeys with two pretty tough injuries to have.’

Prop Will Stuart is set to return for England against Australia on Sunday following a nightmarish eight-month injury lay-off

England's 'Pom Squad' will be reunited, with Fin Baxter (back row, third from right) also back from injury. 'There's a huge amount of confidence that whoever's going to come on is going to finish the job,' says Joe Heyes (front row, right)

England will expect to find an upper hand against the Wallabies at the set-piece. Australia’s pack is a different beast without giant lock Will Skelton, meaning the hosts should dominate the power battle. Stuart’s 135kg frame adds significant forward momentum.

‘There's no secrets,’ added Heyes. ‘In international rugby, seconds can change a game. You have to be switched on all the time. You have to be mentally engaged all the time. There are times at our clubs where all the scrums are going down in training. Here our scrum has been staying up. There's a huge emphasis on getting into a contest and actually going at each other.’

Throughout the week, rugby’s leading referees have been gathered in Windsor, studying scrum footage ahead of the Nations Championship. There will be a clampdown on loosehead props tucking their shoulders, which can cause the scrum to overbalance and collapse. The sport’s lawmakers want to see more technical accuracy and Stuart’s experience will provide a significant boost.

England train their scrum man-on-man in live sessions, never against a machine to ensure they are prepared as best as possible.

‘The first scrum in training felt quite weird,’ admitted Stuart, who used the time on the sidelines to cut his weight, before returning for Bath at the start of the season.

‘I was pretty head down in the trenches. I geared everything towards getting back fit. I was probably quite insufferable to live with for about five months. My wife made a million cups of tea for me.

'I thought about getting a scooter but it wouldn't have been really worth it for me, because I've got quite a higgledy-piggledy house. I would have been scooting for two metres before I had to carry it over some steps. Instead, I got a peg leg that you can put on the end of your knee, so I became quite independent quite quickly.

‘You come off the crutches and then they put you in these elevated wedges. They gradually decrease the size of the wedge. As soon as I was back in normal shoes, walking fairly competently, we went out to visit some friends in Kenya which was amazing. Then it was back to the grindstone.

‘As soon as I got through the first scrum and my achilles didn't explode, I was fine. I had a couple of games in pre-season where I felt like Bambi on ice. Turning 30, I can’t just run out on the pitch and train the house down. It takes me about an hour and a half to get moving. I wanted to get back to that England level. With long-term injuries, the more you play, the more your body gets used to it.’

England will expect to find an upper hand against the Wallabies at the set-piece. The hosts should dominate the power battle and Stuart’s 135kg frame will help

Stuart in action against Australia at Twickenham in November 2024. The 30-year-old says 'it's good to be back'

Stuart helped England scrum coach Tom Harrison to analyse the Springbok pack in the summer. South Africa provide the set-piece benchmark for the rest of the world but, even in Stuart’s absence, England’s scrum has been one of their strongest assets this year.

‘I had a few conversations with Tom, especially going into that South Africa Test (which England lost 45-21 after a late flurry of South Africa tries),’ said Stuart. ‘We had a few back and forths about previous scrummaging experiences against Ox Nche or with Thomas du Toit.

‘The main thing that stands out, aside from them being fairly massive men, is that they are just very well drilled. Speaking to Thomas, they're very cohesive and they work very well as a unit. People look at a prop and think they’re very destructive. But when you have a very cohesive tight five, doing the same thing at the same time, it's very hard to stop.

‘I think England’s scrum has been an area where they’ve held their own. Tom pretty much let me off the leash for nine months. It’s good to be back now.’

Sports.title: LIV Golf relaunch collapses as $300M backers withdraw after last stars standing including Bryson DeChambeau refused to commit
Sports.content:
LIV Golf's relaunch looks set to collapse after BC Partners Credit decided to drop its $300 million backing of a new iteration of the league.

After losing funding from the Saudi Public Investment Fund, the league's 2026 season ended earlier than expected due to financial difficulties.

After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, the league looked to find a way to survive and launch 'LIV 2.0' without the Saudi riches.

BC Partners committed to investing around $300 million as long as certain conditions were met.

But they had a deadline to show it had enough player support for a 2027 league and, according to the Financial Times, has now shelved its backing due to a lack of player commitments.

According to the Sports Business Journal, a source said: 'None of the big names signed', later confirming that included Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Joaquin Niemann and Cameron Smith.

LIV Golf is set to wind down permanently after the $300M backer of 'LIV 2.0' withdrew funding

The Saudi Public Investment Fund pulled its massive funding in LIV Golf earlier this year

The Athletic adds that the league is now pivoting to a complete wind-down and shutting down LIV Golf entirely as BC Partners felt time had run out and it no longer believed it could form a viable league.

The liquidation process is expected to start in a New Jersey bankruptcy court on Thursday.

Numerous big names publicly declared they would not return in recent weeks, including Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia and more.

Only four players had publicly committed - Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland, Brendan Steele and Ben Campbell.

Speaking to Bunkered last month, BC chief, Ted Goldthorpe, said: 'The players are everything. They're our partners and they're very, very important to our future.'

Just this week, Bryson DeChambeau spoke publicly about the relaunch and said he hoped it could last 'forever' under new ownership

Speaking on the 'Figuring Out' podcast he said the new version can 'make full financial sense' as he acknowledged problems with the Saudi-funded model which shook up professional golf.

'The business model makes a lot of sense,' DeChambeau told host Raj Shamani. 'And we're actually working through that right now for this new model where it will make full financial sense.

Dustin Johnson is among the big names who was unwilling to commit to the new league plans

Jon Rahm was among the big names who recently said he would not be involved in LIV 2.0

'It's no funny business, no nothing. It's going to be done right. And this is going to be a league, hopefully, that exists forever.

'The point of it is that the team golf stuff, I was very excited about,' DeChambeau said. 'I really care, and I still do care deeply about the team golf stuff.

'And the top company just wasn't really managed that effectively. And I know that now... I didn't know that during the time.'

Sports.title: Como star pays touching tribute to Spanish footballer killed in fatal collision with goalkeeper as Cesc Fabregas' rampant side score NINE in Champions League thrashing of Lens
Sports.content:
Como star pays touching tribute to Spanish footballer killed in fatal collision with goalkeeper as Cesc Fabregas' rampant side score NINE in Champions League thrashing of Lens

Goalscoring Como playmaker Nico Paz paid his respects to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, following his death on Tuesday, during his side's Champions League thrashing of Lens.

Paz scored his side's third goal in their 9-1 romp at Lens on Wednesday night and during the celebrations marked his own tribute to De Miguel.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and he paid homage to his hometown club by holding a shirt aloft with a picture of De Miguel alongside a caption: 'Rest in peace'. Paz also spent time in Tenerife's youth system from 2014-16.

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Anastasios Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

It's another for Como, with Nico Paz firing them into a 3-0 lead against Lens ⚽️



He pays tribute to Jesús de Miguel after his goal ❤️ pic.twitter.com/OGyEPMnZlt — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 4, 2026

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 - Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline - as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Cesc Fabregas' side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

READ: Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer speaks out to reveal his 'enormous pain' and says he will 'face whatever comes' after police opened homicide investigation and fans called him 'murderer'

Sports.title: Scott Parker's baptism of fire: West Ham fight back from three goals down to earn draw at Cardiff in new manager's first match in charge
Sports.content:
Scott Parker's West Ham launched a thrilling comeback from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in his first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and the travelling fans were furious in the away end.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point for the new boss.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers manager on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked.

Nuno was axed after a run of poor performances and the club opted to bring in a familiar face, with Parker having made 129 appearances for them as a player between 2007-2011.

It was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Scott Parker took charge of his first West Ham game after Nuno Espirito Santo's sacking

Max Kilman is seen scoring the dramatic equaliser to make it 3-3 against Cardiff

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott into early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute. Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed. There was no reprieve for West Ham when Perry Ng curled a ball over a static defence after 36 minutes.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Cardiff had missed their last two spot-kicks, but this time Moylan was entrusted with the responsibility and sent Hermansen the wrong way.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Jarrod Bowen was a key man for the Hammers as they staged a remarkable recovery

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola blasts Liverpool stars for 'cheap and messy' defeat at Fenerbahce - and blames the NOISE inside stadium for second goal as Turkey curse continues
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola blasted his ‘cheap and messy’ side after they fell to a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce.

Former cult hero Dirk Kuyt was in the dugout as two Englishmen – Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown – scored for the Turkish giants to cancel out Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak’s strikes before Vedat Muriqi headed home a winner.

All three goals were avoidable but may have been due to the deafening atmosphere and Iraola said: ‘(They were) cheap goals. Messy goals.
