‘The free-kick is quite far out, through the wall. The last goal was a long throw, the second one Cody (Gakpo) touched the ball just in front of Alisson.

‘In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate, it was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication was difficult between Cody and Ali.’

Iraola also stressed his frustration with his team conceding three from set-pieces, saying: 'It's something that we were doing very well in the league, we were doing quite well until today.

'We knew it was one of the strengths of Fenerbahce. We concede from a free-kick, a corner and even from the long throw at the end.'

Tonight's loss was Liverpool's second in as many games but first in the Champions League this season

Vedat Muriqi's 79th minute header sealed the victory for Fenerbahce

Liverpool full-back Kostas Tsimikas also had some criticisms of the Reds defensive performance as he said: 'We didn't defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically, we conceded another goal. I think we have to mark better if we want to win games.'

Meanwhile Kuyt, who played 285 times for the Reds, said: ‘It was a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce. I have to give a very big compliment to the players and the staff who keep pushing them.

‘We told each other to stick together and be united. That’s something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against. We made a miracle tonight, not many expected us to win.’

It was Liverpool’s second straight defeat after the 1-0 reverse at home to Arsenal and the third Champions League game on the bounce where they have conceded three goals.

The result was also the third defeat in Istanbul in 13 months, extending Liverpool's miserable run in Turkey since their 2005 Champions League final heroics.

Iraola's side travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Sports.title: O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting
Sports.content:
Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, but it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

Sports.title: Alisson FUMES at Liverpool team-mate Jeremy Jacquet after Reds star turned his back and deflected Mason Greenwood's free-kick beyond goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Alisson is usually composure personified for Liverpool but lost his rag with Jeremy Jacquet on Wednesday night.

The Brazilian gave his team-mate both barrels after Fenerbahce's equaliser - a heavily deflected Mason Greenwood free-kick.

Jacquet was at the edge of the Liverpool wall and twisted his body to take evasive action, with the ball ricocheting off his midriff and past the goalkeeper.

Jacquet has been a shining light for the Reds in his debut campaign but it was a poor moment that left his stopper livid.

Replay footage showed Greenwood's powerful attempt appeared to be heading wide before the deflection off Jacquet completely changed the trajectory.

Alisson had been moving swiftly to his left before being wrong-footed and the ball flew off the wet surface to his other side.

Alisson was raging at Jeremy Jacquet's poor blocking attempt for the Fenerbahce equaliser

Jacquet's expression indicated he knew he'd made a poor mistake for the goal

The 34-year-old's fury was immediate and he screamed at Jacquet, gesticulating wildly in his direction.

The centre-back appeared to recognise his mistake and brought his hand up to cover his eyes on a grim evening in Istanbul.

On commentary for TNT Sports, Ally McCoist said: 'It's Jacquet and he's livid (Alisson), does he turn his back? He certainly does, you've got to face it.

'The goalkeeper is livid, absolutely livid and with justification as well. He's (Jacquet) is side on for someone who has had a good start to the season.'

Jacquet has been partnering Virgil van Dijk in almost every game so far this term for Andoni Iraola's men and acquitted himself excellently.

Having joined from Rennes in the summer for £55million after agreeing the move in January, he's seamlessly replaced Ibrahima Konate, who left on a free transfer before signing for Real Madrid.

Jacquet is still just 21 and the France international will no doubt want to avoid the ire of his goalkeeper and learn his lesson when it comes to forming a solid wall.

Trey Nyoni had opened the scoring for the Reds before Greenwood's leveller. Alexander Isak then came off the bench to give the visitors the lead once more before Fenerbahce roared back.

Two goals in the space of six minutes gave the Turkish side a 3-2 lead in the pouring rain, to the delight of interim boss and cult Liverpool legend Dirk Kuyt and the home side held on for a famous win.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres shows he still has an important part to play for Arsenal after starring role in win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta begins next phase of his masterplan, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
The next phase of Mikel Arteta’s season masterplan was seemingly underway: get the Arsenal frontline firing.

The plaudits for a defence which has conceded just eight goals across the Premier League and Champions League are well endorsed.

Yet, as Viktor Gyokeres was making a compelling case for challenging Kai Havertz’s spot, Arteta’s backline decided to have a temporary, rare malfunction.

By full-time Slavia Prague’s winless streak in the Champions League had reached 23 games — the joint-worst ever in the competition alongside AEK Athens, despite a late onslaught which momentarily caused the visitors jitters. Slavia boosted their shot count up to 17, compared to Arsenal’s 12. The north London club had taken their eye off the ball having reached half-time two goals up.

David Raya was called upon for a world-class save, using his full frame to dive and deflect Oskar Kubiak’s header onto a post.

Wiktor Nowak then pulled a goal back on 90 minutes from inside the area having collected substitute David Jurasek’s pass to tap home near the goalline.

Noni Madueke celebrates scoring the opener for Arsenal against Slavia Prague

Viktor Gyokeres netted the second for the Gunners with this curling effort

Nowak had another chance, as he went agonisingly close to a further Jurasek cross. Such laxness by Arsenal would be punished elsewhere in Europe, though they still remain unbeaten in the Champions League after four matches.

An annoyed Arteta said: ‘It was two very different halves. The first one, where we played at a really high level. It should have been three, four or five (goals).

‘Right from the beginning (of the second half), we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we had to do, in every concept.

‘I already mentioned a few things and some others that I will keep to myself.’

Even without William Saliba, who made the squad for the first time this season following a back injury sustained at the World Cup in July, the Gunners have usually been imperious in defence.

It’s their attack which has its fair share of holes, not helped by Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury and the lack of an in-form No9.

Yet, a bit of love and persistence can do wonders for a striker — and could be the antidote Arteta needs to rejuvenate Gyokeres, who caused Slavia a migraine with both his footwork and finishing.

Behind the Bane mask Gyokeres figuratively wears in his celebrations lies a man whose confidence has taken more than a knock or two.

Mikel Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend

Having struck 21 goals across all competitions last season, the Swede has largely occupied the bench in the current campaign.

Yet, the two pieces of play Gyokeres executed on a chilly Prague evening showcased just why he has an important part to play this season for Arsenal.

David Raya’s aerial punt accidently found its way to Gyokeres, following a defensive mishap, which the striker chested down.

MATCH FACTS: SLAVIA PRAGUE (4-2-3-1): Domchak 5; Vlcek 6, Holes 6, Zima 6, Kubiak 5; Moses 6, Sadilek 6; Ayaosi 5, Sulieman 5, Sturm 5; Nowak 7. Scorer: Nowak 89 ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 7; White 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Hincapie 6; Zubimendi 6, Rice 7; Madueke 7, Merino 7, Eze 7; Gyokeres 8. Scorers: Madueke 9, Gyokeres 38.

Instead of recycling the ball — an easier option for a man still finding his way — he went for the maverick option, producing a well-executed flick-on which found Noni Madueke. The winger reached the area, fending a defender off, before coolly slotting home.

Then before the break, Gyokeres had a goal of his own. After a neat one-two with Declan Rice, the Swede stormed into the box, before curling the ball in off the post from inside the area.

For all his deficiencies and limited chances thus far, the moment felt important for a striker who has now struck two goals and three assists in his past five appearances.

Havertz is Arteta’s No1, but one striker won’t be enough to properly sustain a campaign by which the league title and a first Champions League trophy in the club’s history are viable aims.

Even Madueke, enjoying a prolonged run on the right wing in Saka’s absence, was in inspired form.

Arteta made six changes to the Arsenal side that beat Liverpool at the weekend, with Merino earning a start on the ground where he exactly one year ago struck a second-half brace in Arsenal’s 3-0 victory against Slavia Prague last November.

Daniel Toula scored late on for Slavia Prague but they were unable to find an equaliser

Merino had his shot tipped over the bar after Madueke’s opener, the pressure already being felt by the home side.

Eberechi Eze went on a jinking run, featuring a nutmeg to the delight of the visiting fans, and it was all getting rather open.

The Gunners were close to going three goals up, Gabriel’s effort cleared off the line after Nazar Domchak spilled the ball.

Slavia suddenly came to life in the final minutes and had Arteta fretting on the touchline. An extraordinary turnaround was in sight.

Nevertheless, the form of Gyokeres will be a positive Arteta can take from a night not at his usual standards.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans blasted by club legend's son over behaviour towards the Glazers
Sports.content:
Man Utd fans blasted by club legend's son over behaviour towards the Glazers

Manchester United supporters have made their feelings clear towards the clubs' hierarchy

View 2 Images (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Kasper Schmeichel has rallied for Manchester United supporters to back their club. The son of former Red Devils shot-stopper Peter Schmeichel sympathises with the protests but highlighted the adverse impact it had on the squad.

‌



‌



United earned a much-needed win over AS Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday after coming from two goals down to beat the Serie A side. Michael Carrick's men were booed off after a tepid first-half before Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha (2) inspired a second-half fightback.

‌



The pressure is on Carrick after failing to replicate the form which earned him the permanent post at Old Trafford. The 45-year-old has maintained his place in the dugout despite defeats to Como, Bournemouth and Chelsea, but the key decision-makers continue to face pressure.

‌



Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel incident breaks silence as police launch investigation READ MORE :

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are the recent targets for criticism but fans are still fuming Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family's ownership.

However, former Leicester City and Celtic goalkeeper Schmeichel believes that the frustration being vented towards the United stewardship isn't helping matters on the pitch. He said on BBC 5Live: "I’d still be very tentative, particularly considering your next two games are Aston Villa and Liverpool.

"That’s a tough ask even if you’re on a good run. If you want to force a change, you have to a little bit get on the bandwagon to promote the positivity.

‌



"I like that the fans, they stayed. They could have gone at half time and been frustrated and missed the traffic, but I like the fact that they stayed.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"And once the first goal went in, that was enough to create the atmosphere. Now the fans have their chance to influence what’s going on on the pitch for the next game. Now they have the chance to go and back it up.

“I completely get wanting to protest and all of that, but like I say, for the players, it just doesn’t help. So now, if you want your team to do well – which I very much believe they do, nobody wants to come and watch their team lose – now it’s about doing exactly what they did second half. Backing the team the same way.

‌



“When things go wrong, let’s not get negative straight away. Put things into context sometimes. For example, you are coming up against a very good Aston Villa side.

View 2 Images Manchester United's Stretford End protested the club's owners (Image: PA)

‌



"So things can go wrong in games, but it’s about the reaction. Then, most of all, it’s the players’ responsibility to give the fans something. Give them something to cheer about and they will respond."

Tennis balls were thrown on the pitch before and during the win in Europe, meanwhile derogatory chants towards Wilcox and the United ownership emanated from the Theatre of Dreams.

‌



It forms part of the anger from United supporters, who believe their club has been the subject of mismanagement at senior level, as the club continue to struggle since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure 13 years ago.

There have been growing calls for figures like Wilcox or Berrada to face the music, with the director of football's only media appearance coming from club channels following a three-match unbeaten run.

Article continues below

However, Carrick remained tight-lipped when asked about it in October. He said: "I don't think that's for me to say. I've got no problem with how it is for me sitting here and talking to you guys."

Sports.title: Ally McCoist fumes over controversial Mason Greenwood incident during Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist fumes over controversial Mason Greenwood incident during Liverpool clash

Mason Greenwood was involved in a controversial incident during the early stages of Liverpool's Champions League clash against Fenerbahce

View 2 Images Mason Greenwood was controversially denied a penalty against Liverpool (Image: (Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP via Getty Images))

Ally McCoist was left stunned that Fenerbahce were not awarded a penalty for a foul on Mason Greenwood. After 20 minutes of Liverpool's Champions League clash against the Turkish giants, Greenwood was played through on goal, but a firm shove from Kostas Tsimikas knocked him off balance and prevented him from shooting.

‌



Claims for a penalty from Greenwood and the home support were waved away with VAR also failing to review the incident. Upon watching replays of the potential foul, McCoist was adamant that a penalty should have been given.

He said on TNT Sports: "It's a penalty, it's two hands, not even one hand. That prevents him for me getting a shot on goal. Both hands. I think it's a penalty, I really do. It's a shame because it's a great ball and an exquisite touch.

"I think so (got away with one), I really think so. He pushes him both hands when he's in the process of having an attempt on goal just because it doesn't look like it, doesn't make it not a penalty."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Liverpool went straight up the other end, and Trey Nyoni put them in front with a deflected effort which further angered Fenerbahce. However, Greenwood equalised moments later with his free-kick wrong-footing Alisson after a touch from a Liverpool player.

The set-piece from Greenwood appeared to be going wide but a stray touch from Jeremy Jacquet changed the trajectory of the ball ,which left Alisson fuming.

Analysing the goal, McCoist added: "He [Greenwood] gets a break doesn't he? I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall.

"Does somebody turn their back on it? It's the perfect answer. It's Jacquet and he's livid, does he turn his back? He certainly does, you've got to face it. The goalkeeper is livid, absolutely livid and with justification as well. He's (Jacquet) is side on for someone who has had a good start to the season."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was blamed for the goal Liverpool conceded to Fenerbahce

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Following Liverpool's opener, Fenerbahce dominated proceedings with Irfan Can Kahveci striking the bar before Greenwood's goal. The latter also went close with a left-footed effort from close range.

Greenwood arrived at Fenerbahce from Marseille this past summer in a €39million (£32.5m) deal. He had spent two years in France with a loan spell at Getafe coming before that.

The United academy product was free to join the La Liga club on a temporary basis after he was no longer in the plans of his boyhood club.

Greenwood was suspended by United when he was charged with attempted rape, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and controlling and coercive behaviour in 2022. He denied the charges, which were subsequently dropped, and later left the club permanently.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'

Matheus Cunha's late brace saw Manchester United see off Roma in the Champions League - with Rio Ferdinand demanding the Brazilian maintain that level

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand has laid out his demands for Matheus Cunha (Image: Getty Images)

Rio Ferdinand hopes that Matheus Cunha's match winning brace for Manchester United serves to kick on his career at Old Trafford as he concedes the Brazilian has not delivered enough.

‌



‌



Cunha is into his second year in Manchester having moved from Wolves for £62.5million, but has been part of a team that's been regularly criticised following a nine-game winless run. That was snapped with a comeback win over Roma on Tuesday night.

‌



Cunha scored twice in the final 10 minutes as United came back from 2-0 down to win 3-2, leading to huge celebrations at Old Trafford. The Brazilian was sent off in the final moments of the game, but Ferdinand still sees it as the benchmark going forward.

‌



Last term Cunha impressed in patches, scoring 10 times, but his display in midweek was his most defining in a red shirt to date and Ferdinand is now hoping for more.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said on his YouTube channel: "I think for Cunha this could be liftoff where he starts to catch fire,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel. ‘I think he’s a hugely talented footballer and he showed glimpses, especially last season.

"Could this be the game that unlocks him? Because I haven’t seen it enough yet with him. You see moments, and you go, 'Oh, look at that, that’s why we paid the big money for him', but not enough.

‌



"He needs to be watching back that performance and go, where were the fans feeding off me there? Where was I getting them going? Where was I getting the team and being the pressure point for the team? It was without the ball a lot of the time. And keep bringing that every game."

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was Man Utd's match winner on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Cunha has had to show his versatility this season with United's only genuine No 9, Benjamin Sesko, out injured. That has seen the ex-Wolves man having to lead the line on occasion.

The 28-year-old acknowledged their recent struggles, but maintained he needed to be the type of player who stood up when the chips were down.

‌



He said: “I think everything, when we tried to do it, being part of Man Utd is very hard because in these kinds of moments in the season, we know we always have these kinds of comparisons with the past. We need to have these kinds of games like today, and then we’ll pass the hard moment. But today was a blessed day for me.

“Being part of this, I have a responsibility. I always talk inside about that – I need to be this kind of guy – to have the responsibility in the hard moments and the good moments. I always need to show up and be there for nights like today.”

Sports.title: Arsenal star on Real Madrid radar as injuries and squad depth could force his hand
Sports.content:
Arsenal star on Real Madrid radar as injuries and squad depth could force his hand

Martin Zubimendi has struggled for minutes this season in an Arsenal team that is overflowing with quality and depth with Real Madrid long-term admirers of the Spaniard

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi has not yet been at Arsenal for 18 months, but questions are being asked about his future

Arsenal star Martin Zubimendi is struggling to catch a break at the Emirates with Real Madrid still long-term admirers of the midfielder.

‌



‌



The Spaniard, fresh off winning the World Cup in the summer, has struggled for minutes, which in part has owed to some untimely injuries. A fortnight ago he broke his nose after coming on as a substitute in a win over Everton. Prior to that, after the Gunners played Leeds on October 10, he sustained a knock in the warm down.

‌



Zubimendi was on Mikel Arteta's radar for several transfer windows before he eventually captured the midfielder from Real Sociedad, but he's far from a guaranteed starter nowadays.

‌



The 27-year-old's fall down the pecking order began last season when, despite being a regular for much of the season, he was dropped for the Champions League final as Myles Lewis-Skelly was preferred to face PSG.

‌



Arsenal's squad depth has been well documented, but inevitably there are players who will lose out as a result. In midfield Arteta currently has Declan Rice, who is an ever present, and the likes of Lewis-Skelly, Mikel Merino, Martin Odegaard and summer signing Bruno Guimaraes to compete with Zubimendi.

All six of Zubimendi's Premier League outings have come from the bench. Of his 10 appearances in all competitions he's only been a starter on two occasions.

‌



Arsenal's depth of quality could leave certain individuals wanting to move on in search of more minutes. Zubimendi has long been Real's radar, reports The Sun. That interest began when Xabi Alonso, who knew him from his time at Sociedad, was in charge.

View 2 Images The Spaniard is yet to start a Premier League game this season

Arteta has maintained that Zubimendi, who started 34 of the team's 38 league games last term, remains a player he values, but underlined the fact that there are plenty of players wanting opportunities.

“Martin is a very important player for us," he said. "He has been a bit unlucky with what happened with his ankle, with the nose afterwards. We have options in midfield and, like everybody else, he has to be ready.

“Everyone will have the chance to play, then it is about performing. His energy, his application, his will to help is unquestionable. He is an unbelievable player for us.”

Sports.title: Three men arrested after suspected murder of 'kind and talented' footballer, 26
Sports.content:
Three men arrested after suspected murder of 'kind and talented' footballer, 26

Three men have been arrested following the murder of Ezekiel Williams, the non-league footballer who died of his injuries after being assaulted in Milton Keynes

View Image Ezekiel Williams' death has resulted in three arrests (Image: Hendon)

Three men have been arrested following the suspected murder of a “talented” and “inspirational” non-league footballer, Thames Valley Police have said.

Ezekiel Williams, 26, of London, died from his injuries after an assault in the early hours of Sunday morning in Midsummer Boulevard, Milton Keynes.

Kettering Town FC, whom Williams joined for the 24-25 season, remembered him as a “talented, kind, and a truly inspirational individual” in a social media tribute after his “sudden” death. Detectives launched a murder investigation after Mr Williams died of his injuries in hospital on Monday.

Two men, aged 21 and 28 from Luton, have been arrested on suspicion of his murder. Another man, aged 30, also from Luton, has been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. All three remain in custody. Mr Williams was described online as a box-to-box midfielder, who also played for FC Romania, Northwood, and Harrow Borough.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Kettering Town FC’s tribute read: “Ezekiel showed great leadership qualities from the get-go at his time here and his humble approach made him a highly popular member of the dressing room.

“He was a talented, kind, and a truly inspirational individual who had his faith at the forefront of his heart, and this led him to be the wonderful young man that he was, someone whose warmth touched everyone lucky enough to know him, and whose example will continue to inspire us long after today.”

They added that a GoFundMe had been set up in his memory, and that he would be “sadly missed” by the footballing community.

Detective Inspector Rob Underhill, said: “Our thoughts are first and foremost with Ezekiel’s family and loved ones at this devastating time. Specially trained family liaison officers are supporting them as they come to terms with their devastating loss. We have made three arrests in connection with this investigation and do not believe that there is any wider risk to the local community.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“We are carrying out a thorough and extensive investigation to establish exactly what happened. We recognise this incident will cause concern within the local community. There will continue to be an increased police presence in and around The Hub and Milton Keynes city centre over the coming days, and I would encourage anybody with concerns to speak with our officers.

Article continues below

Police are appealing for anyone who was in the area of Midsummer Boulevard and The Hub between 1am and 2am on Sunday morning to come forward, along with any dash cam or CCTV footage from the area at time.

Anybody with information can contact 101 or report online quoting reference 43260570882, or report anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Sports.title: Inside the rise of Will Lankshear: Harry Kane and Alan Shearer comparisons as England squad beckons
Sports.content:
"Will Lankshear is as good a finisher as I've seen since Alan Shearer".

If you've started to hear the hype around Middlesbrough's record £20m striker, get ready for even more.

England manager Thomas Tuchel is reportedly sending one of his scouts to see if Lankshear can add to his 13 goals in 13 Championship games against Wrexham on Wednesday night, with Friday's England squad an outside possibility.

Pundits are already queuing up to make classic number 9 comparisons, with veteran EFL manager Neil Warnock heaping praise on the 21-year-old's "unbelievable, special finishing".

‌



Lankshear, who has 15 goals for Boro in all competitions this season, also scored on his England Under 21s debut in September.

And his Tottenham origins, predatory goalscoring instincts, and humble, hard-working personality are allowing commentators to make the obvious Harry Kane references.

How Michael Carrick channelled Sir Alex Ferguson to turn around 'embarrassing' Man Utd display READ MORE :

Lankshear missed Wednesday night's game with Wrexham ahead of the upcoming international break, but with the lack of up and coming English forwards behind Kane, could Lankshear eventually jump the queue and gatecrash Tuchel's Euro 2028 plans?

‌



'Baffling decision for Spurs to sell Lankshear'

Football London's Tottenham correspondent Alasdair Gold has described Spurs' decision to sell Lankshear as "baffling" and expects him to pass the 20-goal mark "within weeks".

Gold makes the stark contrast to Tottenham's underperforming forwards and says Boro fans must be "laughing at their fortune".

In fact, since joining the Boro, Lankshear has only scored one fewer goal than Tottenham have as a whole team.

Tottenham sporting director Johan Lange made the decision to cash in on Lankshear in the summer - reportedly £8-10m up front and the rest in add-ons.

‌



Gold said: "Lankshear's second goal in the victory against Charlton was reminiscent of a certain Ballon d'Or winner he looked up to in training.

"He will become a very good Premier League striker and it's mind-boggling that Spurs did not simply loan out a player who was not desperate to leave permanently, or even heaven-forbid, give him a chance to prove himself."

However, Gold says the north London club have matching rights on any future offers for Lankshear as well as a 20% sell-on clause that would benefit them regardless of whether they or another club signs him down the line. It is against the rules to have a buy-back clause with EFL clubs so that not an option.

'He had offers from bigger clubs'

After Middlesbrough manager Kim Hellberg arrived in November 2025, no team created more chances in the Championship - but no team in the Championship missed more big chances either. They needed an elite finisher to go again for Premier League promotion.

‌



In the summer, Hellberg, head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones drew up their transfer shortlist, with Lankshear described by one insider as a "dream" target.

The Spurs man had been a long-term target for Boro after they tracked his progress for many years. They tried to sign him in January, but he opted to honour his loan at Oxford.

Scott told Teesside Live: “We have to use our sales pitch. Someone like Will for example, he has a burning desire to be in the Premier League and play at the top level.

“I don't want to embarrass the lad but he had several opportunities that were financially a lot more rewarding for him. I would argue that some clubs were bigger because they were playing in Europe.

‌



“But he bought into this, really liked what we were about. He saw himself as a No.9 here and he's about feel. He gets a good feel Will, and the more time I spent with him you realise he's not flash, he's not looking for the biggest and best training ground."

Everyone at Boro has been blown away by just how successful he’s been so far.

‌



A one-touch finish expert

Lankshear's instinct in the penalty area is ‘elite’ already.

That might feel like a big claim given he’s only playing in the Championship, but that trait doesn’t really matter what division you’re in. Lankshear just has that knack of being in the right place at the right time, as shown by the fact that 10 of his 13 league goals have been one-touch finishes.

‌



Coaches I’ve spoken to say that instinct is hard to teach. Lankshear just has it.

Hellberg is a coach who focuses massively on individual development.

‌



Lankshear has yet to register an assist this season, and Hellberg has spoken a lot about working on other sides of Lankshear's game, in terms of his pressing and his back-to-goal stuff.

And it’s not just on the pitch where Lankshear has impressed. People behind the scenes at Boro talk of a young lad who’s mature and has his head screwed on, but is also humble too.

‌



He’s also said to be a really driven character, and obsessed with improving all the time. A typical centre forward, Hellberg and his team-mates have joked about his intensity in front of goal in training.

Hellberg added: "He even celebrates if he scores a small goal on a possession drill - he still celebrates all his goals with a fist. I think that's why he scores so many goals. Even if he touches the ball very few times in a game.

‌



"He's come here and is taking a massive development through the season. I think he was top from the first day in the box and how he finished, but he has increased his quality in the run-and-turn game.

"It comes from massive pressing. He has taken big steps, and he works so hard every day to improve, and that's what's taking him here. But at the end of the day, also having fantastic teammates that set it up in a brilliant way helps.

Team-mate Riley McGree jokes: “In training he loses his head when he doesn't finish and score! It's really good to see, because I can relate to that as well.”

This is a young player that’s been compared to fellow former Tottenham striker Harry Kane for many years. Even moving to Boro for a record fee brought with it attention and therefore pressure.

‌



He’s handled everything so far with class and maturity. Let's see what happens next.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino chosen for bonfire effigy as FIFA chief could be grilled on Trump links
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino chosen for bonfire effigy as FIFA chief could be grilled on Trump links

Gianni Infantino is clinging onto his position as FIFA president ahead of his re-election bid in March, but he remains the firing line following a series of controversies

View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino worked closely (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been selected as this year's effigy for an annual bonfire in Kent. The Edenbridge Bonfire Society unveiled Infantino's cartoon effigy ahead of their celebrations on Thursday.

‌



‌



The society explained that he'd been chosen for his 'string of decisions that have left their mark on the world of football in the wake of the World Cup'. Previous celebrity targets have included former UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer and US President Donald Trump, whose face is part the effigy.

‌



Infantino worked closely with Trump during the US-held Club World Cup in 2025 and this year's international edition. The FIFA chief could now face questions over his links to the Commander-in-Chief after the Democrat Party seized control of Congress at the midterm elections in the US.

‌



In July, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee confirmed that they'd launched an investigation into a 'sustained campaign' by FIFA and Infantino to curry favour with Trump. They also requested that Infantino submit documents and appear before the Committee.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



A spokeswoman for the Committee Democrats then said in September that Infantino and FIFA's level of co-operation with the investigation had been 'woefully inadequate'. The spokeswoman for the Committee Democrats also said on September 23 that staff had received a briefing on litigation relating to the FIFA bribery scandal.

She added: "FIFA has yet to turn over any priority documents requested by the committee - including those that would show how much money FIFA has given the Trump family - answer key questions around the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize or explain how the Kushner-Infantino scheme to sell off the World Cup was conceived."

‌



Two days after the Committee's investigation was launched, on July 28, The Times reported Infantino was developing a plan to sell stakes in a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors.

Later the same day, FIFA confirmed the proposal was that FFE should run the commercial interests of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions, and that the leader of the private investor group would be Thrive Capital. Thrive was founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

‌



Should Gianni Infantino resign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is this year's bonfire effigy in Kent (Image: Gareth Fuller/Press Association)

‌



The FFE plan was rejected by three continental confederations, including European football's governing body UEFA, which threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments unless the plan was abandoned. Infantino announced the idea had been withdrawn on August 1.

UEFA nevertheless said it had 'lost confidence' in Infantino over the affair and has pledged to identify a candidate to stand against him in next year's FIFA presidential election, though nothing has been announced so far with two weeks to go until the deadline for candidacies to be submitted.

‌



Infantino appears to have strong support for re-election in Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. Campaign group FairSquare has called on national associations to challenge Infantino’s eligibility to stand for a fourth term.

FIFA's statutes say no person may serve as president for more than three terms, but on the eve of the 2022 World Cup final it was announced FIFA Council had taken the decision to discount Infantino's first term between 2016 and 2019, leaving him free to run again in 2027.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
