In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out
Sports.content:
Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, 19, has been identified as the innocent bystander fighting for life after being shot in the head and neck outside a Queensland pub.

She remained in a critical and unstable condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital on Monday afternoon. Metro South Health confirmed the teenager is still fighting for life in the intensive care unit.

The teenager was active on social media just hours before the shooting. She and her partner were seen lip syncing to Justin Bieber's Daises in a video posted on Saturday afternoon.

Four people were wounded outside Fitzy's Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on Saturday night, while more than 100 spectators, including families with young children, attended the Logan City Titles boxing event.

Phil Austin, from the Australian National Boxing Federation Queensland, categorically rejected suggestions it was a bikie or organised crime attack targeting the boxing.

Austin was in the venue's foyer when the shots erupted.

'The wider community is questioning how can this happen in Logan?' Queensland Police Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said on Monday.

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau remains critically injured after suffering gunshot wounds to her head and neck

Vision of bullet marks on a mirror after four people were shot outside Fitzy's Loganholme during a boxing event on Saturday night

Boxing official Phil Austin was in the foyer when shots erupted, with flying glass striking his arm

'That's a popular local pub, a well-respected institution. That location had children, teenagers, mums and dads at that sporting event.'

Taskforce Maxima is a specialist Queensland Police squad that investigates outlaw motorcycle gangs and serious organised crime.

It is assisting Logan CIB and State Crime Command, which are jointly leading the investigation into the Fitzy's Loganholme shooting.

But Austin told Daily Mail that speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime was 'people putting two and two together and getting five'.

'I haven't seen any reputed organised crime figures at a fight show in this country in years,' he said.

'Bikies used to go to events, but since the government changed their laws, you just don't see them.'

Austin said he did not recognise any of the victims and could not say whether they had been attending the boxing.

'I don't even know if they were there to watch the boxing,' he said.

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) remained in the intensive care unit on Monday afternoon

Austin rejected speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime

'There's more than just boxing happening at that pub.'

He said no fighters or trainers appeared to have been involved and challenged assumptions that the boxing event itself had been targeted.

'We just happened to be there,' he said.

'It could have been the flower arranging show. It's just the fact that we were there.

'We have no idea why what happened happened. The only thing that we know for sure is it's a tragedy.'

Austin said he had just finished seeing a fighter and left the room being used as the dressing rooms near the venue's front doors when the shooting began.

'I'm in the foyer. I've got maybe a couple of metres, and then there's just a series of shots very, very quickly,' he said.

'We're talking about five or six shots in that or less seconds.'

Police say shots were fired from a Mitsubishi's front passenger window near the venue's drop-off area

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside the vehicle, according to police

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) had shared a video lip syncing to a Justin Bieber song just hours before the shooting

Flying glass struck the back of his arm.

'I was wearing a long shirt. Nothing hurt, but it just sort of reinforced me like, okay … this is happening,' he said.

'Before I could sort of basically say to myself, 'Oh crap,' it's over.'

Austin saw a car with its lights on but did not see anyone get out.

'It was my impression that they were actually still in the car,' he said.

Police said a Mitsubishi approached the passenger drop-off area during an intermission and shots were fired from its front passenger window.

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside.

Austin went to alert his crew in the boxing hall at the rear of the venue, away from where the shots had been fired.

Three men aged 27, 37 and 38 remain in hospital with serious injuries but are improving, police said

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting

'Then people's reactions start to kick in, and there's a bit of pandemonium, really, a lot of very, very angry people,' he said.

'They used the boxing room, basically, like a safe haven for everybody.'

Patrons began leaving through the back as hotel staff and security marshalled the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said everyone who witnessed the violence would carry some trauma from the night.

'This could have been your family member,' she said.

'This was a random group of people at the front of a popular hotel that became victims.'

The three other victims, men aged 27, 37 and 38, all suffered gunshot wounds to their abdomens. The 38-year-old was also shot in the arm.

All three remained in serious conditions on Monday but were improving, Adams said.

Police have not confirmed whether the men knew one another.

Police believe the attack involved pre-planning but say it remains premature to speculate about gang or organised crime involvement.

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting.

CCTV from nearby homes showed its occupants being collected by another vehicle after the car was torched. Police believe one of those involved may have suffered burns or another injury.

A ute was also found burnt later that night, with investigators still examining whether it was connected.

Adams urged anyone who knew or suspected who was responsible to come forward.

'There will be people out there who know who did this or suspect who did this,' she said.

For Austin, who has a son the same age as the critically injured teenager, the shooting has hit particularly hard.

'I've got a son her age, so it's really, really hit home hard,' he said.

He offered the federation's support to the victims, their families and friends.

'This is an awful, awful time for everyone,' he said.

'Let's just hope this girl recovers. It's just awful.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia

Conor Benn has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn was stopped in the second round of his world title challenge against Garcia in Las Vegas, with a brutal right hand sending the Briton crashing to the canvas before the American finished the job.

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old.

But he appears to have an unexpected opponent in mind.

Benn took to social media to share a fight poster featuring himself and McGregor, accompanied by the caption: 'Benn vs McGregor coming soon, 2027'.

He added to the speculation by responding: 'Any day of the week.'

Conor Benn (pictured above) has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia

Benn is understood to be interested in making the fight happen and is expected to explore potential terms with the Irishman.

Benn has previously been tipped to face McGregor in a lucrative crossover bout, with boxing legend Roy Jones Jr suggesting that the fight would make sense.

He said the crossover bout would be one of two major paydays for the Brit before he considers bringing his career to a close.

Jones also suggested such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn.

The prospect would offer Benn the chance to headline another major event without the pressure of a world title being on the line, while a fight against McGregor would attract an audience well beyond traditional boxing fans.

McGregor is one of the biggest names in combat sports, having become a global superstar during his time in the UFC before stepping into the boxing ring to face Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

The Irishman is also coming off a difficult period of his own, having suffered a fresh setback on his return to the Octagon against Max Holloway.

A fight with Benn would undoubtedly attract huge attention, although there is no indication yet that the pair are close to agreeing a deal.

Roy Jones Jr has said such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn

Benn's call-out comes after a brutal night in Las Vegas, where his hopes of becoming a world champion were ended in devastating fashion.

The British fighter had talked up his chances of upsetting Garcia, but the American's speed and power proved too much.

Garcia caught Benn with a vicious right hand in the second round, dropping him heavily to the canvas. Benn managed to get back to his feet, but Garcia immediately went on the attack again, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in after just one minute and 25 seconds of the round.

It was a crushing result for Benn, who had worked his way back into contention following his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Benn lost their first encounter by decision in April 2025 before getting his revenge with a points victory in November.

He subsequently returned to welterweight to challenge Garcia for the WBC title, but the American proved a step too far on the night.

The defeat also raised fresh questions about Benn's future at 147lbs, with making the weight having been a talking point in the build-up.

After the fight, Benn admitted he was unsure what came next and spoke about the sacrifices his boxing career had demanded of his family.

Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old

He made it clear that spending time with his children was his immediate priority, leaving his next move uncertain.

A lucrative showdown with McGregor would offer a very different route back into the spotlight from another world title challenge.

McGregor, meanwhile, has endured his own difficult return to competition.

The former two-weight UFC champion had been out of action since breaking his leg during his trilogy fight with Dustin Poirier in July 2021.

His long-awaited comeback against Holloway was supposed to mark the start of a new chapter, but things quickly went wrong.

McGregor injured his knee after attempting a jumping kick in the opening seconds of the fight. Unable to continue, he was forced to withdraw after just 69 seconds, handing Holloway the victory.

The result was a frustrating setback for the Irishman, whose return had generated enormous interest among UFC fans.

McGregor subsequently announced plans to undergo surgery, leaving his immediate and long-term future uncertain once again.

McGregor's long-awaited comeback ended in disaster at UFC 329 in Las Vegas (above)

The Irishman blew his knee out after throwing a kick within the first seconds of the bout

At 38, he remains one of the most recognisable figures in combat sports, but another comeback will depend on his recovery and whether he can return to full fitness.

A boxing match with Benn would be a different proposition from another UFC appearance, though it would still require McGregor to make a significant commitment to training and preparation.

McGregor is no stranger to a crossover fight.

His most famous venture outside MMA came in August 2017, when he faced Floyd Mayweather in one of the most heavily promoted boxing matches of all time.

McGregor had never competed in a professional boxing bout before, but that did little to dampen interest in the contest.

The pair embarked on an extraordinary promotional tour, trading insults in front of huge crowds as the fight became a global spectacle.

McGregor made a competitive start, but Mayweather quickly took control before stopping him in the 10th round.

Mayweather improved his professional boxing record to 50-0, while McGregor returned to the UFC having secured a huge payday and further cemented his status as one of sport's biggest commercial attractions.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'
Sports.content:
Aussie boxing legend Jeff Fenech hospitalised as he faces fresh new health battle: 'He's always a fighter'

Australian boxing legend Jeff Fenech has been hospitalised with heart problems, with his NRL star son-in-law Bradman Best revealing the family’s concern ahead of his Kangaroos debut.

The four-weight world champion, 62, was admitted to Strathfield Private Hospital around 10 days ago after suffering severe fatigue, breathing difficulties and feeling unwell.

Fenech has since had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests to investigate whether a potentially life-threatening staph infection has returned.

A recurrence has not been confirmed.

Best, who has a baby daughter with Fenech’s daughter Kayla, disclosed the hospital stay while discussing the boxing great’s influence on his career.

The Newcastle centre is preparing to make his Australian Test debut against Fiji on Sunday, but took time to acknowledge Fenech’s health battle.

Jeff Fenech, 62, has been hospitalised after suffering heart problems, fatigue and breathing difficulties

Bradman Best paid tribute to his father-in-law ahead of his Australian Test debut

Fenech has reportedly had a blood clot removed from his wrist and undergone tests for a possible recurrence of a serious infection

‘Jeff has been massive for me, I just want to give a quick shout-out to him,’ Best said.

‘He’s actually in hospital at the moment.

‘I’m thinking of him. He’s tough, he’s always a fighter.’

Best said Fenech had become an invaluable source of advice as he worked towards representing Australia.

‘Jeff has done a lot for me in my career,’ he said.

‘I was visiting him last week and he’s always giving me tips on what to do and how to be better.

‘It’s special having a father-in-law like that who’s a four-time world champion.

‘He’s an icon in Australia and it’s special having a bond like that with him.’

Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his world-title clash with Erislandy Lara have been disrupted by his trainer’s hospitalisation

Fenech became one of Australia’s greatest boxers, winning world titles across four weight divisions during a career that earned him the nickname ‘The Marrickville Mauler’

Asked whether Fenech’s condition was serious, Best remained hopeful.

‘Yeah, he will be right. He’s always a fighter. He’s been in there with a few heart problems and stuff, but he’ll be good.’

The hospitalisation has also interrupted Tim Tszyu’s preparations for his planned WBA middleweight world-title clash with Erislandy Lara.

Fenech became Tszyu’s head trainer in July, helping guide him to a unanimous decision victory over American star Errol Spence Jr.

Tszyu credited the veteran trainer with helping inspire that result, which set up his pursuit of a world championship in a second weight division.

With Fenech sidelined, fellow trainer Basil Nassis has taken charge of Tszyu’s work in the gym.

The Lara bout is expected to take place in Australia in November or December, according to the reports.

Fenech hopes to recover in time to be involved, although the Telegraph reported he is unlikely to perform padwork during the build-up.

The latest scare follows two major heart operations.

In October 2019, Fenech underwent emergency open-heart surgery in Thailand while preparing Jack Brubaker for a fight against Tszyu.

He needed another six-hour open-heart operation in 2024 during a serious infection.

Sports.title: British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE

'Bring him on,' roared Daniel Dubois when asked if he would like a third fight against the greatest boxer of his generation who has beaten him twice.

Oleksandr Usyk, who is in a state of limbo somewhere between vacating all the heavyweight tiles and semi-retirement, is a genius so may not fall readily into the trap baited on the banks of the Thames in the dark hours of this Sunday morning.

Ukraine's war hero will have watched Dubois annihilate the gallant Fabio Wardley and recognised that Dynamite Daniel is no longer the callow youth he wiped the canvas with a couple of times during his reign as the undisputed world champion.

Promoter Frank Warren is not given to understatement but when he said 'Daniel has matured now' he was only scratching the surface of the transformation.

It may be a stretch to compare Dubois with the once terrifying Sonny Liston but to those rivals wearing the other belts he needs if he is to become undisputed then he is starting to look like a monster.

'I want them all,' said WBO champion Dubois. He was referring to the winner between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December, who will thereby hold a WBA title, as well as IBF and WBC champions Filip Hrgovic and Ajit Kabayel.

Daniel Dubois knocks down Fabio Wardley during his annihilation on Saturday night

Dubois has declared himself ready to fight anyone in the heavyweight division

Their availability, especially that of AJ or the Gypsy King, will be determined no doubt by there being many more millions in the Aladdin's Cave from which Saudi Arabia has helped finance the welcome flux of mega-fights of late.

If so then Warren is promising a 2027 bursting with monthly heavyweight spectaculars as lustily anticipated as Dubois' second demolition of Wardley . At the rapid conclusion of which another packed O2 crowd was switching its allegiance from a love affair with Fabio's romanticised emergence from white collar boxing to realisation that Britain has a world beater in the ascendancy.

One who may be growing, also, into more of a box office star than the monosyllabic Liston ever was. If his accurate bravura prediction of a 'bash and smash' slaughter of Wardley and his most jovial media conference yet which followed are anything to go by.

Having nursed his confidence in the Dubois family cocoon Daniel now has a mansion of his own to live in and a selection of race cars to drive. No more Mister Shy Guy but none the less likeable for that.

The transition to full manhood was rounded off over the two fights with Wardley. This included recovery from two early knockdowns in the first Fight Of The Year battle to a brutal 11th round stoppage victory.

And now the onslaught triggered by a staggering right hand blow only 17 seconds after the first bell which imposed an eight count on the ropes. Followed by an overwhelming TKO in round two. Wham, bam and thank you man. No criticism this time of a delay in calling it off. In flew the white towel, in jumped referee Steve Gray.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua fight each other in December - and Dubois wants the winner

There has been some nagging at the edge of Dubois' triumph. Suggestions that Wardley came back too soon after the second-half beating in May. But if five-and-a-half months is not sufficient time to recover then how long would be? The immortal Joe Louis used to fight once a month, for heaven's sake.

Wardley, honest man that he is, blamed himself. Having lived to fight another day he vows to do better enough to launch a comeback campaign for another world title. Meanwhile Dubois, at 29 last month, heads for the stratosphere as champion of the next generation of heavyweight boxing.

As the new monster of the prize-ring? It took The Greatest Of All Time to stop the Liston beast In his awesome tracks. Might Usyk be the Muhammad Ali in waiting for Dubois? Maybe. Perhaps not since he is the older legend now. It would be fascinating finding out.

The tombstone on Sonny Liston's grave in Las Vegas describes him simply as A MAN. Frank Warren is right about Dubois becoming exactly that.

Sports.title: Liverpool FC owners emerge as potential buyers of Cadillac F1 shares amid TWG uncertainty
Sports.content:
Fresh doubts have emerged over the future of Cadillac Formula 1's majority ownership amid reports Mark Walter's TWG Global is looking to offload some of its shares - with Liverpool FC owner Fenway Sports Group said to be among the interested parties.

US billionaire Walter and his companies are the subject of a federal probe by the U.S. Department of Justice, investigating whether Walter's insurance companies, including Delaware Life Insurance Company, Clear Spring Life and Annuity, improperly invested policyholder funds in affiliated businesses. The transactions reportedly involved are around $20 billion in loans and investments that allegedly were not adequately disclosed.

Some of those funds were allegedly used to expand Walter's burgeoning sports empire, which at one point included the LA Dodgers baseball team, LA Lakers basketball team, a minority stake in football club Chelsea, and the LA Sparks WNBA team. TWG Global has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

TWG Global is also the parent company of TWG Motorsports, which majority owns the Cadillac F1 team as well as its NASCAR, IndyCar, IMSA and Australian Supercars squads. The Cadillac brand's parent company General Motors also holds an undisclosed minority share in the F1 team as it supplies infrastructure and personnel, and is developing future power units.

Why Cadillac F1 could be next on the chopping block

Walters has already moved to sell the Lakers and his 12.8% share in Chelsea, and the LA Sparks are also up for sale. Sports business website Sportico has now reported that Walter is also looking to offload part of his majority stake in the Cadillac F1 team, valuing the team at around $3billion.

The Washington Post has reported that one of several interested parties is John Henry's Fenway Sports Group, which owns Liverpool FC and the Boston Red Sox baseball team. FSG recently sold 38% of its stake in Liverpool, and already has a presence in motorsports as a 50% shareholder of the RFK Racing team in NASCAR.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

While TWG Global initially dismissed suggestions it could sell part of its F1 team, there are plausible reasons why it could be the next asset up for sale if Walter is forced to replace the related-party loans in question with fresh capital.

Walter’s group, Guggenheim Baseball Partners, purchased the LA Dodgers for $2.15 billion in 2012 out of bankruptcy court.

Lucrative local TV rights and a swell of popularity and sponsorship income overseas in the wake of signing Japanese superstar Shohei Ohtani, has seen the club become the first baseball franchise to reach 1.1 billion gross revenue in 2025. That has elevated the Dodgers into the same stratosphere as the world's biggest sports franchises like Real Madrid, FC Barcelona and the Dallas Cowboys NFL team.

As its valuation soared to around $7.8bn, according to Forbes, while it won back-to-back World Series championships in 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers team is Walter's goose with the golden eggs, so it is likely the last top-tier sports asset TWG will cling on to.

The Cadillac F1 team is in a very different position, having only joined the series this year after a protracted entry process. Having paid a $450m anti-dilution fee for the right to join as an 11th expansion team, TWG Global and its partner General Motors have reportedly been pouring resources understood to be north of $1bn into building up the team, which includes state-of-the-art headquarters both in Silverstone in the UK and in Fishers, Indiana.

Cadillac has had a reasonable start to life as an F1 team, with relatively respectable performances for a start-up team marred by subpar reliability, but its road to become a successful F1 team is still a long-term proposition.

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Meanwhile, F1's popularity boom and its budget cap has meant team valuations have soared in recent years, with the top teams now turning profits.

Paired with the scarcity of a closed 11-team grid, that franchise system has led to an inflated figure of $3bn for a currently uncompetitive team, albeit one with significant infrastructure assets and GM backing.

TWG Global has been contacted for comment, while GM representatives declined to comment on the recent reports.

Sports.title: Ocon's F1 story is one of success, even if this is the end
Sports.content:
There's really not much reason to think otherwise: it looks increasingly likely that this could be the end of Esteban Ocon's active Formula 1 career. A career blessed with plenty of highlights, a handful of podiums and a victory scored behind the wheel of a car that wasn't capable of winning on merit.

He made a lot of the opportunities that came his way - not just on the track, but throughout his career. And even if it ends now, that career has already become far more than anyone could reasonably have expected, given where he started.

There aren't many stories like his in modern F1, with kids from modest backgrounds - without wealthy families or rich sponsors behind them from an early age - reaching the pinnacle of motorsport, let alone achieving what Ocon has managed.

But his abrupt departure from Haas could well mark the end of that chapter of his racing career. Things could change. He could still return, because he's still one of the best drivers in the world. It's just very difficult to see how right now.

It's almost impossible to imagine Ocon on the grid when the 2027 season begins in Bahrain - if it begins in Bahrain - with most seats already taken and those potentially still available having plenty of candidates queuing up for them. And there's little reason to believe he'd suddenly jump ahead of the others.

There's still a question mark over Cadillac's second seat. But there's Colton Herta, with his American passport, and Yuki Tsunoda as another possible option. Liam Lawson's future hasn't been confirmed either, but Red Bull isn't suddenly going to add a 30-year-old Frenchman to the pool of candidates for its junior team. That's essentially a fight between Lawson and 19-year-old Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov.

What's more likely is that Ocon would once again have to find a place on the substitutes' bench, waiting for an opportunity until somebody slips in the shower.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

And there are plenty of examples of drivers who have eventually made it back after choosing that route. Even on the current grid, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Nico Hulkenberg are examples. Ocon himself belongs in that group: he returned to racing with Renault in 2020 after spending a year on the sidelines as Mercedes' reserve driver.

But, as uncomfortable as the truth may be, the way Ocon's 2026 season ended so suddenly makes the prospect of a comeback even less likely than it would have been had he simply finished the year with Haas.

There's no point speculating about what actually happened between him and the team. And it would be wrong to give more visibility to the rumours flying around.

What we do know is that something happened during the Mexico Grand Prix weekend. And whatever it was, it was enough for Haas to take Ocon out of the car and hand it to Ryo Hirakawa, a driver with no previous F1 starts, who made his grand prix debut at the age of 32 - something we hadn't seen since Andre Lotterer jumped into a Caterham at Spa in 2014.

Whatever happened, it was serious enough not only for Haas to sideline him for the weekend, but also to decide that he wouldn't race for the team again this season.

Yes, perhaps the situation was also convenient for Haas. It now has an opportunity to give Rafael Camara, its future driver, some actual race experience. That will certainly be useful for the Brazilian, but also for the team, which can identify areas to work on, get to know him better and benefit from all the other things that come with running a young driver in a grand prix.

But Haas wouldn't have shown Ocon the door just for that.

When a driver disagrees with his team, it's certainly not ideal. When it gets to the point where the team takes him out of the car, it's worse. And when the driver in question is Esteban Ocon, it's difficult not to talk about his reputation and see Mexico 2026 as another stain on it.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Reputation is a tricky thing.

It's often formed according to its own rules, through freak circumstances and, nowadays, through the mystery of social media algorithms. When there's something to hate, the modern world provides more than enough tools to multiply the effect, exaggerate it beyond recognition and turn the whole thing into a farce.

But reputation exists. And Ocon has a reputation for being a somewhat difficult character to work with.

After all, his previous spell with a team ended in a remarkably similar way, with Alpine asking him to vacate his cockpit before the end of the 2024 season.

And then there's the whole outcry over his collisions with team-mates.

It's not actually as bad as the social media hate suggests, and many of those incidents weren't even his fault. If you go back and look at the incidents themselves, the picture isn't nearly as clear as the usual social media reaction would have you believe.

But it is what it is. And it's also true that anyone considering Ocon as a future driver will inevitably have that preconception about him - however fair or unfair it may be.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team, Laura Mueller, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

There's a puzzling disconnect between that image and the person we see in interviews.

Believe it or not, Esteban Ocon is one of the nicest people in the F1 paddock to talk to. Friendly, chatty, very polite. Yet there are enough people who would tell you that he can be difficult to deal with at times.

We talked about it when I interviewed him for GP Racing magazine a couple of years ago. We'd visited him at his training centre in the south of France and then had a long conversation in the car on his way home to Geneva.

I told him that a sporting director from an F1 team had once described Ocon to me as one of the most brutal guys when it came to discussions in the stewards' room.

I asked whether he thought that was part of his character. And he agreed that he understood what people might be talking about.

"But yeah, when there's something that has to be said, especially in Formula 1, it has to be said," he told me back then. "We have no time to waste here. So, it's important to be straightforward. Maybe I'm too straightforward at times, but well… I'm not going to let anything go after I've worked so hard to get where I am. You see how many hours I put in every day here - and I don't want to get, you know, eaten alive by doesn't matter who it is, be it some team manager, team principal, or a world champion.”

And we talked about how that part of his character was perhaps formed in the early days of his career, when his future depended not only on results but also on his ability to stand his ground and be as pushy as necessary to secure support.

Esteban Ocon, Alpine F1, celebrates on the podium Photo by: Jerry Andre / Motorsport Images

His family had sold their house to fund his karting career, but they simply couldn't provide enough money for him to progress through the junior formulas.

He needed to be a fighter, because nothing was handed to him.

And you've got to admire that - just as you've got to admire his whole journey.

“That's probably the right way to put it: I had the weight of my family on my shoulders, from a very young age,” he said. “And I’m not saying it to seek pity: it was worth trying and we succeeded to end up where we wanted to be - and now everything is good. But it's clear that I had to deal with these sorts of pressures, I had to be tough when it mattered, and I had to be heard when people were not necessarily listening, or weren’t convinced. And, you know, to make these businessmen, investors listen to you, when you're 13 or 14, and really pay attention, is not easy.”

It's probably not right to look at this as though it has now become a problem for him in Formula 1. Because he made it this far thanks to being who he is. And a decade-long career at the pinnacle of motorsport, with a grand prix victory to his name, is something nobody will ever take away from him.

As sad as it may be, perhaps that's simply all there was for Ocon in Formula 1.

There's a certain irony in the fact that what could turn out to have been Ocon's final F1 weekend as a race driver was also the weekend Kimi Antonelli won the world championship with Mercedes.

Because Ocon was once Toto Wolff's favourite kid, too. Wolff even said it was only a matter of time before Esteban would drive for the Silver Arrows.

It was never meant to be. And perhaps there was a reason for that, too.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Chris Graythen / Getty Images

Ocon is undeniably fast. You don't have a 10-year career in F1 without being fast, let alone win a grand prix. But Formula 1 is also Formula 1. And only the absolute best, with the complete package required to reach championship level, actually get there.

There's no denying that, in terms of pure speed, there are far more drivers capable of winning a world championship than there are actual world champions. There's luck. There are circumstances, which play a huge role in how careers develop. And some of those things simply didn't fall into place for Ocon. Or perhaps his complete package wasn't convincing enough at the right moments - for Wolff, for example, to put him in a Mercedes when the opportunity arose.

After all, Ocon was available when Lewis Hamilton decided to leave for Ferrari. But by then, Toto already had a new favourite kid.

And he was ultimately proven right.

Whatever happens next, even if Ocon never finds his way back onto the grid, there's no reason to look back at his career with pity or regret. Because the career he's had is one that thousands of drivers would give almost anything to have. It's a bit sad - and even silly - that it could end like this. But it's certainly not what he deserves to be judged on.

And also...

As difficult as it looks now, even if it seems impossible, we're talking about someone who's already made an impossible dream come true: a kid from a small French town, whose dad was a mechanic, making it all the way to F1.

Don't count him out just yet.

And whatever happens next, he deserves to be praised for what he's already achieved.

Sports.title: Mercedes takes blame for Russell's poor Mexico GP: "We let him down"
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has admitted to ‘letting George Russell down’ at Formula 1’s Mexico Grand Prix, with the Briton’s bid for victory derailed within seconds by a technical issue.

Russell was starting from the front row alongside Lewis Hamilton at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, and his initial getaway was good enough to retain that position and take the polesitter’s slipstream, but his Silver Arrow encountered an energy deployment issue.

By the time he got to Turn 1, Russell was down to sixth. A few corners later, he was attacking Isack Hadjar but failed to back out going into Turn 6 and tapped the Red Bull into a spin, landing a 10-second penalty.

As a consequence, Russell was sixth again by the time the red flag was waved for Valtteri Bottas’ hefty crash, as the penalty dropped him behind Lando Norris, and he failed to make any inroads during the second part of the race.

After the chequered flag, the 28-year-old congratulated team-mate Kimi Antonelli for his world title but did not stick around; Mercedes excused him from his media duties, landing a €5,000 fine from the FIA.

“I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he's distraught about the situation,” Wolff said. “It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi. I have known George for such a long time and I know for a racing driver this is a catastrophic moment.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car and we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we have thought it should be.

“I'm very much with him, at the moment. I've been in situations where he's very difficult to cope. Him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me. That's absolutely honoured.”

This wasn’t the first time a lack of energy deployment caused trouble for Russell; it also happened at Spa-Francorchamps down the Kemmel Straight, leading to a collision with Hamilton. The Briton retired on the post.

Russell was also struck by other mechanical problems, notably power unit failures that caused retirements from the lead in Canada and third in Malaysia.

“Definitely he has had bad luck at some point in the season,” Antonelli admitted when asked if Russell would ‘give him a big push’ in 2027. “He has had a little bit more than me, being honest. I've also had my moments in Silverstone and Barcelona. Also, after Silverstone, we had to trash our new PU because it had a problem in it, and we had to take an earlier penalty, which was in Monza.

“Definitely, we've had our bad moments, but still, he will definitely come back. You know, he's super quick. He has shown this season that when he's on it, it's very hard to beat.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

“So it's just about, you know, on my side, keeping focused on myself, keep trying to raise the bar, keep improving, keep developing, because I think it's not going to be only a matter of George at the end of this season, but also for next season, Red Bull, especially with Max [Verstappen], Ferrari and McLaren, eventually, we're all going to be up there, and it's going to be a tight fight. So, it's going to be important to be on top of the game, not only against my team-mate but against all the others.”

Russell eventually posted a long message to Instagram on Monday evening, delving into his emotions following the weekend’s events.

“Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart. This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances,” wrote the Australian GP winner, who took only two more victories in the next 18 grands prix.

“It’s been the first proper season of my career where I’ve had more bad days than good. Has it been tough to deal with? Yes, very. Has it been tough to pick myself up week in, week out? Yes, very. Confusion at times? Often. All I know is that I’ve given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year.

“I want to sincerely congratulate Kimi on what has been an absolutely incredible season. You truly deserve the Championship.

“Thank you to the team for producing the best car and power unit this season; it’s been inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top.

“Now, all I can promise is that for the rest of this season, and into the next one, I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of producing for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns.

“Thanks for all the support.”

Russell still has a chance to clinch his highest-ever finish in the drivers’ championship, having taken fourth place in 2022 and 2025. He currently lies fourth, again, with 250 points – 11 and nine points adrift of Verstappen and Hamilton respectively.

Additional reporting by Roberto Chinchero and Ronald Vording

Sports.title: Herta to contest FP1 for Cadillac in Brazil to obtain final superlicence point
Sports.content:
Cadillac test driver Colton Herta will conduct his sixth Friday practice session of the Formula 1 season at this weekend's Brazil Grand Prix to collect his missing FIA superlicence point required to race in the series.

Herta, who has been building up for an F1 campaign with private testing, FP1 sessions and a troubled F2 campaign, needs 40 points to obtain the required FIA superlicence. Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results.

Cadillac will now rectify that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car, which yields a single point. Teams are only required to run a rookie in four FP1 sessions per year, but Sao Paulo will be Herta's sixth of the season as the squad is keen for Herta to finally obtain the licence.

That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Valtteri Bottas for a second year alongside Perez, or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027.

"I’m really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the MAC-26 for another FP1 session," Herta said. "Interlagos is such an iconic, historic track, and driving an F1 car around there is going to be an awesome experience.

"Every time I’ve stepped into the car this year, from Barcelona to Budapest, COTA and Mexico City, I’ve felt more comfortable and better integrated with the engineering team.

"My goal for Friday morning in Brazil is the same: execute the run plan cleanly, give Checo and the engineers the best possible setup data to start their weekend, and keep building on my progress in the car. I’m grateful to the team for giving me this opportunity."

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Photo by: Chris Graythen / Getty Images

Cadillac heads to Brazil after a bruising Mexico weekend, which ended with Bottas suffering a high-speed crash in the race due to a sudden front-left suspension failure. Team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team had "implemented mitigations" to avoid a repeat.

"Following our post-race investigations, Valtteri suffered a suspension failure, and we have implemented mitigations going forward," Budkowski said.

"I’m also pleased to see Colton return to the MAC-26 for another FP1 outing, stepping in for Checo. His growth in the car across his sessions has been impressive, and his feedback remains invaluable to our 2027 development programme."

Herta's bid to obtain his superlicence hit a snag when his car broke down in Monza, leaving the 26-year-old short of the 100km threshold required for the session to award a point. In Brazil, 24 laps of the Interlagos circuit will satisfy that requirement.

Sports.title: Ocon to skip the rest of F1 2026 with Camara to debut for Haas in Brazil
Sports.content:
The Haas Formula 1 team has decided that Esteban Ocon will not race again for the squad, with 2027 rookie Rafael Camara getting an early debut this weekend on home soil.

Following increasingly strained relations between Ocon and the squad, a heated argument in Mexico proved the final straw that made team principal Ayao Komatsu decide to bench the Frenchman.

Reserve driver and Toyota protege Ryo Hirakawa replaced him from Saturday onwards in Mexico, going on to score a point on debut in 10th place. The team has now confirmed Ocon, who is a free agent next year, will not return.

"We have now notified Esteban Ocon that he will not return to a race seat with TGR Haas F1 Team this season," Komatsu explained.

"Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward.

"The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations."

Ferrari junior Camara, who had already been signed by Haas to replace Ocon for 2027, will take the wheel of the VF-26 at the Brazilian Grand Prix.

The 21-year-old, who currently leads the Formula 2 standings and made a stellar impression on Haas in private testing, will have the opportunity to begin his F1 career several months ahead of schedule.

The final green light came on Tuesday afternoon, although Camara had already been placed on standby during the Mexico Grand Prix weekend following Ocon's sudden removal from the Haas line-up.

It is not yet confirmed whether Camara or Hirakawa will race for the team in the remaining rounds at Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with it likely being a combination of both drivers.

Rafa Camara has conducted private testing in older machinery with both Ferrari and Haas. Photo by: Davide Cavazza

Camara has never driven a 2026 F1 car, but will not arrive at his high-pressure home debut unprepared. During the season, he has completed five Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) outings, four at the wheel of Ferrari's SF-25 and one driving the Haas VF-25.

The latter took place in August at Portimao in Portugal and played a crucial role in convincing the US-owned team of his natural ability.

"Looking ahead, we've chosen Rafael Camara to drive alongside Ollie Bearman at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix," Komatsu confirmed.

"Having excelled in his TPC outing in August, we know Rafael's capabilities and we're looking forward to welcoming him into the team this weekend and working with him through his Formula 1 debut driving the VF-26 in Brazil."

The change of plans will also have consequences for Ferrari. Friday morning's FP1 session, originally allocated to Camara, will instead be handed to Dino Beganovic, giving the Swedish driver another opportunity to get behind the wheel of the Maranello team's car.

Sports.title: Why Bearman is yet to be announced as a Haas driver for F1 2027
Sports.content:
With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year.

There is no real doubt that Bearman will stay where he is, with both parties keen to continue for another season into 2027.

“I think it's very clear. I want to continue with Haas and that's definitely my goal," Bearman said in Mexico on Thursday. "It's not really in my hands. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago, but there are a few bigger picture things that we're working on."

Team principal Komatsu added: "I don't like to go into the details of our contract, but Ollie is showing amazing potential. He's contributing a lot to the team's success and we want to grow together. We want to move up the grid as a team.”

And while Komatsu had to dismiss unsubstantiated rumours over Bearman's pay demands, holding up a deal as "absolute nonsense", the real reason behind the delay is not about 2027, but about what happens next.

Autosport understands that should Ferrari be unable to guarantee him a seat in 2028 - after three years of being loaned out to customer team Haas - then Bearman will have the freedom to part ways with Maranello. It is this "bigger picture" that Bearman was referring to in his answer, and a picture that has become increasingly clouded in recent months.

Oliver Bearman, Scuderia Ferrari, Jeddah 2024 Photo by: Mark Sutton

Bearman is still on course to complete the full Ferrari Driver Academy pathway, all the way from F4 to a race seat with the Scuderia - Charles Leclerc being the only driver thus far to have completed the entire trajectory.

But a new road block has emerged in the shape of Lewis Hamilton, who has regained form this year and exercised the contractual option that secured his place at Ferrari for 2027. While Bearman initially looked like a perfect successor to Hamilton, the seven-time world champion's recent comments in the media about his longevity do not portray a man who is walking away from Ferrari and F1 anytime soon. Leclerc, meanwhile, has already agreed a long-term contract extension until at least 2030.

So, if Ferrari isn't able to guarantee Bearman a seat for 2028 and the 21-year-old Briton would be free to explore other options, it makes sense that there is a need right now to clarify certain aspects of his long-term future before formally announcing an extension with Haas.

Komatsu stressed that there is no disagreement regarding the desire to continue the partnership. “I don't think I can go into the details of the what's the hold up, but it's very clear from both parties that they want to continue working together,” he said.

"We work really well together, push each other. He brings a lot to the team and then we are growing together so our intentions from both parties are fully aligned. We're trying to find a solution to work together next year and I'm sure we will”.

The Bearman camp's priority, then, seems to be about ensuring that another year at Haas does not tie him down longer than necessary and potentially limit future opportunities. The paradox is that all parties involved appear to be pursuing compatible objectives. Haas wants to retain Bearman, the driver wants to keep racing, and Ferrari has every interest in protecting a young talent in whom it has invested for years.

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

What complicates the picture is the impossibility of guaranteeing today what might happen two seasons from now. For Bearman, therefore, the issue is not finding a seat for 2027. The real challenge is ensuring that the seemingly inevitable decision to remain at Haas does not become an obstacle to his prospects for 2028.

That delicate balance is what is currently being worked out behind closed doors. And it is probably the most likely explanation for an announcement that, only a few weeks ago, appeared to be nothing more than a formality.

Sports.title: McLaren to bring upgrades to Brazil GP with F1 2027 in mind
Sports.content:
McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 Formula 1 car at this weekend’s Brazil Grand Prix, featuring a front wing concept which is expected to feature on its 2027 challenger.

The team had surged to the front when it substantially updated the MCL40 in Hungary, with Lando Norris winning that race and the following one at Zandvoort, but it has since slipped back in the pecking order despite introducing another comprehensive upgrade package in Baku and further new parts in Austin.

McLaren had the fourth-quickest car in the last four qualifying sessions, with a 0.511s deficit to pole position and a 0.236s gap to the third-fastest challenger on average, but is still working away at improving the MCL40 – with an eye on 2027.

“We’ve got some updates coming to the car across the front wing, rear wing and some floor components as part of our normal development cycle,” said Peter Prodromou, chief technical officer, aerodynamics. “The aim is to make up ground, improve our performance over the remaining races and build momentum into next year.

“Sao Paulo has been a good circuit for us in the past and is a fairly representative track, so we’re hopeful these upgrades can help us take another step towards the front.

“The season isn't over yet: these upgrades are designed to improve the car now and help us in our fight for third in the championship. While the learning we take from these upgrades will feed into next year’s development, we also expect to carry over the concept of the new front wing into the launch specification of next year’s car.”

Peter Prodromou, McLaren Technical Director Aerodynamics Photo by: McLaren

McLaren has a 17-point deficit to third-placed Red Bull but has scored just 59 points to its rival’s 152 across the last five rounds.

The Mexican race was still encouraging, with Norris taking fifth just 12 seconds adrift of race winner Max Verstappen, yet the reigning world champion wasn’t optimistic for the next few rounds.

“If we look at Baku and stuff, I think we're still going to be struggling for pace,” he said on Sunday evening. “So we need to improve the car in certain tracks and certain areas still a lot more.

“Today it was good, but I'm not convinced that if we go back to the tracks we struggled at we'd be good all of a sudden. It's just today suited us, but I don't want to rely on a bit of hope and luck on performance.

“We know what we need to improve on, it just takes time, and hopefully we can have a better day in Brazil.”

Sports.title: The reason behind Honda’s power unit lasting five laps in Mexico GP
Sports.content:
In its Mexico Grand Prix preview, Honda’s Shintaro Orihara had described Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as “a very challenging track for the power unit”, but he perhaps didn’t expect Aston Martin’s weekend to go so awry.

Despite decent pace and mileage in free practice – Fernando Alonso was just 0.769s down on pacesetter Charles Leclerc in FP2, with the AMR26s covering a whopping 144 laps across all three sessions – it all went wrong in the competitive sessions.

Honda did fix some driveability and turbo lag issues between FP3 and qualifying, but Alonso encountered “abnormal signals on the water systems” on Saturday afternoon, which didn’t prevent him from outqualifying Lance Stroll; still, both cars were out in Q1, four tenths down on the Q2 cut-off time.

In the race, the pair retired after five laps due to cooling issues.

“We knew that with the special high-altitude circumstance of Mexico City, we would face some additional challenges compared to other racetracks for the cooling,” said Orihara, Honda’s trackside general manager and chief engineer, following the race.

“However, we found that our ERS cooling circuit was under heavier stress than anticipated and this is why we had to stop the car in different sessions.

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Despite completing a series of laps during the practice sessions, the issue occurred today and during qualifying yesterday.

“At each race this year, we need to learn for 2027, even the hard lessons. We have a lot of data that we can bring back to this circuit next year, including on the turbo lag, and we will work on the solutions.”

Orihara pointed out on Thursday that in previous years the MGU-H supported the turbo, therefore reducing lag, but the new, simpler power units no longer feature that device – and that too was a problem with the thinner air at Mexico City’s high altitude.

While a frustrated Stroll only gave laconic answers to the media at the end of the weekend, Alonso was slightly more loquacious and underlined the scale of the challenge for Aston Martin and Honda.

“The car is very good,” the Spaniard said. “The problem is just, we cannot do more laps than a certain number, apparently, with the engine. Hopefully we learned a lesson and we come next year more prepared.”

But the Adrian Newey-designed machine had potential – even in Mexico. It’s fair to say Alonso and Stroll didn’t get much of a chance to show what they could do in the race; yet, putting the Spaniard’s quickest three sectors together on Sunday (he pitted on lap three, which prevented him from completing a decent lap), he was nearly as quick as Williams’ Carlos Sainz, despite presumably having a much heavier car with a full tank of fuel.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“On Thursday, when we sat together, we said this is a track that has a lot of low-speed corners,” Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack said. “And if we get the driveability under control, that we can be competitive. For example, corners like the stadium section, [Turns] 4-5-6, low-speed stuff.”

Reliability therefore is the crux of the issue – as well as keeping morale up. “It's difficult for everyone to keep the motivation high in such situations, and we are struggling all year already,” Krack admitted.

“We had a very difficult start of the year, then the period when we introduced the upgrades and the ADUO, we [had] a bit better results. Now, we have more trouble in terms of reliability. In Texas, we had different issues with incidents. You know, it's part of racing.

“The thing is, everybody tries his best, everybody is motivated to do better, and I have no doubt about the motivation. We don't have to motivate them, it's motivating them the highest possible.”

And if anyone is staying motivated, that will be Alonso. “I’m doing my best every time, every lap I do, every morning I wake up, every preparation I do, every food I take – everything is focused on performing at my best behind the wheel,” he insisted again, despite his seventh retirement of the season.

Additional reporting by Luis Ramirez

Sports.title: Cracked sump almost put Antonelli out of Mexican Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes has revealed Andrea Kimi Antonelli came close to retiring from the Mexican Grand Prix.

The team discovered the new world champion’s car had developed a fault in its power unit in the final laps.

Mercedes’ deputy team principal Bradley Lord described it as “a sign of the fact that this is Kimi’s year and things are rolling with him.”

“We got the car back after the race, took the floor off the bottom, [and found it was] covered in oil,” he told High Performance Racing. “Sump cracked.”

Antonelli was already detecting signs of trouble from his Mercedes power unit. “Kimi said he thinks about four laps from the end he could start to feel the engine just starting to struggle. So [he was] right on the edge of retirement [from] that race and yet it held together.”

The Mercedes driver lost almost two seconds on the final lap of the race, though he said that was because he was crying. He would still have clinched the title had his engine failed, but a retirement would have robbed him of the iconic photograph with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton he wants to put on his wall.

Lord also shed more light on the loss of power George Russell suffered on the run to turn one at the start of the race, which allowed several of his rivals to overtake. “He’s taken the lion’s share of these technical problems and quirks and we had another one on Sunday,” said Lord.

“He was in prime position for going for the lead into turn one and then [has] a de-rate out of nowhere because of one of the complex bits of the energy rules mean he’s back in P5, P6 and caught up in the [mess] with Hadjar.

“It was a little bit like Spa, the start of the race there where he was so well positioned and then it just became that collision at turn four.”
