Sports.title: Stats: Hirakawa is sixth one-off starter to score a world championship point | 2026 Mexican Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won the race and the new world champion finished third: this year’s championship-deciding race resembled last year’s, though the similarity was superficial.

There may have been three drivers still in contention but this wasn’t a down-to-the-wire nail-biter: Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s coronation was virtually assured before he even set foot in Mexico.

Third place ensured Antonelli succeeds Lando Norris as F1’s second new world champion in as many years. That hasn’t happened since 2010 when Sebastian Vettel became the fourth new world champion in a row, following Kimi Raikkonen, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button.

Norris’s reign as world champion therefore lasted less than a calendar year. At 329 days, this is the sixth-shortest individual duration as champion. However others who had short spells as champion won the title more than once, giving them longer reigns:

Shortest reigns as world champion (days)

*Died before winning the championship

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli’s championship success produced several notable statistics which were previously covered here:

Lewis Hamilton became the oldest driver to claim pole position for a grand prix in his lifetime. At 41 years and 297 days old he is the most senior pole-winner since another Ferrari driver, Mario Andretti, took pole position for the 1982 Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton is the fifth-oldest driver ever to claim a pole position in F1.

Oldest F1 pole-winners

Driver Race Track Age Giuseppe Farina 1954 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 47y, 78d Juan Manuel Fangio 1958 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 46y, 208d Jack Brabham 1970 Spanish Grand Prix Jarama 44y, 16d Mario Andretti 1982 Italian Grand Prix Monza 42y, 195d Lewis Hamilton 2026 Mexican Grand Prix Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 41y, 297d

Hamilton’s pole position was his first for over three years. That’s well short of the longest spell between consecutive pole positions: Raikkonen went 3,262 days (over eight years) between his pole positions in the 2008 French Grand Prix and 2017 Monaco Grand Prix.

That record-extending 105th pole position for Hamilton was a close thing: he beat George Russell by just nine-thousandths of a second. But that was three times the scale of his last pole-winning margin. Hamilton beat Verstappen to pole by just three thousandths of a second in Hungary three years ago.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Unexpectedly, 17 places behind Hamilton on the grid was Ryo Hirakawa, who arrived in Mexico only expecting to take part in the first practice session. However Haas’s shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon after Friday’s running handed Hirakawa his grand prix debut at the age of 32 years and 239 days. That made him the oldest debutant since Andre Lotterer made his one-off appearance for Caterham in the 2014 Belgian Grand Prix – he was older by 39 days.

It’s not uncommon for a driver to take part in practice and then be replaced due to illness or injury. Occasionally, teams swap drivers between garages if damage leaves them with only one car available, as happened with Logan Sargeant and Alexander at the 2024 Australian Grand Prix.

But it is very unusual to see a healthy driver begin a race weekend with a team and then be replaced someone else. The last time something akin to Ocon’s substitution happened was when Ensign attempted to run Ricardo Londono-Bridge in the 1981 Brazilian Grand Prix.

The race moved to Jacarepagua that year and the Colombian driver took part in the then-customary pre-event acclimatisation session for the new circuit on Wednesday. However the FIA refused to grant him a superlicence, so Ensign replaced him with Marc Surer.

Hirakawa’s surprising weekend continued as he scored a point despite originally taking the chequered flag in 13th place. Penalties for Oscar Piastri and both Alpine drivers meant Hirakawa, like Arvid Lindblad earlier this year, finished his first grand prix inside the points.

As it stands, Hirakawa will not take part in any more races – Rafael Camara will take over in Brazil. F1’s rules only allow Haas to use a total of four drivers all season, unless they get a dispensation, and the team has an obvious reason to keep Camara in the season as he will drive for them next year.

Hirakawa therefore stands to join the tiny group of drivers who scored a point in their only start. Just six drivers can claim this unusual feat, and only one – Neville Lederle – did it driving solo in a race run to Formula 1 regulations:

Single-start points-scorers

Driver Race Position Points Notes Joie (George) Chitwood 1950 Indianapolis 500 5th 1 Shared car with Tony Bettenhausen Dorino Serafini 1950 Italian Grand Prix 2nd 3 Shared car with Alberto Ascari Eric Thompson 1952 British Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations Oscar Galvez 1953 Argentinian Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations George Amick 1958 Indianapolis 500 2nd 6 Neville Lederle 1962 South African Grand Prix 6th 1

It remains to be seen whether Ocon will return to start another race. At the beginning of the season the Mexican Grand Prix was due to be his 200th career start. Without him, the number of race-winning drivers on the grid has fallen to 12.

Finally, Verstappen’s sixth win at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez makes it the venue he’s scored the most wins at. He could equal that with a sixth win at Yas Marina next month – if the race takes place.

Sports.title: On This Day: Penske makes final CART appearance as longest season ends | Brief
Sports.content:
The end of CART’s longest-ever season, 25 years ago today, marked a watershed moment in the series’ battle with the rival Indy Racing League, formed by a split five years earlier.

Cristiano da Matta won the 21st and final event of the 2001 campaign at the Fontana superspeedway. However the season was marked by rows over technology, the controversial cancellation of a race in Texas on safety grounds and the appalling Lausitzring crash which almost claimed the life of Alex Zanardi.

Significantly, the 2001 finale saw the last appearance of the powerhouse Penske team before it defected to the IRL. Over the coming years rival engine manufacturers followed them and CART fell into bankruptcy. The two series reunited in 2008 and Roger Penske’s organisation purchased the merged IndyCar series in 2019.

Sports.title: Official: Ocon will not return to drive for Haas, Camara to take over in Brazil | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Haas has confirmed Esteban Ocon will not return to drive for them following his shock ousting for the team last weekend.

Rafael Camara , who was due to make his Formula 1 debut for the team next year, will take over Ocon’s car from this weekend’s round in Brazil.

Ocon participated in Friday’s second practice session in Mexico and was due to remain in the car for the rest of the weekend. However Haas unexpectedly announced on Friday morning that Ocon’s place had been taken by Ryo Hirakawa, the team’s test driver who participated in the first practice session driving Ocon’s car.

Ocon subsequently issued a statement confirming there had been a difference of opinion between him and the team but strongly denying any claims “physical violence was used to resolve any differences”. He challenged race engineer Laure Mueller’s instruction regarding tyre strategy during second practice.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu has not explained the team’s reasons for dropping Ocon.

“We have now notified Esteban Ocon that he will not return to a race seat with TGR Haas F1 Team this season,” he said in a statement issued by the team. “Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City – but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward.

“The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations.”

Haas announced last month that Ocon won’t return to drive for the team next year. Camara will therefore make his debut at his home race this weekend.

The team has not given any indication who will drive for them at in the final three rounds of the championship. Komatsu said Camara “excelled in his TPC [Testing of Previous Cars] outing in August.”

“We know Rafa’s capabilities and we’re looking forward to welcoming him into the team this weekend and working with him through his Formula 1 debut driving the VF-26 in Brazil,” he added.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Verstappen puzzled by engine braking: ‘It just decides by itself what to do’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen said he couldn’t explain the engine braking problems he reported on his radio during the latter stages of the Mexican Grand Prix.

“It happens randomly,” said Verstappen, who won the race despite. “The engine just decides by itself what to do, to be honest. So, I don’t know.

“Maybe I need to have a conversation with the engine before going into the race. Maybe it has to behave better.”

He suspected the problem was linked to the demanding conditions at the track. “We don’t know, sometimes it just happens. It’s not very consistent.

“I think, honestly, everything is running so hot here, and also for the turbocharger and everything, it’s tough to make everything spot on.”

Sports.title: “Silly” power unit rules prevent passing, says Hamilton: “The engine can go faster” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s power unit rules made it harder for drivers to race at the Mexican Grand Prix, according to Lewis Hamilton.

The Ferrari driver spent the final laps of the race trying to attack race leader Max Verstappen . He said he was unable to do so because of the limits on energy deployment. This causes the effect known as “clipping”, where the amount of power being delivered drops.

“You can’t overtake here,” said Hamilton in the post-race press conference with Verstappen and Andrea Kimi Antonelli. “I think it’s something the FIA need to [address]. It’s just quite bad, I’m sure these guys would agree.

“We have this clip at the end of the straight where you can’t go past a certain speed, so everyone just follows. It’s the silliest thing when you are behind and you have a little bit more power in the slipstream. You should be able to go past that to have a chance to overtake.

“The engine can go faster, it’s just they have these silly clips. It’s the worst engine profile setting that I think they’ve probably ever had in this sport and it doesn’t provide great racing. So today you probably didn’t see much overtaking, unfortunately, because of that.”

Other drivers warned before the race that the “speed limiter” would inhibit overtaking. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has rejected criticism of the series power units and said fans “don’t understand” what clipping is.

Hamilton acknowledged other factors make overtaking especially difficult in Mexico. The high altitude means the air pressure is lower which makes it harder to keep cars cool when running in traffic. He also thinks the track’s configuration could be improved.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Obviously the starts were fun, but it’s a very hard track to follow [other cars at] with the thin air and low downforce. I gave it everything to try and get close to Max.

“I don’t know if they need to change the last corner because it’s so quick. I don’t know, there could be a change to the track, maybe, to enable us to have a little bit better racing.

“But everyone having this [clipping] this year just diminishes any opportunity of that.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says doubters “added fuel to the fire” in his world championship pursuit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
New world champion Andrea Kimi Antonelli says he was driven to disprove those who said he wasn’t ready for Formula 1.

Mercedes brought him up through the junior ranks quickly, skipping Formula 3 entirely and only spending a single season in Formula 2. Antonelli made his F1 debut last year, aged just 18, with Mercedes’ works F1 team rather than one of their customers.

Antonelli’s first season did not go entirely smoothly. He endured a nine-round spell during which he failed to score on seven occasions.

However he was competitive right from the start of his second season and quickly overtook team mate George Russell in the championship. Antonelli clinched the title yesterday with four rounds to spare.

He said that had been a satisfying response to those who suggested he wasn’t ready for F1.

“It’s always good to shut off some of the noise,” said Antonelli. “I think in many ways it does help to add fuel to the fire, the fact that some people said that I didn’t belong in Formula 1 or I wasn’t ready for it.

“At some points last year, it probably looked like that I wasn’t ready for it. But I think last year, being able to experience those moments made me much more ready ahead of this year. Experiencing really low and difficult situations, high-pressure moments, really helped me to face certain situations this year, and definitely they made me mature a lot as a driver and as a person.”

Antonelli clinched the title with nine grand prix wins, the most of any driver. But he admits there was room for improvement in his performance. “I’ve had moments where I could have done better, a lot better. It’s just a constant learning process.

“But I think last year, being able to race [with] Mercedes, obviously [going] straight under the spotlight, made me grow much, much faster than if I would have gone to a smaller team, for example.”

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Predicts A Mayweather vs Garcia Fight Won’t Happen
Sports.content:
Rumors of a high-profile fight between Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) and Floyd “Money” Mayweather (50-0, 27 KOs) have been circulating, but Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya believes that on February 6, 2027, Garcia will not be sharing the ring with Mayweather.

The Golden Boy Promotions CEO, Oscar De La Hoya, thinks Mayweather is capable of giving Garcia a good fight. However, he believes that instead of Mayweather, Ryan Garcia will face Teofimo Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) on February 6th.

Back on October 21st, Ryan Garcia posted breaking news on all of his social media platforms. Garcia claimed a Hall of Fame boxer reached out to him to discuss a potential title fight.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia said. “But it’s real Floyd, and I agreed to a fight at 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world, 50-0 vs. the current champ.”

Garcia doubled down on the claim when he posted a second message on his Instagram account, and this message included a photo of Garcia and Mayweather in what appears to be a FaceTime call.

As time went on, fight fans were becoming skeptical about the Mayweather vs. Garcia matchup actually happening because Garcia was doing all the talking while Mayweather remained silent.

Then, finally, on November 1st, Floyd Mayweather posted the  for his upcoming exhibition bout. Included in the , Mayweather confirmed the Garcia fight when he stated, “This is a lil tune-up before me and Ryan Garcia lock up Feb. 2027.”

At this point, it seemed like the bout was official, but during a recent interview with Sean Zittel, Garcia’s promoter Oscar De La Hoya made a statement that puts the fight in doubt.

“I do love that Teofimo fight, uh, sometime in February on DAZN. And you know the Floyd Mayweather thing, yes, there are a lot of rumors, a lot of speculation.Who knows? I don’t think it will happen, but look if it does, I’ve always said yeah, it’s a 50/50 fight,” De La Hoya stated.

Ryan Garcia has one more fight on his Golden Boy contract. Garcia keeps talking about Floyd, but if his promoter is leaning toward Teofimo, then there’s a good chance we will see a Garcia vs Lopez title bout in February.

Fighting the WBA welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez makes a lot of sense. If Ryan wins, he will have a victory over a high-level opponent, and the win would equate to Garcia becoming a unified champion.

If he decides to fight Floyd Mayweather he has everything to lose and nothing to gain. If Garcia loses to Mayweather, it’s an embarrassment, and if he defeats Mayweather, nobody is going to give him credit for beating a 50-year-old man.

Sports.title: Is Diego Pacheco Built For World Titles Or Permanent Contender Status?
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco needs his November 14 clash with Darius Fulghum to deliver a clear direction. Padding his record with another win over a contender helps, but the undefeated super middleweight has reached a stage where championship talk requires a targeted belt and a credible route to get there.

Facing Fulghum, 30, is not necessarily a bad fight on paper, but when you look at what has been bypassed over the last two years, the frustration for fans makes complete sense. Pacheco walked away from Christian Mbilli twice. The IBF ordered a final eliminator in late 2024, but Pacheco backed out to fight Steven Nelson instead.

A few months later, the WBC ordered a purse bid between them for an interim title, and Matchroom withdrew him again. While traveling to Quebec on an away promoter’s budget is a legitimate business concern, walking away from two separate sanctioning body routes against the same contender gave fans the impression he wanted no part of Mbilli’s pressure.

Then came the Hamzah Sheeraz situation in January 2026. The WBO ordered a purse bid for the vacant super middleweight belt. Pacheco was the No. 2 contender with a clear path to an actual world championship, yet he pulled out right before the bid. Even with Eddie Hearn presenting it as a matter of timing and readiness, walking away from a vacant title shot against another young, tall puncher did not sit well with the public.

Most recently, when the WBO super middleweight opening emerged against Janibek Alimkhanuly around September 2026, Pacheco was bypassed completely in favor of the Fulghum date. While Jacob Bank took the call to face Janibek, Pacheco opted for an in-house Matchroom card in Carson. Fulghum is an accomplished amateur and a solid puncher, but he does not carry the status of a title fight or an elite final eliminator.

At 25 years old, Pacheco has reached the point where building fights no longer cut it. Taking on Fulghum while Mbilli, Sheeraz, and Janibek were all realistic possibilities makes this look like matchmakers protecting an asset rather than letting him fight for the hardware.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Says Jaime Munguia Looks Worn Down
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia looks worn down despite being younger than Canelo Alvarez, according to Tim Bradley. He argued that years of taking heavy punishment have taken a massive toll.

Munguia’s recent outing against Nikita Zon only added to worries that began with his knockout defeat to Bruno Surace, pointing to a fighter who looks uneasy whenever punches head his direction.

“I think even though he’s younger, he is worn down. And I think he’s worn down even more than Canelo Alvarez because when you look at Munguia and his style, all he do is eat shots. He eat punches. His defense is trash,” Bradley said on Boxing King Media.

Munguia settled the score by beating Surace in a rematch and picked up a win over Armando Resendiz, yet neither result dispelled doubts surrounding his punch resistance. Getting hurt by Zon, a fighter without a reputation for big power, made those questions impossible to ignore.

“I think even though he’s younger, he is worn down. And I think he’s worn down even more than Canelo Alvarez because when you look at Munguia and his style, all he do is eat shots. He eat punches. His defense is trash,” Bradley said on Boxing King Media.

The initial knockout against Surace looks like a clear dividing line. Since that stoppage, Munguia has appeared rattled by incoming fire, even during rounds he controls. An offensive fighter who relies on exchanging blows loses a critical edge the moment hesitation creeps into the equation.

Struggling with Zon does not prove his chin is completely shot, but it does suggest a real psychological change. The willingness to scrap remains intact. The automatic confidence required to withstand flush shots seems diminished.

Bradley pointed out that extra bulk might be hurting Munguia inside the ring.

“You got all these new muscles and six-pack and all of that stuff, and you running out of gas like that, bro. Like, you need to rethink whatever the hell you doing, man,” Bradley noted.

Cardio issues only make defensive flaws worse. Once the punch volume declines, opponents can exploit holes in his guard without fearing immediate retaliation. When doubt about taking a punch enters the mix, an offensive dynamo quickly gets stuck in hesitation.

Paulie Malignaggi agreed with that bleak view, declaring that Munguia is slipping fast. Malignaggi suggested a rematch with Canelo could materialize precisely because Alvarez would view him as an easy target.

That perspective reveals how the industry currently rates Munguia. Wins are keeping him in line for marquee bouts, but shaky moments in the ring are making elite competition eager to sign the contract. Avenging the Surace loss closed a chapter on paper, but regaining absolute trust in his punch resistance is proving to be a much tougher fight.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Took Zuffa Cash Over Cuban Nightmare
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley owes nobody an apology for taking Zuffa’s money. When Eddie Hearn brushed off the financial gap as merely “a couple hundred grand,” Bentley gave the only reasonable answer a 31-year-old prizefighter could give.

He makes his promotional debut this Saturday at the Copper Box Arena against Shane Mosley Jr. While losing his WBO middleweight belt clouded the move, Bentley views the extra cash as life-changing security.

“Couple hundred grand more is a lot of money. That’s a deposit on a house at least, or more than a deposit on a house,” Bentley told Pro Boxing Fans. “A couple hundred grand more might be change to him. But to me, that’s a lot of money. Him and his family are secured and they’re good for life. What about me? Why can’t I have that opportunity?”

It is hard to argue with that logic. Promoters can lecture fighters about championship legacy because they do not have to absorb punches to keep the hardware. For Bentley, the pay bump provides real stability for his family.

Matchroom had floated an idea for him to headline in Ghana, honoring his family roots. Bentley admits he would have loved defending his title there, but his Zuffa deal was already locked in. In the end, he took what made practical sense.

“I’m 31. I ain’t got another 10 years,” Bentley explained. “So, I got to be really selfish and get what I can from this sport before leaving it.”

Now comes the tough part, because the boxing side must justify the decision. Bentley hopes Zuffa can secure matchups with rival middleweight champions, yet those bouts remain unmade. A massive first purse is great, but regular dates against quality opposition will determine the true value of the contract.

Bentley remains frustrated over how the WBO handled his mandatory commitment against Yoenli Hernandez. He believed he had clearance for a voluntary defense before facing Hernandez next year, but claims the sanctioning body shifted its stance once his new promotional pact leaked.

“As soon as everyone caught wind I was moving promotional stables, that’s when everything changed,” Bentley said.

He noted that neither he nor his management ever laid eyes on the petition Hernandez supposedly filed. While that represents Bentley’s side of the fallout rather than concrete evidence against the sanctioning body, it explains his bitterness.

All of that takes a backseat to Mosley. The American is durable, hungry, and dangerous. A loss on Saturday would completely derail Bentley’s timeline for regaining world honors.

Bentley made his financial case. Saturday night is about showing what Zuffa paid for.

Taking on Yoenli was widely viewed as a disaster waiting to happen. The Cuban amateur standout is an absolute nightmare style matchup, and getting taken apart by him for short money would have left Bentley empty-handed, battered, and right back at square one. Cashing in on the front end makes total sense when the alternative is getting wrecked for peanuts.

The trap, though, is thinking Zuffa is a safe harbor. They operate with cold, corporate efficiency. If Bentley slips up and Mosley beats him on Saturday, that multi-fight deal suddenly might not be worth the paper it is printed on. Promotions love you when you give them leverage, but once an older fighter loses his title and drops his debut, the interest dries up fast.

Without a belt to force anyone’s hand, Bentley’s situation is limited. He got his payday, but if Mosley outworks him, Zuffa could easily shelve him or cut bait entirely, leaving him right where he feared he would end up, just with one nice check in the bank.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder vs Jai Opetaia Announced For Fury-Joshua
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder faces Jai Opetaia on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, serving as the co-feature to Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua on Netflix, Ring Magazine announced today. On paper, it sounds massive.

In reality, the matchup leans heavily on Wilder’s legacy rather than any guarantee of a thrilling contest. The real question is whether the former champion has anything left to offer, or if he is simply being set up as a marquee name on Opetaia’s resume.

Opetaia makes the jump from cruiserweight to take on a veteran whose present-day form is a massive question mark. Wilder once captivated audiences because someone was practically guaranteed to hit the canvas. Yet recent setbacks have drained that aura. Bouncing back against Tyrrell Herndon and Derek Chisora did little to prove he can still run with top-tier heavyweights. Herndon brought virtually zero profile, while outpointing Chisora hardly signals a career renaissance.

Because of that decline, Wilder becomes an ideal target for Opetaia. He delivers elite name value, championship pedigree, and the lingering threat of a highlight-reel finish. At the same time, his age and physical mileage make him a vastly safer proposition than young, dangerous contenders like Daniel Dubois, Agit Kabayel, Filip Hrgovic, or Moses Itauma.

Opetaia’s camp likely would not jump at those fights with anywhere near the same eagerness. Even someone like Bakhodir Jalolov would represent a much rougher initiation into the heavyweight division. Those challenges would force Opetaia to prove his mobility, punching power, and chin hold up against heavyweights who are in their prime.

Targeting Wilder lets Opetaia chase the spotlight without taking on that degree of risk. Even an explosive stoppage victory would leave plenty of doubts about how he matches up with the division’s elite.

Wilder still holds one classic trump card. If that trademark right hand lands cleanly with full power, Opetaia could be out cold before his slick boxing fundamentals take control. Opetaia showed vulnerability against Huseyin Cinkara, raising genuine concerns about how he handles elite heavyweight firepower.

That equalizer only matters if Wilder actually pulls the trigger. With his history of shoulder trouble, the real capability of that weapon remains unclear until fight night. If he looks tentative, sluggish, and unable to establish respect, Opetaia could roll over him early.

That is the major gamble with putting this bout in the chief-support slot. A faded Wilder getting dominated may generate flashy clips for social media, but it makes for a lopsided, disappointing viewing experience. His name dresses up the marquee, yet it remains to be seen how many fans still view him as must-watch TV.

Opetaia would gain far more credibility by testing himself against a top heavyweight contender or booking a cruiserweight collision with David Benavidez. Wilder offers a different prize entirely, letting Opetaia look devastating against an opponent fans remember as terrifying.

Whether Wilder still has any of that venom left will determine if this co-main event actually delivers on its billing. Wilder has looked completely faded, uncoordinated, and gun-shy for a long time. His legs are gone, his punch resistance has evaporated, and the explosive athleticism that once compensated for his lack of basic boxing fundamentals is nowhere to be found.

Putting him in with someone as sharp, fast, and aggressive as Opetaia feels cynical. For the organizers and Opetaia’s handlers, it checks cynical commercial boxes: It is built to lure casual and older viewers. Those fans remember the destructive knockout artist who ruled the WBC division and had the trilogy with Fury. They see the name, assume it is an explosive heavyweight collision, and either tune into Netflix or buy into the buzz.

The result offers almost no real sporting substance. Hardcore fans see right through it. If Opetaia blasts out a 41-year-old, fragile shell of Wilder, what does it prove? It tells us nothing about how Opetaia handles a legitimate, prime heavyweight contender who can absorb shots and fire back.

Yet, the highlight reel will be circulated everywhere, marketed as Opetaia making a devastating statement in the heavyweight division. The casual viewers will dismiss it regardless. If Wilder looks dreadful, clumsy, and gets wiped out in a round or two, casuals will simply view the whole thing as a sad mismatch featuring a washed fighter rather than crediting Opetaia as an elite heavyweight force.

It ends up in that weird circus middle ground: too lopsided and artificial to earn respect from hardcore purists, and too sad of a spectacle to leave casual viewers satisfied once the opening bell actually rings.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Says Osleys Iglesias Is Too Good For Canelo
Sports.content:
Paulie Malignaggi knows the Canelo Alvarez matchmaking blueprint inside out. His belief that Osleys Iglesias is “too good and not popular enough” points to a familiar formula: target a credible foe with just enough flaws for Canelo to exploit.

Because of that, Malignaggi considers Lester Martinez a far more realistic candidate to be selected for Canelo’s next opponent in 2027. Martinez brings real grit to the table, yet his technical limits give Canelo’s corner a clear path to victory. Iglesias presents a far uglier package involving size, elite craft, plus power.

“I think at the moment [Iglesias] is probably too good and not popular enough,” Malignaggi explained to Boxing King Media.

Malignaggi drew a direct line between Iglesias and the way David Morrell missed out on Canelo during his undisputed championship run. As he sees it, Morrell and David Benavidez brought too much threat with too little commercial upside. Malignaggi views Iglesias through that exact lens, even if Canelo’s camp hasn’t formally turned down the Cuban.

The argument is simple. An elite boxer can easily earn a title shot on merit while packing enough danger to price himself out of the running. Martinez strikes a far more appealing balance for the Mexican superstar.

“He’s continued to win, but has looked a little bit flawed, just flawed enough to where you’re saying, you know what, that might be a guy we could pick off here,” Malignaggi noted.

Lester battled Christian Mbilli to a grueling draw last year, proving his durability over 10 hard rounds. Yet that contest revealed his limitations. He would make Canelo sweat, though an elite counterpuncher would find plenty of clean openings. Malignaggi pointed out that Martinez lacks a consistent jab, handing Canelo room to dictate terms.

Iglesias, meanwhile, possesses a powerful jab that spells trouble. His right hand could easily cause more headaches than Terence Crawford’s, purely through reach advantages. Iglesias leans on his pedigree in the Cuban amateur system to control range, making Canelo eat leather long before he enters punching distance.

Slipping into the pocket is just as risky. Iglesias hides a vicious right hook that travels on an unorthodox arc courtesy of his long frame, catching opponents blind as they surge in. Factor in his southpaw stance alongside genuine power in both fists, and Canelo faces a nightmare puzzle.

Martinez delivers some name recognition with hardcore fans, along with clear technical flaws. Iglesias brings pure stylistic poison with minimal mainstream buzz. Martinez would come to fight, but his flaws make him beatable for the aging Canelo. Iglesias has the exact skillset that keeps his phone silent.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Faces Another Aging Heavyweight In Nelson Hysa
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel defending his WBC belt against 42-year-old Nelson Hysa on November 28 continues a habit of feasting on past-prime heavyweights. Kabayel holds wins over far superior opposition, making this soft showcase completely useless for proving how he stacks up against the division’s dangerous young lions.

The Merkur Spiel-Arena in Düsseldorf stages this mismatch between the German titleholder and the obscure Albanian. Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) provides flashy numbers for promotional posters, yet he walked into this championship opportunity without defeating a single credible top-15 contender.

“This is the fight we wanted to make,” promoter Frank Warren said when announcing the event.

For Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs), this matchup continues a blatant habit of feasting on guys past their expiration date. Zhilei Zhang had already blown out 41 candles before Kabayel took him out in February 2025. Arslanbek Makhmudov was 34 when they clashed in December 2023, while earlier targets Kevin Johnson and Pavel Sour had long crossed into their 40s before stepping through the ropes.

Those previous opponents brought vastly different threats to the table. Zhang owned legitimate one-punch power, having already demolished Joe Joyce and Deontay Wilder. That made Kabayel’s stoppage a genuine statement win. Getting off the canvas to fold the Chinese southpaw with a body shot proved he could take heat and execute under fire.

Yet Zhang’s gas tank betrayed him, just like his age. Kabayel capitalized on those glaring flaws, but surviving an aging slugger who runs out of petrol after three rounds does not prove he can handle the division’s elite young guns.

Makhmudov brought a completely different danger profile. He arrived younger than Zhang or Hysa, carrying an undefeated record built on chilling knockout power. Kabayel ruthlessly exposed his stiff movement and crude defense, sending the Russian power puncher down three times before the referee intervened in the fourth round. It looked devastating on screen, even if Makhmudov arrived with an empty resume propped up on weak opposition.

Even Kabayel’s masterclass against Frank Sanchez deserves a massive asterisk. Sanchez fought essentially on one leg after suffering a severe knee injury. Stripped of his wheels, the Cuban was transformed into a sitting duck along the ropes. Kabayel did not out-box or out-maneuver a prime contender; he cornered an injured man who could neither retreat nor generate leverage to fire back.

Subtract Sanchez, and what is left of Kabayel’s record? An exhausted 41-year-old Zhang who ran out of oxygen after three rounds, a crude, stiff Makhmudov who had never beaten anyone, and a string of washed 40-somethings. Taking on Nelson Hysa is not an aberration; it is just standard operating procedure.

Hysa has shown nothing to suggest he belongs in the same ring with world-class operators. Blowing out Thomas Narmo in two rounds last August was another empty showcase against a bottom-tier opponent. It offered zero proof that he can survive deep water, handle relentless body shots, or deal with someone who hits back.

Kabayel is custom-built to expose fighters at this level. His relentless assault to the midsection has dismantled far superior heavyweights. Hysa will quickly find himself drowning under steady pressure, with zero answers once the body attack starts sapping his legs.

The bigger problem is what Kabayel actually gets out of this mismatch. Beating up a 42-year-old keeps his undefeated record clean and ensures he hangs onto his WBC belt, yet tells us nothing about how he copes with prime, dangerous heavyweights who possess the youth and stamina to drag him into deep waters.

Kabayel built a solid following through his relentless engine. Asking fight fans to stomach another aging victim merely stalls the division, delaying the crucial tests against prime heavyweights everyone actually wants to see.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Targets Aging Erislandy Lara For Belt
Sports.content:
Tim Tszyu grabbing a second belt sounds great until you look at who is holding it. Erislandy Lara is 43, fights once a year, and represents a safe shortcut to a championship rather than any kind of statement at middleweight.

Picking up the WBA strap off a semi-retired veteran will look good on paper, but beating Lara proves nothing about where Tszyu stands against actual middleweight threats.

The December 13 date at Cbus Super Stadium in Queensland is pure home-cooked business. Lara has defended this belt just four times since picking it up in May 2021. Holding a title hostage across five years through inactivity is not dominance; it is just boxing politics at work. His points win over late sub Johan Gonzalez last December told everyone what they already knew: Lara is running out the clock.

The Cuban still knows how to survive, jab, and make opponents look bad. But expecting the slick operator from eight years ago to magically appear in Australia is wishful thinking.

Tszyu’s team knows exactly what they bought here. They get a recognized name, a major title, and an opponent old enough to be Tszyu’s father who barely fights. From a purely competitive standpoint, he doesn’t come out ahead. If Tszyu beats Lara, hardcore fans will just say he ran over a 43-year-old museum piece. If he struggles or loses, his stock completely craters. The entire maneuver is purely about leverage, optics, and business.

Casual fans and mainstream Australian sports outlets do not track Lara’s inactivity or birth certificate; they just see that Tszyu went up to 160 and captured another major title. It gives his team a shiny promotional bullet point that lasts forever, regardless of how watered down the accomplishment actually is.

Holding the WBA middleweight strap transforms Tszyu from a challenger hunting for fights into a belt-holder who dictates terms. In modern boxing, belts are chips at the negotiating table.

If Terence Crawford, Canelo Alvarez, or anyone else wants to talk big-money unification or cross-weight clashes down the line, Tszyu having a 160-pound trinket gives him contractual leverage, a higher purse split, and immediate PPV headliner status in Australia.

Since Sebastian Fundora battered Tszyu inside seven rounds in their summer 2025 rematch, Tszyu has coasted on decision wins. Beating an inactive Errol Spence Jr. at 154 was convenient, but now Tszyu gets to leap straight to a middleweight belt without trading punches with a single real contender at 160 pounds.

It is soft matchmaking dressed up as elite action. Tszyu might leave the ring wearing middleweight gold, but taking a belt off Lara’s ghost will fool nobody paying close attention.

The undercard tells the same story. Jermell Charlo steps in against Brock Jarvis, a guy already knocked cold by Liam Paro and Keith Thurman. Charlo has been sitting on the couch since Canelo took his lunch money in 2023.

Ghana News.title: Too many schoolchildren dying on our roads – Mahama backs TraffiTech
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has defended the introduction of the TraffiTech-GH speed enforcement system, citing the deaths and life-changing injuries suffered by schoolchildren knocked down by speeding vehicles as a compelling reason for stricter traffic regulation.

He said the country could no longer afford to delay measures to control speeding while children continued to lose their lives or sustain permanent disabilities on their way home from school.

The president said protecting vulnerable road users, particularly schoolchildren, must be a priority in the country's efforts to reduce road crashes.

"If you look at the number of children knocked down every year in Ghana when they are coming from school, you will understand why it is important for us to check over speeding. Children coming from school are knocked down and killed or permanently injured, and so it is important for us to check speeding," he said.

Speaking to 1957 News on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) at Jumby Bay Island in Antigua and Barbuda, President Mahama maintained that the need to protect lives justified the deployment of technology to enforce traffic regulations.

His comments come amid public debate over the introduction of TraffiTech-GH, particularly concerns about the cost of penalties, the condition of roads and whether motorists should be subjected to stricter enforcement before the government addresses existing infrastructure deficiencies.

Road safety cannot wait.

President Mahama rejected arguments that the government should first repair roads and improve related infrastructure before introducing the automated traffic enforcement system.

He said road maintenance and traffic law enforcement were not mutually exclusive responsibilities and that deficiencies in the road network should not become an excuse for allowing dangerous driving to continue.

He cited the United Kingdom, where speed cameras are deployed despite roads not being in perfect condition, to support his argument that traffic enforcement should not be postponed until all infrastructure challenges have been resolved.

"My understanding is that Traffitech has begun with overspeeding; they have not yet added the other components of jumping red lights and parking wrongly. And so I hear they [the public] say we should fix the roads before we introduce Traffitech. I mean, it doesn't happen like that. The roads are not perfect in the UK, and yet they have speed cameras," he said.

The President's argument is that controlling excessive speed is an immediate road safety intervention, particularly in areas where pedestrians and children are exposed to fast-moving vehicles.

Road crash figures reinforce concerns

Available road safety statistics highlight the scale of the country's road safety challenge.

Figures released by the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) show that Ghana recorded 2,949 road crash deaths in 2025, compared with 2,494 in 2024, representing an 18.2 per cent increase.

The crashes also resulted in 16,714 injuries, while pedestrian knockdowns increased by seven per cent to 2,561 cases.

Of those killed in road crashes during 2025, 328 were below 18 years, representing approximately 11 per cent of the fatalities.

The figures underline the risks faced by children and other vulnerable road users, although the national statistics do not separately establish how many of the child fatalities occurred while pupils were travelling to or from school.

The NRSA has repeatedly called for stronger enforcement and greater cooperation among road safety stakeholders to reverse the rising fatalities.

Warning signs for motorists

While defending the speed enforcement initiative, President Mahama said its implementation must be transparent, with motorists adequately informed about the locations of the cameras.

He specifically urged the police and the agencies responsible for TraffiTech-GH to install visible signposts ahead of camera locations to alert drivers that they were approaching monitored sections of the road.

He said advance notification would help motorists understand where the technology was deployed and encourage compliance with speed limits.

"All I will urge is that the police and those implementing Traffitech should put up signs showing where the cameras are, because that is one of the things you need to do if you are introducing this kind of innovation. You need to put signposts, warning motorists, that there is a speed camera ahead. I think that transparency is important," he said.

The directive, he indicated, was intended to ensure that the introduction of technology-driven enforcement was accompanied by openness and adequate public information.

'Don't overspeed'

On complaints that the fines imposed under the TraffiTech-GH system were too high, the president urged motorists to avoid the penalties by observing prescribed speed limits.

He maintained that drivers who complied with traffic regulations would have no reason to incur speeding fines.

"If it is too expensive, then don't overspeed; that's all, there is a solution to it," he said.

The TraffiTech-GH system is expected to strengthen enforcement of road traffic regulations through automated monitoring, with speeding enforcement forming the initial phase. Other violations, including running red lights and illegal parking, are also envisaged under the broader system.

President Mahama's defence of the initiative places the protection of schoolchildren and other vulnerable road users at the centre of the debate, as the government seeks to use technology to address dangerous driving and reduce preventable deaths on Ghana's roads.

Ghana News.title: Parliament to reverse LGBTQ bill’s passage over errors in penalties – Agalga
Ghana News.content:
Parliament will rescind the passage of the anti-LGBTQ bill to correct errors in its penalty provisions, Majority Leader James Agalga has disclosed.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, he said mistakes in calculating penalty units could create serious problems when courts apply the proposed law.

“For instance, how to compute penalty units was completely done in error, in some cases,” he said.

The House will therefore reverse its approval at the third-reading stage. That will allow lawmakers to reopen consideration of the bill and correct the provisions before sending it to the President.

“The penal provisions are not aligned. They are not aligned properly,” Mr Agalga said.

He explained that the penalties must align with existing legislation. The corrections would leave the bill's substance largely intact.

“So, not much of substance would change.”

The planned reversal follows months of controversy over the bill’s May 29 passage. Speaker Alban Bagbin subsequently directed Parliament to revisit the process.

He raised concerns about procedural compliance and whether the bipartisan support recorded at committee level was reflected on the floor.

Then Majority Leader Mahama Ayariga defended the passage and maintained that Parliament had followed its rules.

The legislation also triggered disagreements over proposed exemptions for journalists, lawyers and health professionals.

Critics within Parliament argued that the changes weakened the bill. Its defenders maintained that the exemptions protected legitimate professional duties.

Mr Agalga said the latest intervention concerned how the penalties would be applied in practice.

“Otherwise, the bill as it stands in this current form would have serious challenges when it comes to implementation,” he warned.

He confirmed that Parliament intended to complete the corrections during the current meeting. Asked whether the bill would reach the President this month, he replied: “Absolutely”.

He also rejected suggestions that the delay reflected a change in the President’s position.

“Contrary to all the wild speculations that the President has shifted goalposts and all that. No, he hasn't.”

Mr Agalga said Parliament had identified the defects and was responsible for fixing them before transmission.

“We have the duty of enacting laws,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Iran’s chief negotiator says Americans voted ‘no to war’
Ghana News.content:
Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf dismissed Donald Trump's threat to renew strikes on Iran

Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections.

"We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X.

"If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned.

Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices. But he insisted that he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran in February.

In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran".

He went on to say: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that."

Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends".

In recent weeks, Trump has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran.

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei - who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly seriously wounded in the same Israeli air strike on the first day of the war that killed his father and predecessor, Ali - said he did not expect US policy to change.

Khamenei released a statement saying anyone who thought there would be any change from American "hostility towards the Iranian nation" was "gravely mistaken".

He also said the war would have "much wider dimensions" if it resumed.

In a separate development on Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC said two of the vessels were still burning, and two additional tankers had been intercepted, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. It said they were trying to travel through a prohibited southern route in the Strait of Hormuz.

BBC Verify has been investigating the IRGC claims, and has not found any evidence that four tankers were destroyed.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre said a tanker was struck by two unknown projectiles about 14 nautical miles (26km) north-east of Limah, in Oman's Musandam peninsula, on Tuesday evening. No casualties were reported, it added.

On Monday, an Indian crew member of a dhow - a wooden sailing boat - was killed in an attack north-east of Limah. Omani authorities rescued thirteen other crew members.

The IRCG also reported on Wednesday that its forces had shot down another US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.

It made a similar claim on Monday night, when US officials said the US military had carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.

In an interview with the Financial Times ahead of the midterms, Trump suggested he was happy with the state of the conflict, and that he did not consider them to be "really in a war".

When asked about what the newspaper described as "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack on Iran this week, Trump said they were "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it".

Indirect talks to end the conflict have been stalled for months.

President Masoud Pezeshkian maintained on Tuesday that his government had been trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue".

"No-one will benefit from this war" if it were to resume, he warned.

He also emphasised that Iran's supreme leader had granted the government powers to negotiate "issues that he had previously considered off-limits".

Crowds demonstrating against the US president in central Tehran on 4 November

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqai said on Monday that the basis of the current indirect negotiations mediated by Qatar remained a seven-step proposal that Iran submitted in September. But he added that the proposal had been "condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days".

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and the US naval blockade.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

Additional reporting by Gabriela Pomeroy

Ghana News.title: Real Madrid reach verbal agreement to sign Gabriel
Ghana News.content:
Real Madrid are confident they can win the race to sign Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel after reaching a verbal agreement with the teenager.

The 16-year-old is registered at United but hasn't returned to the club since walking out in September.

Gabriel, who played against Atletico Madrid on United's pre-season tour, had been expected to become the club's youngest debutant in September's Carabao Cup tie against Brighton.

However, he has opted to look elsewhere for senior football and has been training on his own in Spain.

His availability alerted clubs around Europe, including Barcelona and Paris St-Germain, but Real now expect to sign the youngster in January.

Although no club-to-club talks have taken place, sources have told BBC Sport that Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives.

Gabriel, who scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut, has secured a European Union passport, which is expected to make it easier for him to sign for a club outside England.

United would be due compensation if Gabriel leaves, though the figure would be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League.

He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season campaign.A United source described Gabriel as

"The best 15-year-old in Europe" this year, while former interim manager Darren Fletcher said, "The world is his oyster."

Speaking after the EFL Cup defeat by Brighton, United head coach Michael Carrick said: "We've got to be really careful of the whole situation.

"He's a young boy...from a club point of view, looking after our younger players - their welfare, their well-being, their exposure - we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation."

Ghana News.title: Agalga defends Ablakwa over interdiction of passport scandal suspect
Ghana News.content:
Majority Leader in Parliament, James Agalga, has defended Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa over allegations of irregularities in the issuance of Ghanaian service passports, saying the minister acted appropriately by interdicting an officer implicated in the matter to allow investigations to proceed.

He said the minister could not be held culpable merely because the alleged misconduct occurred within an institution under his supervision, particularly when he had taken steps to address the matter.

Mr Agalga maintained that the appropriate course of action was to investigate the officer concerned, establish the facts and impose sanctions if wrongdoing was proven.

Speaking on Joy News' PM Express on Wednesday, November 3, he said the allegations he had been briefed on concerned service passports and should not be confused with claims about the sale of diplomatic passports.

"Those allegations, to the best of my knowledge, have nothing to do with diplomatic passports. I am told a certain individual who was even recruited into office in 2004 is complicit in some activities associated with service passports," he said.

He explained that Mr Ablakwa had ordered the interdiction of the officer as soon as the matter came to his attention, thereby creating room for investigations without the officer remaining in active service.

Mr Agalga said such a response was consistent with the responsibility of a minister supervising an institution where alleged misconduct had been reported.

"The Foreign Affairs Minister, when the matter came to his attention, immediately caused the interdiction of the officer involved to pave the way for some investigations to be carried out. That is a business," he said.

Prosecution possible if wrongdoing is established

The Majority Leader said the minister's responsibility did not end with the interdiction but extended to ensuring that the allegations were properly investigated and that anyone found culpable faced the appropriate disciplinary or legal consequences.

He said the outcome of the investigations should determine the next course of action, including possible dismissal or prosecution.

"Ultimate responsibility requires that you deal with situations such as ensuring that proper investigations are conducted. And if the outcome of the investigation implicates the officers involved, then you exact punishment in accordance with the conditions of service, the code of conduct of that particular officer," he stated.

He added that the sanctions could include dismissal and prosecution, depending on the findings.

Mr Agalga argued that the minister could be accused of wrongdoing if he failed to act after becoming aware of alleged misconduct within the ministry or an agency under his supervision.

However, he questioned why responsibility for the alleged actions of an officer should automatically be placed at the minister's doorstep when steps had been taken to facilitate investigations.

"Beyond that, the only time you can accuse the minister of wrongdoing is if the minister fails to act," he said.

Calls for parliamentary investigation

On whether Parliament should independently investigate the passport allegations, Mr Agalga pointed to the oversight responsibilities of the Foreign Affairs Committee.

He said the committee had the authority to summon the minister, the Director of Passports and other officials of the ministry to answer questions and provide information on matters arising within their jurisdiction.

According to him, the committee could initiate its own inquiry whenever members considered an investigation necessary.

"They have all the power at their disposal to summon the minister, including agency heads," he said.

He added that the committee could invite officials to appear before it to explain the circumstances surrounding the allegations and respond to questions from members.

Mr Agalga, however, challenged the Minority's approach to the matter, asking whether its representatives on the committee had formally activated the committee's investigative powers.

He specifically questioned whether the Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, had initiated proceedings through the committee before raising the allegations on the floor of Parliament.

"The fundamental question I want to ask is, did Honourable Abu Jinapor, who is Ranking Member and the Minority on the Foreign Affairs Committee, trigger the investigative role of the committee they belong to?" he asked.

His comments come amid growing political controversy over the issuance of Ghanaian diplomatic and service passports.

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has raised concerns about six individuals whose service passport applications it claims were approved using official designations that were inaccurate or did not correspond with their actual positions at the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) and the Fisheries Commission.

In a petition dated October 30, 2026, the party asked the United States Embassy in Ghana to review the treatment of the affected passport holders and tighten checks on the documents. The claims remain allegations and have not been established by an investigation or court.

The controversy has also spilled into Parliament, where Mr Abu Jinapor raised separate allegations that diplomatic passports were being sold for between US$10,000 and US$50,000. His claims against Mr Ablakwa triggered a dispute with the Majority Leader and subsequently led to the Speaker ordering his removal from the chamber after he failed to substantiate the allegations.

Mr Agalga's position is that allegations of misconduct within the Foreign Affairs Ministry must be investigated and that appropriate sanctions should follow where wrongdoing is established.

Ghana News.title: Strong winds uproot historic tree Okomfo Anokye planted many years ago at Agona
Ghana News.content:
Strong winds have uprooted the historic tree planted by the legendary priest Okomfo Anokye at Agona in the Ashanti Region.

The historic tree, said to have been planted many years ago, with some historians quoting around 330 years, went down Tuesday, during strong winds that passed through Agona.

From videos shared on social media from Agona, the tree came down upside down, with roots pointing skyward and branches facing the ground.

The Onton tree is said to have been planted by Okomfo Anokye himself around 1690 as a powerful spiritual symbol for the Asante Kingdom.

In Agona, Graphic Online understands many are saying the way the tree came down upside down, with roots pointing skyward and branches facing the ground, was a "spiritual sign".

Ghana News.title: 2027 Budget won’t get rubber-stamp treatment by supermajority – Agalga
Ghana News.content:
Majority Leader in Parliament, James Agalga, has dismissed suggestions that the governing National Democratic Congress' (NDC) numerical strength in the House could undermine parliamentary scrutiny of the 2027 Budget, insisting that the legislature will not abandon its oversight responsibilities.

He said although the NDC enjoyed a super majority, that advantage would not prevent Parliament from critically examining proposals brought before it by the Executive.

Mr Agalga gave the assurance in an interview on Joy News' PM Express on Wednesday, November 3, ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget.

His comments come amid concerns that the governing party's overwhelming numbers in Parliament could make it easier for the government to secure approval for its fiscal proposals without sufficient scrutiny.

But the Majority Leader said the size of the Majority caucus should not be mistaken for a willingness to rubber-stamp government policies and expenditure plans.

"We have a super majority. But that is not to say we relent in our efforts to ensure that Parliament's mandate to scrutinise whatever the Executive arm of government brings up before the legislature is done effectively," he said.

He maintained that Parliament would continue to discharge its constitutional responsibilities, regardless of the numerical advantage enjoyed by the governing side.

"So, never mind we have a super majority, but we will do what is expected of us as the legislative arm of government," he added.

The 2027 Budget is expected to outline the government's revenue and expenditure priorities, economic targets and policy measures for the coming fiscal year.

Parliament's consideration of the estimates and accompanying policy proposals will provide an opportunity for members to examine the government's spending plans, question allocations and assess the implications of its proposed fiscal measures.

Mr Agalga's assurance signals that the Majority leadership intends to maintain Parliament's scrutiny of the Executive's proposals despite the governing party's commanding position in the House.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
