World.title: IEC puts backup power measures in place ahead of vote counting
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has assured that contingency measures are in place to ensure that voting and the subsequent counting process are not disrupted by electricity outages.

Briefing the media on Wednesday, just a few hours before voting stations close at 9pm, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said generators and alternative lighting facilities have been made available to voting stations in areas that have experienced power outages.

READ | Elections 2026 | Voices from the ground

Mamabolo has praised the turnout of voters for the 2026 local government elections, with its preliminary estimates recording approximately 12 million voters who have cast their votes across the country as of 5pm today.

But even so, with voting scheduled to close at 9pm, Mamabolo has urged eligible voters who have not yet cast their ballots to make their way to their registered voting stations.

World.title: eThekwini wards to watch as MK Party challenges established political loyalties
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With only a few hours left before the 2026 local government elections close, eNCA Elections Analyst Wayne Sussman turned his attention to three key wards in eThekwini

According to Sussman, the results in Ward 26 near Durban city centre, Ward 86 in the Umlazi area and Ward 99 in the Umkomaas, Magabeni area could offer a picture of how political support has shifted since the 2021 local government elections.

He says the three wards are particularly interesting given the emergence of the uMkhonto weSizwe Party during the 2024 general elections.

First, he looked at Ward 26, which he describes as a closely contested inner-city ward.

Sussman notes that in 2021, just a few votes separated the ANC and DA in this ward.

READ | Ekurhuleni power battle: Can the MK Party weaken ANC support?

However, since the emergence of the MK Party, support has shifted significantly, with the Jacob Zuma-led MK Party leading.

He says the result makes him wonder whether the MK Party will pick up this ward.

“Can the ANC recover support and retain the ward, or will the Democratic Alliance come in here and win? This is going to be a fascinating contest to watch in the heart of Durban tonight,” he questions.

Turning to Ward 86, long an ANC stronghold, Sussman notes that in 2021 the ANC led and was tailed by EFF and IFP

But by 2024, the MK Party rattled the ground once again.

World.title: Presidency condemns political murders
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Director-General in the Presidency, Phindile Baleni, has condemned political killings.

She warned that police will deal with those responsible for these violent crimes.

“It is quite sad that certain people believe that their best way to express their political opinions is by killing others. “The democracy in the country enables us to choose our leaders at different points, and there are ways to allow for democratic principal transition between the different administrations or when people step down from positions,” she said.

Baleni's remarks come amid growing concerns about political killings. Natjoints Co-Chairperson Tebello Mosikili said they recorded 20 murders involving political representatives, party members and supporters, with seven arrests having been effected.

Mosikili indicated that SAPS has prioritised these investigations.

Baleni called on South Africans to be responsible, and if one wants to express an opinion, this must be done through established mechanisms and public participation.

World.title: In Trump's shoes: How cost of living fuels fury among relentless voters
World.content:
US President Donald Trump and President William Ruto attend the signing ceremony of a peace deal between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo at the United States Institute of Peace in Washington, DC, on December 4, 2025. [AFP]

The honeymoon for President Donald Trump, the second US president to serve two non-consecutive terms, ended in great disarray as the Democratic Party took control of both chambers of Congress in the mid-terms in stunning version on Wednesday, with the last two years of Trump’s presidency likely to be a horrible nightmare for him and for Republicans.

Gaining 7 seats in the Senate for a total of 54, well above the 50 needed to acquire a majority, and securing an extra 25 for a total of 228, comfortably above the 218-seat mark that sets a majority in the 435-member chamber, the Democrats will have the capacity to frustrate Trump’s policies which have often gone unchallenged, in what many feel is a breath of fresh air in US politic.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

World.title: Why did America swing back to the Democrats? It was the economy all along
World.content:
At face value, it’s not all that complicated.

President Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress were elected in November 2024 to fix the economy. Now it’s November 2026, and Americans feel even worse about it than they did two years ago.

So, it’s the economy, stupid.

But with respect to James Carville, it’s not quite that simple.

America’s economy is in surprisingly good shape. Unemployment is low – low enough for economists to consider the US economy to be at “full employment.” Overall consumer spending, the bedrock of America’s economy, has remained mostly resilient. And the AI revolution has revved an economic engine so powerful it’s projected to become the largest spending boom in modern US history.

If the economy is so strong, what got Americans fed up with Republicans just two years after they voted them into power?

Inflation is back, and voters drew a straight line connecting Trump’s signature policies to their financial anxieties. Tariffs. Lax AI regulation. Strict immigration restrictions. And especially the Iran war.

“If it weren’t for the war in Iran, this would be a very different midterm election,” said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union.

The cost of living

Americans still haven’t adjusted to the significant jump in the price of … well, pretty much everything … since 2021.

Inflation had come back down to earth in the last year of Joe Biden’s presidency, but that wasn’t enough to convince voters to give Democrats another chance in 2024. And that anger about the high cost of living has festered throughout Trump’s return to office.

Still, Trump and Republicans had a fairly compelling economic story to tell in the early part of this year.

The US economy in January posted its best month of job gains since 2024.

Manufacturing jobs had turned positive for the first time in 14 months.

Big tax refunds from the Republican-passed One Big Beautiful Bill Act were starting to show up in bank accounts.

Mortgage rates had fallen below 6% for the first time in three years.

The stock market kept hitting record highs, buoyed by AI stocks.

Consumer inflation, which had hit a four-year nadir in April 2025, returned close to that low point in January and February 2026.

Then America went to war with Iran, and everything changed.

Customers buy gasoline at a 76 gas station on Ventura Boulevard in Sherman Oaks as prices rise to nearly $7 a gallon on October 14, 2026. Christina House/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images

Oil prices surged to four-year highs. Diesel prices hit a record. And gas prices had never been this expensive on an Election Day.

Americans may hate inflation, but they get particularly irate about high fuel prices. Gas prices are plastered on giant billboards all over town, and filling a tank serves as a weekly reminder about how much more they’re shelling out: High gas and diesel prices alone have added $1,150 in costs for the average US household since the start of the war, according to Brown University researchers.

As fuel prices rose, bond yields surged, and so too did mortgage rates – recently rising at their fastest pace in three years.

After three straight years of paycheck gains outpacing price hikes, that trend kicked into reverse in March. Rebounding inflation has been eating into workers’ take-home pay ever since – and the average American’s real pay has shrunk since Trump has been back in office.

Americans blame Trump

It’s not a surprise that Americans had fond memories of the economy under Trump’s first term. At every point during Trump 1.0, Americans’ hard-earned dollars stretched further than prices – their pay gains nearly doubled the pace of inflation throughout his first four years in office.

That’s why Americans polled by CNN in October 2024 favored Trump over Vice President Kamala Harris as a better custodian of the economy by 15 percentage points. No shock there: Biden’s net approval on the economy was -31 points in the final CNN poll taken before he dropped out of the race.

Trump’s marks are now worse than Biden’s. By a wide margin: His net approval on the economy is -46 points, according to an October CNN poll.

Trump 2.0 has been a completely different story than Trump 1.0. For many Americans, it seems like costs are spiraling out of control and the American Dream is unattainable.

The Trump administration and congressional Republicans have laid blame at Democrats’ feet for the poor state of financial affairs they inherited. But some of Trump’s policies – especially his unpopular war – clearly made Americans’ cost of living worse.

It’s not just gas prices, which have added about $75 a month to people’s expenses. It’s other costs that voters associate with Trump and the Republicans – some of which are adding hundreds of dollars a month to their bills.

For example:

Republicans’ failure to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies in 2025 sent monthly Obamacare premiums up 58%, on average, for this year.

Electricity costs jumped 8.7% during Trump’s second term. Trump has been among the biggest champions of unfettered growth for AI.

Trump’s immigration policies and tariffs have raised the cost of auto repairs , which surged 12.3% since Trump took office.

They also sent homebuilders’ costs up by 13.3%.

Trump’s tariffs added $820 in taxes for the average American household this year, according to the Tax Foundation.

“Let’s say, for the sake of argument Biden totally screwed up: That in no way exonerates Trump,” said Steven Durlauf, an economist at the University of Chicago who researches wealth inequality and mobility. “Inflation has been badly managed by Trump. Voters have to place responsibility with the administration’s policies.”

All the evidence points to the voters doing just that. That’s a big reason why Trump’s Republican party took a beating in Tuesday’s midterm election.

Out of options

Inflation is only part of the story. Many Americans feel like the economy has left them behind.

The K-shaped economy accounts for some of that: Wealthier Americans with money in the stock market and who own a home are significantly more immune to rising costs than less-affluent Americans who are increasingly living paycheck to paycheck.

A big part of the problem is the lack of available options to achieve the American Dream: A massive undersupply of childcare options and housing have priced out many folks and have denied access for some who can.

“The middle-class ideal is becoming increasingly unobtainable,” said Durlauf.

The same is becoming true of the job market. Although still relatively strong, jobs are by no means booming like they had been in the immediate post-pandemic years. Mass layoffs haven’t become the norm, but for folks without a job, applications feel like they’re going into the ether.

“Another way to say low-hire, low-fire job market is lack-of-opportunity job market,” Long said.

In this economy, many Americans just feel stuck.

World.title: Google will let schools turn off AI, but they may also lose Search
World.content:
New York — Google is rolling out new controls for schools to limit students’ access to the company’s AI tools. But if schools opt out of AI altogether, they’ll also lose access to Google Search.

The policy change could mark a major shift in how students and educators interact with one of the biggest providers of education technology in the world. Google’s Chromebook laptops are used by tens of millions of students, sometimes starting in kindergarten.

The move comes as many communities have pushed for stricter limits on screen time and AI use in schools, amid growing fears that the technology could stunt students’ learning and development or pose safety risks. A number of school districts, including New York City and Los Angeles public schools, banned generative AI tools for many or all students this school year.

Google on Tuesday said its products that use AI, like its Gemini assistant and Google Search, will be off by default for K-12 student accounts, until school administrators “explicitly turn them on.” The change reverses an earlier move by Google in August to turn on Gemini by default in its Google Classrooms app.

But now, if schools want to turn off AI entirely, they’ll also lose access to Google Search.

The company said the changes are in response to calls from educators and policymakers for more control over AI tools.

Chris Phillips, vice president of education at Google, told the New York Times that “search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” and that schools that ban AI “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

Google has made AI central to Search in recent years — adding “AI overviews” summarizing answers at the top of many results pages and expanding the size of the search bar to accommodate longer queries.

Google’s Tuesday blog post does not offer specifics on how these controls will work, or what students might see if they tried to access Google Search from a school that has banned AI. Phillips wrote in the post that the company will “share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition.”

In response to questions from CNN about how the new controls would work, Google pointed to a Tuesday afternoon post on X in which the company said the policy change would give schools “more choice, not less.” It added that schools would be able to toggle on Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search individually.

But the post still implies that schools will not be able to use Search without AI features, saying: “AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.”

The policy change came as part of a larger announcement by Google about a slate of updates to its AI tools for learning, based on the idea that the technology should help students work through problems rather than simply giving them answers. Under this new “guided learning” principle, Google says that when its systems detect, for example, that a student is using Search for homework help, they’ll be prompted to walk through the problem or topic step-by-step rather than receiving a single answer.

It’s an approach also being taken by other AI companies, as they seek to convince educators and parents that their products are valuable learning tools, and that experience with AI in school is essential to success in the workforce later.

OpenAI in August announced “ChatGPT for Teens” which, in addition to safety controls, focuses heavily on learning, allowing parents and teens to turn on “Study Mode” to work through questions. Many tech companies have also provided funding to train teachers in AI.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who announced the New York Public Schools AI ban this year, responded to Google’s policy change by accusing the company of trying to “force” AI into schools.

“No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he said in an X post Tuesday.

World.title: Iran supreme leader says midterms results will not reverse US’ “hostility” towards Tehran
World.content:
Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that anyone who believes the midterm results will shift Washington’s stance on Tehran is “deeply mistaken.”

“Anyone who still clings to even a slim hope that the system of domination might change its behavior or undergo party and factional shifts, or who believes that concessions to US could turn it away from its hostility toward the Iranian nation, is deeply mistaken,” Khamenei was quoted as saying by the Iranian state-backed outlet, IRNA.

The Supreme Leader has not been seen in public since he was appointed in late February, after US-Israeli strikes killed his father and predecessor earlier this year.

The US-Israeli joint war in Iran became a focal point of campaigns in the run up to the midterms – after regional violence this year spiked gas and diesel prices for millions of families across the world, including in the US.

World.title: How Nigeria’s Funke Akindele is helping take Nollywood global
World.content:
Africa’s highest grossing filmmaker is about to release another potential blockbuster. On December 11, media mogul Funke Akindele will release “The Four: No One Fights Alone.” The movie, which is her eighth major theatrical feature film, tells the story of four strong women who fiercely fight for the future of a young man they love.

Its cultural themes are consistent with her approach to storytelling.

“I tell the Nigerian or the African stories that people can sit back, relate to, but I make sure it’s a global standard, so that when it cuts across, they can understand it and we get more audience,” she told CNN’s Larry Madowo in Lagos earlier this year.

Box-office success

Akindele, who wears several hats in her career as an actress, producer, writer and director, earned the distinction of being Africa’s most commercially successful filmmaker after the 2025 release of “Behind the Scenes” made more than 2 billion naira, roughly $1.6 million. The movie, about a real estate mogul facing a crisis who reexamines her generosity, was the first Nollywood film to cross that financial threshold. It was streamed on Netflix, which helped it gain a global audience.

“I’m so happy, it’s a big pat at the back,” she told Madowo about the success of the movie.

Nigeria’s movie industry is the world’s second largest by volume, according to UNESCO, behind India’s. It produces more than 2,500 films a year, surpassing Hollywood’s output. Film production is the country’s second-largest source of jobs, employing more than 1 million people.

A shot from the 2025 film “Behind the Scenes,” starring Funke Akindele FAAN

Akindele is the first African filmmaker whose films topped the Nigerian box office for three consecutive years.

Her 2023 film “A Tribe Called Judah” was the first Nollywood movie to make 1 billion naira at the box office — more than $745,000. The comedy-drama tells the story of five brothers with different fathers who rob a store to save their sick mother, played by Akindele. She says she wrote the screenplay because she wanted to “tell it as it is, no sugarcoating,” adding that she was inspired by real life. She recounts a story of a woman she knew who had seven children by seven men and how society judged her and labeled her a “prostitute.” That experience echoes in Akindele’s character in the movie.

“My own style of writing is being authentic because anything you have to do in life, you have to make sure that you are intentional about it … Ambition is good, but it’s not what will sell the film. It’s the fact that you’re doing something [with] quality, something real, authentic,” she said.

The first big hit

Before the success of “Behind the Scenes” and “A Tribe Called Judah” there was “Jenifa,” her first big financially successful film. The 2008 release tells the story of a village girl who moves to the city to attend university and desperately tries to fit in. The movie launched Akindele to stardom.

“I just wanted to speak to young people out there,” she said, explaining why she wrote the script. “I see storytelling as a tool to show people what is happening in society, correct ills, reach out to young people out there, help them believe in themselves, because I’m very, very passionate about the young people.”

The sequel, “The Return of Jenifa,” in 2011 was Akindele’s first movie to play in Nigerian theaters. And in 2024, Akindele made a second sequel, “Everybody Loves Jenifa,” which she said was her most expensive film to date.

“We filmed in Ghana, and we flew down to Ghana with all the cast and crew members. We filmed in Safari Valley Resorts. That’s a very expensive place to film. And we came back to Nigeria again, and I build all my sets. I don’t go to people’s houses to film. I create the set myself. I could go rent out a place, buy a place, and start constructing sets there. So, ‘Everybody Loves Jennifer’ was very expensive,” she said.

But she said she made her money back, adding that the film “was successful in cinemas and on streaming platforms.”

Funke Akindele talking about her “Jenifa” character with CNN’s Larry Madowo CNN

The hurdles

Despite the success of her films, Akindele ­— who landed her first role in 1998 as Bisi in the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)-sponsored sitcom “I Need to Know” and has acted in more than 100 films — said filmmakers in Africa still face hurdles.

“Our major barrier is distribution,” she said. “The more we partner, the more we collaborate globally, we will break that barrier because when you collaborate with the filmmakers across the world, you get to share experience, you get to share ideas, perspectives, and you get to learn production standards over there, technology, distribution. So I feel collaboration, partnership is really going to help us a lot.”

She encourages filmmakers to partner with other creatives and tell stories that resonate globally.

“If you’re a filmmaker, a story writer, write stories that are authentic, but that can cross the borders. Make sure that the emotion’s there. Everybody can relate to it … you have to be patient, because Rome wasn’t built in a day.”

Nigerian filmmaker Funke Akindele Sabigal

When it comes to a legacy, Akindele hopes that her work leaves a lasting impact on people’s lives.

“I want to be remembered for that woman that gives access to other women, all the people out there, that broke the barrier for them. I want to keep … creating platforms for their voices to be heard, to help them develop their crafts, their skills. That is why I’m here,” she said.

World.title: Is there a ‘mysterious virus’ in Esna? Health Ministry reveals the truth
World.content:
The Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population has settled the ongoing debate regarding the spread of a virus in Esna, explaining that reported cases are merely seasonal viral infections – not a “mysterious virus” – and that most cases are mild with patients recovering at home.

Field Follow-up

Luxor Health Directorate, in coordination with Health Ministry, explained that the affected individuals are experiencing symptoms such as high fever and body aches.

Upon diagnosis, it was determined that these are seasonal viral infections that typically occur at this time of year. The Ministry confirmed that none of the cases require hospitalization.

No Epidemic Virus

The official spokesperson for the Health Ministry, Hossam Abdel-Ghaffar, denied the presence of an epidemic virus in Esna, located in the southern part of Luxor Governorate.

He assured the reports in Esna are of a seasonal viral infection, which is common at this time every year

Official Sources

An official source from the Environment Ministry confirmed that the illness is not transmitted through drinking water, food, or personal contact.

The vast majority of cases are mild, with patients recovering at home through rest and fluid intake; those who required hospitalization have since recovered, he noted.

Eyewitnesses

According to local eyewitnesses, citing physicians specializing in infectious diseases who have been monitoring several cases, this is a known seasonal viral infection that recurs at this time of year.

It manifests as a cluster of cases among residents in the villages of Esna city, characterized by high fever and body aches.

Eyewitnesses added that the vast majority of recorded cases are mild, and patients can recover at home with rest.

The Luxor Health Directorate said that as soon as reports emerged of high fevers among groups of residents in Esna, the Directorate initiated immediate health monitoring, which revealed the nature of the infection.

Intensifying Disease Vector Control

The Directorate also confirmed the intensification of campaigns to control disease vectors—such as insects and rodents—in coordination with the Preventive Medicine department, aiming to ensure a stable health and epidemiological situation in the villages.

Furthermore, the Infection Control department organized a comprehensive training program for new staff members.

The program is designed to enhance their knowledge, develop their technical and practical skills, and standardize operational procedures in line with the latest infection control standards and policies.

Precautionary Measures

The training program also covered isolation precautions based on modes of transmission, whether airborne, contact, or droplet, as well as protective isolation.

Furthermore, it introduced concepts related to the surveillance of healthcare-associated infections, including methods for monitoring bloodstream infections, urinary tract infections, surgical site infections, pneumonia, and events associated with mechanical ventilators.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Israeli media comments on Trump’s statement on halting US Aid
World.content:
Hebrew-language media outlets, including The Times of Israel, commented on statements from US President Donald Trump regarding the US terminating aid to Israel by the end of the year.

In an interview with Fox News on Tuesday, Trump said that his administration would not allow its achievements to be undermined by what he described as “the exploitation of aid to Israel by political candidates”—citing, for example, Abdul El-Sayed, a candidate in the state of Michigan.

The US President explained that El-Sayed has repeatedly questioned why the US provides four billion dollars annually to Israel, suggesting that halting this aid would put an end to the matter.

Trump further noted that he had reached an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cease American aid to Israel by the end of the year, asserting that “Israel no longer needs it.”

He continued: “They are fine with it because they have become a very successful country; they don’t need it. And we will no longer be paying Israel.”

However, The Times of Israel described Trump’s statement as “false,” pointing to a 10-year memorandum of understanding on US military aid to Israel, which provides Tel Aviv with $3.8 billion annually, that does not expire until September 2028.

The Israeli newspaper noted that Trump’s move highlights the declining popularity of aid to Israel across both major US political parties.

The Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation cited security officials as saying: “We were taken by surprise by Trump’s announcement to halt military support.”

According to Fox News, the current security assistance agreement between the US and Israel provides for approximately $3.8 billion annually through 2028.

Netanyahu has previously said that he wishes to gradually phase out Israel’s reliance on US military aid, although the timing and terms of any such change to the agreement have not been specified in detail.

World.title: Bomb threats on board 7 flights across Europe cause disruptions
World.content:
At least seven flights in Europe received bomb threats on Tuesday, causing disruptions at airports – though no explosive devices were found.

The threats targeted at least two flights bound for Warsaw, two for Sofia, two for Rome, and one for Murcia Airport in Spain.

Another flight headed to Sofia had received a similar threat the previous day, and one of the airports in Warsaw was briefly closed.

According to Reuters, the Italian Air Force escorted one of the flights bound for Rome.

Authorities diverted a LOT Polish Airlines flight, arriving from London and scheduled to land at Warsaw’s Chopin Airport, to the nearby Modlin Airport, which was temporarily closed, then reopened following an inspection of the aircraft, during which no suspicious devices were discovered.

Hungarian Defense Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi wrote on Facebook that a Wizz Air flight traveling from London to Sofia was diverted to Budapest Airport following a bomb threat.

Hoaxes reported

In the city of Murcia in southeastern Spain, authorities cordoned off parts of the airport on Tuesday after receiving a report of a bomb on board a Ryanair flight arriving from Manchester.

Officials later confirmed that the report was a hoax.

The airport resumed normal operations after it was determined that there were no explosives on the aircraft.

Ryanair declined to provide an immediate comment on the incident.

Two other Ryanair flights, arriving from Lisbon and Dublin, were also subjected to inspections at Fiumicino Airport in Rome, following bomb threats, according to a source from ADR, the airport’s operator.

The flight arriving from Dublin was escorted by Italian Air Force jets until it landed. The source noted that the alert level was raised, though the airport continued to operate as usual, with no impact on other flights.

No group has claimed responsibility for the incident, and officials have not pointed the finger at any specific party.

World.title: PM reviews progress on remaining phases of Knowledge City in New Capital
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed, during a meeting held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, evening, progress in completing the remaining phases of Knowledge City in the New Capital, as well as efforts to maximize its potential in developing the communications and information technology industry, building digital talent and creating high-value job opportunities.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Communications and Information Technology Raafat Hindi and Chairman and Managing Director of the Administrative Capital for Urban Development (ACUD) Khaled Abbas.

During the meeting, Hindi said Knowledge City was one of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology’s flagship projects. It represents an integrated information community equipped with advanced information infrastructure and laboratories, bringing together specialized technology training, academic education, research and development in advanced technologies, innovation and entrepreneurship. It also hosts local and international companies operating in the communications and information technology sector, providing an environment that promotes integration between academic and research institutions and businesses, attracts investment and supports the growth of the IT industry.

The minister said the ministry was keen to make the most of Knowledge City’s assets in the New Capital by strengthening cooperation among the institutions based there and expanding partnerships with technology companies. These efforts aim to develop digital skills, prepare specialists in various communications and IT fields, equip young people for future jobs, and support research, development and innovation in advanced technologies.

The first phase of Knowledge City includes the Imhotep Centre for Creativity and Development, which hosts a number of local and international companies specializing in electronic circuit design and automotive embedded systems. The centre also houses specialized laboratories for the Internet of Things, Industry 4.0, and the design and manufacture of integrated electronic circuits, helping build national capabilities in these industries.

The first phase also includes branches of the Information Technology Institute and the National Telecommunications Institute, which offer specialized training programs in various communications and IT fields through advanced technology laboratories equipped with the latest technologies and in cooperation with leading international companies. This helps prepare digital professionals and strengthen their competitiveness in regional and international labour markets.

It also encompasses the National Academy of Information Technology for Persons with Disabilities, which serves as a centre for innovation, research and entrepreneurship in assistive technologies. The academy seeks to empower persons with disabilities to contribute effectively to social and economic development through tailored capacity-building programs that enhance their independence and employment opportunities. It also supports innovators and developers in creating solutions in information and communications technology.

Knowledge City is also home to Egypt University of Informatics, established by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology in cooperation with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research to prepare digital talent. The university offers students opportunities to earn dual degrees through partnerships with a number of prestigious international universities.

The university recently graduated its second cohort from the faculties of Computing and Information Sciences, Business Technology, and Digital Arts and Design, as well as its first cohort from the Faculty of Engineering.

World.title: Liberia: National Port Authority Admits Freeport Lagging Behind Shipping Demand; Harbor Master Says Dredging Contract Due This Week
World.content:
MONROVIA – The National Port Authority (NPA) has acknowledged that the Freeport of Monrovia, Liberia’s principal seaport, is struggling to keep pace with the size and number of ships now calling on it. Cargo vessels are queuing offshore, and importers are counting the cost.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

In an exclusive interview with FrontPage Africa, Captain Samuel M. Lynch, the NPA’s Harbor Master and head of its Marine Department, said a contract for comprehensive dredging of the entire port basin and navigation channel is expected to be signed this week. Expansion of container yards and berths would follow within three to eight months, he said.



“The discussion now is that the time is now. The need for it is now that it can’t be pushed further down the line,” Lynch said.

Video footage obtained by FrontPage Africa shows at least five cargo vessels anchored off Monrovia’s coastline, waiting to enter the port. The Freeport handles most of the country’s imported food, fuel, construction materials and other essential goods.

Background: A Senator Sounds the Alarm

The congestion reached the National Legislature last month. In an October 25 letter to Senate President Pro-Tempore Nyonblee Karnga-Lawrence, Gbarpolu County Senator Amara M. Konneh said importers and shipping agents report that Liberia-bound containers spend an average of more than 30 days at sea before berthing in Monrovia. Some vessels, he said, are being routed to or held at ports in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana.

Konneh, a former Minister of Finance and Development Planning, blamed insufficient container yard space and prolonged delays in dredging the port basin and channel, which he said prevent larger vessels from berthing. He also cited “a multiplicity of opaque transaction costs and fees” charged by APM Terminals, MEDTECH Scientific Limited, Global Tracking and Maritime Solutions (GTMS) and others in the supply chain.

The Senator argued that port inefficiencies may explain why consumer prices remain high even though headline inflation has fallen to 4.6 percent and the Liberian dollar has strengthened against the US dollar. He asked the Senate to summon the NPA, APM Terminals, MEDTECH, GTMS, the Liberia Revenue Authority’s Customs Department, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and customs brokers to testify before the full Senate.

Asked about the congestion last week, NPA Managing Director Sekou Dukuly offered a one-line response: “We are working on dredging and expansion.” Lynch’s interview is the most detailed account yet of what that work involves.

The NPA says the problem is more complex than any single cause. It points to a combination of inadequate infrastructure, bigger vessels, limited berths, weather and operational constraints.

Dredging: ‘A Continuous Requirement’

Responding to criticism that successive governments have announced dredging projects without solving the problem, Lynch said dredging at the Freeport is a continuous requirement because of the port’s location and design.

Unlike naturally deep-water ports, the Freeport suffers from sedimentation. Ocean currents carry sand from the river and nearby coastal areas into the port basin, steadily reducing the depth of water available to ships.

“Naturally, the currents bring the sand from the river and from up north, the coastal areas like West Point. All those areas bring it and deposit it inside the basin,” Lynch explained.

Without regular dredging, he said, the draft available to vessels keeps shrinking, limiting the size of ships that can safely enter. Ideally, the port should be dredged every two to three years, and at least every five years, depending on how fast sediment builds up.

The last dredging was carried out in January 2023 by APM Terminals, the port’s container terminal operator, Lynch said. The new campaign will differ because it covers the entire basin rather than selected sections.

“The scope is a bit different than it was in the previous dredge campaigns,” he said.

Bigger Ships, Same Port

Beyond dredging, Lynch named inadequate container yard space and limited berths as the port’s biggest constraints.

He said the APM Terminals concession provided for the development of about 11 hectares, but discussions are under way to use the entire area to handle growing cargo volumes.

The port’s needs, he said, have changed significantly since the concession arrangement was introduced in 2013. Liberia’s population and economy have grown, imports have risen, and global shipping has moved to much larger vessels.

Ships calling on Monrovia between 2011 and 2013 were generally about 295 meters long. Some of the largest vessels in global shipping now reach about 400 meters. Bigger ships bring more containers: a vessel that once required 600 to 800 container-handling moves can now need as many as 1,600. The container yard, Lynch argued, must expand to match.

He said APM Terminals’ concession obligations include developing the terminal to reflect changing shipping requirements and the port’s growing needs.

Lynch disputed Senator

Konneh’s figure of more than 30 days at sea. He said the average waiting time for container ships across the region is about 26 days, while Liberia’s is now about 12 days, up from a low of about six days at one point.

“In all fairness, let’s be realistic. In the whole region here, the average rate, we’re talking about liners now, container ships. The average wait time is 26 days. Ours is not 26. At some point, we were doing six days. We’re now at somewhere around 12,” Lynch said.

He acknowledged, however, that shallow water has contributed to delays. Because of shallow areas in the channel and basin, larger vessels sometimes have to enter at high tide. The NPA has also banned some vessels from moving at night for safety reasons, so ships that finish working late at night must wait until daylight to leave.

Lynch said no single factor explains the delays. He pointed to operational logistics, how quickly containers are cleared from the yard, and the availability of berths.

Rain Slows Bulk Cargo

The Harbor Master drew a distinction between container ships and bulk carriers bringing in rice, wheat, flour and clinker, the main raw material for cement.

These cargoes must be kept dry, so Liberia’s long rainy season frequently halts discharge. Shipping companies, vessel captains and insurers must weigh the risk of cargo damage before allowing work to continue in bad weather.

A bulk carrier with 50,000 to 55,000 metric tons can normally discharge in about 21 days in good weather, Lynch said. In the rains, the same vessel may stay at berth far longer.

“Sometimes they’re taking six weeks. Sometimes they’re taking six to eight weeks,” he said.

Lynch said such delays are caused by the weather, not by port congestion. The NPA is considering additional dedicated berths for bulk carriers so that ships carrying different commodities are not competing for the same limited space.

The Dredging Plan

Lynch said the project will be carried out in two phases. Phase One will deal with shallow areas in the navigation channel and port basin to improve access and restore safer operating conditions. The contract is expected to be signed this week, and dredging equipment could begin arriving within about 10 days, subject to regulatory and administrative arrangements.

Phase Two, expected to begin within three to eight months, will focus on expansion, including additional terminal space and dedicated berths. Lynch said Phase One would bring immediate improvements, while Phase Two would tackle the port’s longer-term limits.

The dredging will cover the area from the China Union and BMC Pier to the Liberia Maritime Corporation (LMC) Pier, the Western Cluster area, APM Terminals’ facility and the Liberia Petroleum Refining Company (LPRC) facility. The fairway from the open sea through the channel and into the breakwater is also included.

The entire basin is to be restored to a depth of 13.5 meters, compared with the 13 meters targeted in previous campaigns. The project will also remove an underwater rock, marked by an isolated danger buoy, that obstructs navigation. Past dredging campaigns avoided it because removing it requires specialized equipment. Lynch said it must now go to give larger vessels enough room to maneuver. The work will require two marine vessels, including one designed to break up underwater rock.

Nine shipwrecks have also been identified in the port basin, two of them in areas used for navigation. Lynch said the NPA intends to remove all nine now, rather than bring specialized equipment back for Phase Two.

He acknowledged that the wider scope will make this campaign more expensive than previous ones, which reportedly cost between US$5 million and US$6 million.

Toward 24-Hour Operations

If the dredging succeeds, Lynch said, the NPA could relax some of the restrictions now placed on ships. Vessels are currently limited to a maximum draft of about 11 meters. Depending on the final depth achieved, that could rise to between 12 and 12.5 meters, allowing larger and more heavily loaded ships to enter.

Deeper water could also allow night-time sailings to resume, so ships can enter and leave around the clock. Under the current rules, a vessel that finishes work at 11 p.m. may have to wait at berth until daylight, keeping the next ship waiting offshore.

But Lynch stressed that dredging alone will not solve the port’s problems without more berths and container-handling facilities.

Seven Berths Against Tema’s 29

Lynch compared the Freeport with its regional rivals. Ghana’s Port of Tema has about 29 berths, he said. The Freeport of Monrovia has seven under the NPA’s management.

APM Terminals’ quay, about 600 meters long, can take about three vessels in good conditions. But ships of different lengths, some about 200 meters and others over 225 meters, make it hard to use every meter of quay space. Some berths are also reserved for particular vessels, such as the LPRC berth for tankers. With so few berths, ships often must wait for others to finish before they can come alongside. Lynch said additional berths, including dedicated bulk berths, would significantly increase capacity and ease congestion.

Who Pays for the Wait

Ships waiting offshore are expensive. Lynch acknowledged that shipping companies keep paying charter fees, fuel, crew wages and food while their vessels sit idle.

He said, however, that the NPA does not set port tariffs on its own, as these are fixed under existing concession and tariff arrangements. The authority’s job, he said, is to use available berths efficiently and bring ships in as quickly as conditions allow.

“We are flexible in terms of using berths for different types of vessels. We move assets around … We try to accommodate as much as possible,” he said.

For importers, especially small businesses with little cash to spare, those costs remain a heavy burden. Senator Konneh argues they are passed directly to consumers.

Questions Over Long-Term Planning

The congestion raises questions about whether Liberia planned for the growth in shipping traffic and the rise of larger vessels.

Asked how the port’s problems reached this stage, Lynch said its requirements had changed considerably since the original studies and concession arrangements were drawn up. Infrastructure considered adequate in 2013, he acknowledged, may no longer meet today’s needs.

Port planning, he argued, should look beyond short-term projections and include regular reviews so that concessions and infrastructure keep up with economic and shipping realities. He said an independent third-party assessment informed the port’s current master plan, which identified the need for expansion, more berths and better operating capacity. The planned dredging, he said, is the first major step toward carrying out those recommendations.

The NPA now says container ships wait about 12 days, not 30. But Senator Konneh’s complaints and the ships visible from Monrovia’s beaches show the need for more openness about port performance, infrastructure limits and the timetable for fixing them.

The first test is whether dredging begins as promised. The second is whether expanded yards and new berths follow. Until then, the Freeport will keep trying to handle growing shipping demand with infrastructure that the NPA itself admits is no longer enough.

World.title: Liberia Pleads for Seafarers as Iran War Sinks, Burns Ships
World.content:
London, United Kingdom – Liberia has told the International Maritime Organization (IMO) that seafarers “must never become targets or casualties” of the wars now spreading along some of the world’s busiest shipping lanes.

Delivering Liberia’s General Statement on Tuesday, November 3, at the 138th session of the IMO Council (Agenda Item C138/11), Liberia’s Maritime Commissioner and CEO, Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe, Sr., expressed grave concern over persistent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, the Sea of Azov, the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Oman, the Red Sea, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Strait of Hormuz. Thousands of seafarers and their vessels remain trapped in these waters by military operations.

“Seafarers are innocent civilian professionals performing legitimate duties essential to international trade and the global economy. They must never become targets or casualties of armed conflicts and geopolitical hostilities,” the statement said.



Commissioner Lighe warned that the “unwarranted attacks” continue to endanger innocent crews, damage commercial vessels and disrupt international trade, and “tragically, claim human lives.” He extended Liberia’s deepest condolences to the families of seafarers killed in the attacks.

Why Liberia Has a Stake

The plea carries particular weight coming from Monrovia. Liberia overtook Panama in 2023 to become the world’s largest ship registry by gross tonnage. It has since become the first flag state to pass 300 million gross tons, about 17 percent of the global fleet. That means a large share of the ships sailing through today’s war zones fly the Liberian flag, and registry earnings are a significant source of revenue for the Liberian government.

Liberian Ships in the Line of Fire

The war around Iran began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran. Since then, ships under Liberia’s flag have been caught in the crossfire again and again.

March 11: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they struck the Liberian-flagged Express Rome in the Strait of Hormuz after it ignored orders to stop.

August 3: The Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Minoan Pioneer was hit by a projectile about 20 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. The strike knocked out the ship’s power and set its accommodation block on fire. Its third engineer was reported missing.

August 31: A laden Liberian-flagged oil tanker was hit by multiple explosive devices while sailing out of the strait. The Liberia Maritime Authority reported that all crew were safe. Two days later, the Authority ordered Liberian-flagged ships in the area to the highest security level, Level 3.

Late September: Three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles on the same day in the Strait of Hormuz, the Oman Observer reported on October 1.

October 5: The Liberian-flagged tanker Lipsi, managed by Greece’s Dynacom Tankers, was hit by a projectile that damaged its engine room and started a fire. The crew was reported safe.

The threat to the Liberian flag predates the Iran war. In July 2025, Yemen’s Houthi rebels sank two Liberian-flagged bulk carriers, the Magic Seas and the Eternity C, in the Red Sea. At least four of the Eternity C’s crew were killed.

A Deadly October

Lighe’s statement came at the end of the worst month for shipping since the war began. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) center counted more than 30 incidents in and around the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Gulf in October. That is more than double September’s total and brings the number of incidents since February 28 to 145. Industry figures cited by Reuters show that more than 30 supertankers have been damaged since the conflict began, 11 of them in October alone.

Among the incidents:

October 6: A projectile struck the Panama-flagged tanker On Peace off the Omani port of Limah and set it on fire. At least 12 of its 19 crew were injured, 11 of them Indian nationals, and Oman’s air force airlifted 10 to hospital.

October 13–14: Two Singapore-registered ships, the GFS Pride and the GFS Giselle, were hit by projectiles. The GFS Pride, a container ship, sank while under tow; all 21 crew were rescued. The GFS Giselle suffered hull damage, and its 22 crew were evacuated. U.S. officials blamed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards. Iran said the GFS Pride hit a mine.
